"Well my original world was basically that. Perhaps there were supernatural elements in the background, I'm not sure, but all in all, at least to me it was a normal world. I lived my life, I woke up, went to school, hung out with friends, it was a pretty alright life all things considered. I don't think it was what I craved deep inside, but it was fine." Felix said in reminiscence.

She raised a brow. "I did not think you would live such a life."

Felix shrugged his shoulders. "I was different back then, less confident, more normal, more… average."

"Fufufu, to hear you call yourself average is truly a wonder, I did not think your ego would allow such a thing. I will remember this memory fondly."

Felix rolled his eyes. "Oh shove it. Continuing on, I ended up dying at about 16 years old, as for how, that doesn't matter in this story. After dying I reincarnated as a Human in another world."

Her lips twitched as she took in what Felix had said. He died when he was… 16? She did not know how long Felix spent in the Daemon Realm, even he himself likely had no idea how long he spent there, so for all she knows he could be less than 20 years old.

He looked to be in his mid twenties going by human age, however appearance was not a good indicator of age, there was Gunther who looked like an old man while she herself looked to be in her mid twenties even though her and Gunther were of similar age. Guy himself was eons old and looked to be in his prime as well, safe to say appearance was not reliable when it came to figuring out someone's age.

Had she robbed the cradle as the mortals say?
Her eyes widened. "That was not when you reincarnated as a Daemon?"

Felix shook his head. "Nope, that was after I died a second time."

She didn't know Felix was incredibly unlucky, or lucky.

"In my second life it was much the same, I had a good mother, but she passed away." Felix sighed in sadness. Her hand slowly snaked over into his, he shot her a quick wing and a smile before continuing. She knew the pain of losing a parent, she would forever deny it, but losing the Twilight that truly cared for her to the being he had become had hurt. "This world however I later found out did have the supernatural."

"Oh? I am aware that some of Veldanava's other creations are similar to this world, with both having supernatural beings, but I have never heard about one myself." She said.

He nodded. "Yeah, it's definitely an interesting world, a world of Curses, and of Sorcerers."

Felix went on to explain the world that he called 'Jujutsu Kaisen'. She became more and more interested the more she learned.

In the midst of his story they were interrupted by the waiter, but once she shooed him away after taking their orders Felix had continued.

Jujutsu Sorcerers that had Innate Techniques, which reminded her of Skills if somewhat different in nature. There was cursed energy which was born from the negative emotions of the populace, Cursed Spirits which seemed similar to Monsters that were born from the magicules of the strong. She learned that Felix had returned to this world of his at some point in the past, through his ability to go to other dimensions no doubt.

The world was truly an intriguing one, one with its own history and story to be told.

He told her a bit about the friend he had made in that world, the so-called 'Honored One'.

He told her about Sukuna, she had known about the butler that Felix had gotten, a Daemon of extreme levels of power, however she had not known of his origins until now.

She had thought him to be an aberration of a Daemon similar to Beretta, but it seems Sukuna was far more unique than she thought.

Then there was perhaps one of the most interesting things of all… Domain Expansions.

The pinnacle of Jujutsu Sorcery, and she could understand why it was called such. It was truly a marvel to hear about, and she couldn't help but consider how to go about recreating such an ability in this world.

It would require much experimenting and patience, but she was Luminous Valentine.

She listened as Felix described his death in his second life, and she couldn't help but laugh. "Fufufu, my Felix dying as a hero, who would have known."

Felix raised a brow. "Your Felix?" He said with an amused smile.

Her eyes widened in alarm as she realized what she had said. "Forget that!" She demanded.

"Hehe, whatever you say, I'll remember the cute blush on your face and that's more than enough for me." Felix laughed.

"Do what you will." She huffed, even as a small smile graced her face.

She took a sip of her wine as Felix continued.

"After dying to truck-kun." She raised a brow at how Felix referred to the cause of his death.

"Truck-kun? What does that mean?" She asked, assuming it was some obscure reference from his past life.

Felix chuckled at her confusion. "Ah, Truck-kun... You see, in my past life, there's this running joke. Whenever someone in a story gets hit by a truck and then wakes up in some crazy new world, we blame it on 'Truck-kun.' It's like this mysterious, all-powerful entity disguised as an ordinary truck, whose sole mission is to transport people to their next life, usually one filled with magic, swords, and over-the-top adventures."

He leaned in, grinning. "So when I say I died to Truck-kun, I'm not just saying I got hit by a truck. I'm saying that was my ticket out of my boring old life and into this one. I may have had good times, but in the end I wouldn't change a thing that happened, and truck-kun played a factor in my appearance in this world."

She raised a brow. Truly Felix's previous world had the oddest things. "I see, then if the opportunity presents itself I will have to thank this truck-kun."

"Hahaha, you and me both." Felix responded. "Anyways after that I ended up reincarnating as a Daemon in the Daemon Realm, I was a mere Lesser Daemon at first."

A Lesser Daemon? To progress from a meager Lesser Daemon to what Felix had become now was incredibly impressive, no matter what Felix thought of himself, he was by no means "average" as he had said he was.

"I was blessed with some incredible Skills to start out with, it turns out that I was from one of the big clans I talked about when telling you about the world of Jujutsu Kaisen, I was from the Gojo Clan, and the Limitless Innate Technique was laying dormant within me, the Voice of the World brought out my potential which allowed me to stand a chance in the Daemon Realm."

"Limitless hmm? The same technique as that Satoru man then." Limitless from what Felix described offered impressive levels of Spatial Manipulation. Nothing she hadn't heard of before, but it was still impressive. Felix had managed to grow the capabilities of Limitless into what he had now, making him in her eyes unmatched when it came to Spatial Manipulation.

"Yeah, Limitless was incredible, but that wasn't my only Skill, I also had a Skill that increased my comprehension at the beginning." Felix explained.

"I see."

Felix then went on to share about his experiences in the Daemon Realm, about how he had gotten cocky and been ambushed by multiple Lesser Daemons, as well as a single Lesser Daemon on the cusps of evolution.

He managed to pull off a lucky win and was taken care of by another Daemon that was once a Human as well which caused her to consider just how many Humans reincarnated into other races in this world.

Eventually he and his benefactor split off, until eventually Felix was summoned to the Cardinal World.

"That is quite the origin story as you put it."
Felix nodded. "It's not the most impressive, but it's mine."

She nodded. "Thank you for sharing it with me."

Felix nodded at her thanks, she turned towards the viewing panel, the main fights had not started yet so there was still time.

"What do you think Hinata is doing?" Felix asked.

"Knowing that girl I'm sure she is catching up on everything she has missed." Luminous guessed.

- Hinata Sakaguchi -

She folded her hands on the table in front of her as she waited for the last member of the newly renamed 'Nine Great Saints' to take their seats.

She sat at the head of the table, to her left sat Saare, and Grigori. Previously Glenda sat next to Grigori before Felix got his hands on her.

She knew very well how Felix ended up acquiring Glenda as a subordinate, Glenda wasn't as slick as she thought she was, Hinata had long known that she had other motives for joining the Ten Great Saints back then, she just didn't care as long as it didn't impact Glenda's duties.

She hadn't imagined that Glenda was under Granbell's thumb however and that she was practically enslaved by him. She bore no ill will to Glenda so she could only be happy for her former subordinates freedom.

On her right row was Leonard followed by Arnaud, Litus, Fritz, Garde, and Bacchus.

Everyone had been called back from their stations for this meeting, even the ones stationed in Tempest thanks to the teleportation circles linking Tempest, Azeroth, and Ruberious together.

She noticed Saare looking at her with an ashen expression for some reason, curious, she would have to inquire as to why he looked like that.

She felt Saare's Unique Skill attempt to analyze her Multi-Dimensional Barrier and just raised a brow as she simply willed for his Skill to fail.

As an Ultimate Awakened her understanding of the Laws of the World allowed her to easily brush off the effects of Skills as long as they didn't reach close to the Ultimate level.

She knew that Saare's Skill specialized in copying Arts, however he didn't master them instantly, he merely gained an understanding of the Art in question, to truly master an Art would depend on his affinity for the Art and his own efforts.

She guessed that Saare was attempting to analyze the Dimension Fault aspects of Multi-Dimensional Barrier.

"Hello everyone, it has been quite some time." She began.

"Indeed it has been some time, Lady Hinata." Leonard responded. "I am glad to see that you are in good health, we had been wondering what had happened to you after the attack on the Tempest Founding Festival."
She already had an excuse prepared, and while she disliked lying she would do so if she had to. "I was dealing with an enemy that had caused me some injuries that I needed time to recover from."

"For even Holy Magic to fail, you must have truly faced someone incredibly." Arnaud said. "And it seems you came out on top as well."
Her lips twitched hearing Arnaud, she wasn't one to take credit for something she didn't do so she shook her head. "I did not defeat my foe, Felix had saved me."

"The Demon Lord?!" Garde shouted. He was always one of the ones most against Ruberious' alliance with Tempest and Azeroth.

She nodded. "Yes, Demon Lord Felix White has become a rather close ally of mine."

"B-But he's a Demon Lord!" Garde objected.

She noticed quite a few people turn away from Garde, the ones who knew who the god Luminous truly was.

Not every member of the Nine Great Saints could be trusted with that information, due to Garde's impatience and his clear revulsion for Demon Lords Luminous decided not to inform him of her identity as she had others.

"Indeed he is the Demon Lord who saved my life." She stated with conviction.

"I don't know Demon Lord Felix all that well but he seemed like an alright guy to me. Looking back on my first encounter with him I would expect one of his nature to immediately kill me, however he sought to teach me a lesson so as to preserve my life in the future." Bacchus added.

Arnaud nodded. "Indeed, he may be a Daemon and a Demon Lord, but I do not think he is inherently malevolent and demonic, he seems to be a rather chaotic being instead."

Chaotic is one way to call Felix.

Garde looked at the two with a flabbergasted expression on his face before crossing his arms and leaning back in his chair. "Fine, I can see that I'm outnumbered here, besides this meeting isn't about the Demon Lord Felix or anything is it?" Garde asked as he looked at her.

She shook her head. "It is not, I heard from someon–" Before she could continue she heard Saare speak up.

"Y-You did it… didn't you?" He whispered with awe coloring his face.

She looked at him in confusion. "Did what?"

"You've become a Complete Saint." Saare voiced out with certainty.

Hinata raised a brow at Saare's incorrect assessment, though she couldn't blame Saare for that. Thanks to her spar with Felix she had managed to rein her Divinity in so that she didn't accidentally kill any weaker lifeform around her.

Though she didn't have perfect control of her power, and she doubted she would for a long time, she was releasing some of her power which must have been enough for Saare to feel the difference to her nature and come to an incorrect conclusion.

Her energy hadn't completely stabilized either yet, it was still slowly increasing, Felix had said he expected her EP to stabilize at around 3,400,000, and that is without the added on energy from her equipment.

Her EP would have been even higher, however forming an Ultimate Skill of her own reduced her own energy considerably.

"What?!"

"Truly?!"

"As expected of Lady Hinata."

"That's enough." She interrupted before things could get out of hand. She then turned to look at Saare and nodded. "I have evolved past my previous state." She stated, not wanting to tell another lie.

Saare sighed. "I see… it seems you have truly surpassed me then."
She didn't respond, she knew Saare's goal of eventually challenging her and taking back his position of leader.

Saare was fairly powerful, especially for his age, he was one of the youngest Saints in history, if he had time to grow he could become a fearsome fighter, she just had an unfair advantage.

She had one of the strongest Demon Lords in existence as her teacher, and she had centuries of experiences as a Hero, they just could not be compared anymore, but she wasn't going to leave Saare with nothing, her entire purpose for this meeting was to establish some new training norms among the Nine Great Saints while simultaneously testing all of them.

"The reason I called for this meeting is to test you all."

"Test us?" Fritz asked.

She nodded. "Yes. I have heard that you all have been slacking in your training somewhat. I will be correcting that all while seeing how far all of you have progressed."

Saare clicked his tongue. "Tsk. Fine then, I'm not dumb enough to see that fighting you would be good for my own growth."

She nodded with an approving smile. Her and Saare may never truly get along, but he was a good subordinate and he could be reasonable most of the time, he didn't let his wounded pride get in the way of his objectives which was something to be admired.

"It has been a long time since I have dueled you Lady Hinata, I am eager to learn under you once more." Leonard said.

Once she got everyone's agreement she stood up. "Excellent, we can discuss other things after our spar. Come, follow me." She said as she created a portal leading to their exclusive training ground.

No one was all that impressed with the portal, but she didn't expect them to be, short range teleportation was fairly easy to do after all, it was the longer ranges that made teleportation truly difficult.

Once everyone had walked through the portal, she closed it behind them.

She took her spot on the other side of the training field. The eight others stood across from her.

"In what order did you wish for us to fight?" Arnaud asked.

She stifled a smirk. "You can all come at me at once." She said with confidence.

"It seems someone has gotten too confident." Saare said as he narrowed his eyes.

His Elemental Armament, an inferior version of the Holy Armament she used, formed on his torso.

The Elemental Armament allowed the user to to bring out nearly 100% of their contracted Elemental's power when in use. Along with that, the Elemental Armament also imbued the user's weapon with Holy Power which allows the user to bypass most Resist Skills, making the users of the Elemental Armament the natural enemy of anything Non-Human.

In exchange for the boost in strength, the Elemental Armament cost a significant amount of energy to maintain, so it was not suited for drawn out battles. Due to Saare's nature as an Incomplete Saint he could maintain the Elemental Armament's power longer than most. However, even that didn't make him immune to its draining effects.

Saare drew his blade as he stood at the ready. The rest of the Nine Great Saints also followed after Saare and equipped their armor and weapons.

"We will not go easy on your Lady Hinata." Bacchus warned.

"Good, you will need to do your best." She goaded.

"Draw your weapon." Saare demanded, his voice low and tense. His eyes narrowed with determination as he faced her down.

With a flick of her wrist, Hinata extended her hand, and the hilt of her Divine Moonlight rapier materialized in her palm, its ethereal glow casting an otherworldly light around her.

Saare's eyes widened in shock, the grip on his sword tightening as he muttered. "Th-That's...!"

The sight of her God-Grade rapier was enough to shake even the most confident of warriors. Hinata knew it was unfair to wield such a weapon against Saare and his team, who were equipped only with Unique-Grade gear. Yet, she would hold back, ensuring the fight remained a learning experience for them and an opportunity for her to attune herself to Divine Moonlight.

"Do not worry, I will hold back." She reassured them, her voice calm and steady. But her words only seemed to stoke the fire in Saare's heart. With a roar that echoed through the training ground, he surged forward, his speed generating a sonic boom that startled the others.

The training ground's barriers absorbed the shockwave, sparing the surroundings from destruction.

Hinata stood her ground, not bothering to don her armor, it would be overkill. Divine Moonlight blazed with Fighting Spirit as she met Saare's strike with the same elegance she had shown in her spar with Felix. The moment their blades clashed, a strong gust of wind surged out from the pressure, small sparks flying and illuminating the two of them for a moment.

That single moment of contact was enough for Saare to immediately sense the vast difference in their strength, her swordsmanship had grown astronomically in the past, she resided in the realms of truly divine swordsmanship in Felix's own words. If she wished she could cleave an entire mountain rage in half merely with her weapon and nothing else at this point.

Saare quickly leaped back, eyes wide with realization. He had put his all into the strike, and she hadn't even needed to take a step back to stabilize herself. She simply stood there, her posture relaxed as she held her ground.

Hinata allowed him to retreat, observing him with a measured gaze. The purpose of the fight was to allow them to learn and for her to gauge their combat styles. If he got demotivated so quickly she would have been left disappointed in him.

Now that she had returned to the future, aware of the challenges that lay ahead, she was determined to prepare Ruberious for the impending threat of the Eastern Empire.

She didn't doubt that Ruberious would get involved with the war with the Eastern Empire if things got dire. Luminous would wait to see how Felix and Rimuru could handle it. However, if they seemed to be having trouble, she would join without hesitation, the Nine Great Saints needed to be powerful enough for that.

"She's strong, much stronger than I thought." Saare announced, his voice tinged with awe and frustration.

"Tsk. It seems she wasn't just boasting when she challenged us." Garde muttered, clicking his tongue in irritation.

"We need to work together to stand a chance against Lady Hinata." Leonard suggested, his eyes never leaving Hinata's form.

Arnaud nodded, shifting his stance slightly as he prepared. "Right. Let's go together."

With that, all of them dashed forwards.

The group moved in unison, their determination palpable. Leonard's armor fused with his Elemental, allowing him to channel its full power, a feat the others mirrored. Their auras flared as they called upon their respective Elementals.

Arnaud with Wind, Bacchus with Earth, Litus with Water, Garde with Flame, Fritz with Wind, Grigori with Earth, and Saare with Wind.

Their power surged, transforming them into formidable opponents as they channeled the formidable power of a Greater Elemental on top of their own rising power.

There was a reason that it was believed that they used to be able to challenge the Demon Lord Council, even if Hinata knew that to be completely untrue, but that did not detract from their prowess.

Greater Elementals on their own could threaten an entire Kingdom if left unchecked, and now each of them possessed that level of power at minimum.

Each one could match a Calamity-Class foe, while Saare barely edged into Disaster-Class, in the past when in this state she had to take Saare seriously, relying on Usurper to weaken his powers enough for her to come out as the victor, but now that was no longer necessary.

Hinata dashed forward, deliberately maintaining a speed they could follow. Even so, her movements were a blur.

She moved across the battlefield in an unpredictable pattern, dodging and weaving through those charging at her, yet as she noticed a blade heading in her direction, she couldn't help but smile. Fritz had correctly guessed the path that she was taking.

It was a small test to see who had been paying attention to their previous fights since this was a move she had used against them in the past. She would have to make sure to praise him after the fight, yet she pushed those thoughts to the back of her mind as she sidestepped the attack.

Using her free arm, she sent Fritz flying with a well-placed punch. His body crashed into the barrier of the training ground.

"Shit! She's behind us!" Saare yelled in panic, his voice echoing across the training ground.

With a flourish of her blade, Hinata unleashed an Aura Slash at Saare. He barely managed to raise his Fighting Spirit-coated blade in time to block, but her attack tore through his defenses, sending his weapon flying from his grip.

"Gah!" Saare cried out, clutching the deep wound left by her strike.

"I was serious when I said this would be a test. I will not hold back completely." She reprimanded him, her voice carrying a steely resolve.

Saare gritted his teeth, using Holy Magic to heal himself. Hinata shifted her focus to the rest of the team, who were closing in on her.

They converged, a coordinated assault designed to overwhelm her.

Leonard was the first to attack, clearly trying to draw her attention to him as he began his assault. His attacks were all strong and precise, yet the subtle glances he let escape betrayed his true intentions.

Taking a mental note for later, she saw him conjure spears of light, only for her to dispel them with a simple breath, a trick she had learned from Felix. It infuriated Leonard just as much as it had her when she first encountered it.

Even without Leonard's accidental slip-up, she could hear the subtle sounds of the ground being disturbed behind her. So, with a swift movement she jumped into the air, spinning in the air to look down as Garde released a concentrated Flame Breath right where she had stood moments before.

Felix had taught her the importance of caution, to focus on even the smallest of changes, why take a hit if it could be avoided? Though, right after he said to ignore that advice when showboating.

The moment she began to fall, she saw Litus leap upwards by expelling Fighting Spirit from the soles of her feet. The small girl was moving with surprising speed. Keeping her guard up as she continued to jump in the air in the most unpredictable pattern she could to avoid any surprise hits from Hinata.

When in range of the falling Hinata, who was simply allowing her body to freefall, Litus raised her blade upwards and slashed downwards toward her. Yet with a simple flick of her hand, she used her rapier to deflect Litus' attack.

As Litus' blade was pushed back, it left her wide open for a follow-up as Hinata created a magic circle in front of her, which sent the girl flying away with a burst of wind. Another thing to add to her list of things to improve upon. Litus could have used the force of her own deflection to send a kick, but she had allowed herself to be left wide open.

As she descended, she deftly parried the magic attacks hurled at her. She admired their effort. At least they weren't letting her descent go unchallenged. However, their attempts were futile.

Landing softly on the ground, Hinata smiled as she felt the ground under her turn soft, almost liquid. Bacchus was trying to make her lose her footing as he caused countless earth spikes to pierce the soft ground directly aimed at her.

Using the very spikes meant to harm her as a platform, she jumped before casting a spell of her own to shatter the spikes, allowing her to land on the ground once again, unharmed.

She turned to face the eight of them. Saare and Litus had recovered, but their faces were pale with the realization of the challenge they faced.

"Come," she said, a glint of determination in her eyes. "We are just getting started."

Each of them exchanged wary glances before charging together. This time, their attacks were more synchronized, their strategies more refined. Leonard thrust his blade forward, aiming for her midsection while Bacchus tried to trap her feet with rising earth.

Hinata parried Leonard's weapon with a flick of her wrist and leaped over Bacchus's earth trap, her movements a blur of grace and precision.

As she landed, Arnaud's wind blades sliced through the air towards her. They arched through the air, surrounding her before the winds changed, and they all attacked at once. She quickly spun, her rapier still alight with Fighting Spirit as she quickly deflected each wind blade in one swift and graceful movement.

As the broken wind blades harmlessly passed by her as nothing but a gust, Hinata saw a flaming wall erupt around her as the temperature spiked by thousands of degrees. She immediately realized that Garde was attempting to engulf her in a fiery inferno.

Conjuring a barrier of pure Holy Power, Hinata dispersed the flames around her, revealing that Garde had only used it as a temporary cover to try to sneak an attack with his spear.

Dodging the spear, she grabbed it with her free hand as it passed by her. Her eyes narrowed before she sent a kick to his stomach. Garde lost his breath, but he didn't let go of his weapon. That was until Hinata raised her rapier and forced him to jump backward.

As Garde landed, he felt the back of the spear hit him in the forehead as Hinata threw it at him as if it were a javelin, sending him crashing to the ground.

Using the opening when Hinata had thrown Garde's spear, Fritz and Grigori flanked her. Yet even then, Hinata's rapier danced between them, blocking and countering with such speed that they struggled to keep up.

Though their attacks were coordinated, they were not exploiting the small opening she had given them as she had hoped. Taking a few more mental notes, she ducked underneath Grigori's halberd and sent a well-placed kick that sent him sprawling.

Blocking Fritz's attack, she pushed him back using her own assault, sending countless feints that forced him to dodge until she finally sent a slash. Fritz's mind had been so focused on blocking the countless feints that when the real attack came, he was left wide open.

She watched as Fritz staggered back from her strike. Hinata straightened, lowering her rapier slightly as her opponents caught their breath. She could see how they realized just how out of their league she was, but she could also see their desire to improve. She was glad she had such wonderful subordinates.

Story: I'm a Daemon, so what?

Chapter 83: Domestic Violence!

- Hinata Sakaguchi -

Hinata straightened, lowering her rapier slightly as her opponents caught their breath. She could see how they realized just how out of their league she was, but she could also see their desire to improve. She was glad she had such wonderful subordinates.

"Well done all of you." She voiced out as everyone began catching their breaths. "It seems you have all been putting some effort into your training." She twirled her rapier as she smiled. "Now let us resume this bout."

As she mentally planned the training lessons she lunged at Saare who had taken the moment she had granted him to regain a fraction of his strength.

The Fighting Spirit on her rapier dulled its edge, or else Saare's weapon would shatter right on contact.

As their blades met, they released a shower of sparks. Saare gritted his teeth, pouring all his strength into pushing her back. But her ability with the blade was almost unmatched.

Saare at the very least couldn't contend against her before she leaped back in time, gaining far more experience, let alone now. Hinata swung her blade, putting more and more strength into each clash before sending a final combo.

Rearing her blade back, she struck at him weakly, smiling as she saw him brace for the clash. Yet the moment his body relaxed from the weak attack, she struck again, disarming him with a deft twist of her wrist with minimal effort, sending his sword flying.

Litus had been using Hinata's exchange with Saare to summon a torrent of water to sweep her off her feet. Yet with Saare defeated, that left Hinata to slice through the water with her rapier, dissipating it into a fine mist.

Before Litus could react, Hinata had vanished from her view. In the blink of an eye, Hinata reappeared in front of Litus, her blade stopping just short of Litus's throat.

Litus froze, eyes wide with shock. Hinata lowered her rapier, nodding in approval before turning to face the remaining warriors.

They attacked with renewed vigor, their desperation evident. But Hinata was relentless. She moved through them like a whirlwind, her rapier a blur of silver light. Leonard's elemental armor shattered under her assault, Bacchus's earth constructs crumbled, and Arnaud's wind attacks were rendered useless.

One by one, every single one of the so-called "Great Saints" were felled, until only Saare and Arnaud remained standing.

Saare's breath came in ragged gasps, his body battered and bruised. But there was a fire in his eyes, a determination that would not be extinguished.

Arnaud was clenching the hilt of his blade tightly as his eyes narrowed at her.

She twirled her rapier lightly in her hand, a mocking smile playing on her lips as she observed the two men before her. "Is that all?" She taunted, her voice dripping with disdain. "Have you given up already?"

Saare gritted his teeth, his muscles tensing. "A little pain won't take me out." He turned his head slightly toward Arnaud. "You ready?" He growled, his voice was strained.

Arnaud met his gaze with steely determination, his sword now glowing with the combined power of the elementals. "I am." Arnaud spoke as his blade began to shimmer, the air around it humming with the gathering energy of five elements, fire, water, wind, earth, and space, each color blending into a radiant, lethal aura.

Thankfully at this point I'm fairly certain I'm safe from being erased out of existence since Chloe's time loop has ended, but you can never be careful.

"Correct, I am still dedicating a portion of my processing power for such a scenario when Chloe's Time Leap is once again activated, or how to prevent its activation in the first place."

'Great, thanks. The more options I have the better.'

"Felix-nii!" Chloe shouted in surprise.

I nodded. "Chloe, there was something I wanted to talk about for a moment."

Chloe clapped. "Sure, if it won't be long I'm sure the rest won't notice."
I nodded as I walked forward, subtly isolating our conversation. "It won't be long, I just wanted to let you know not to tell anyone else about my ability to copy Skills." Ever since Hinata told me I knew I'd have to speak to Chloe about this. I didn't want one of my biggest trump cards getting out after all.
Chloe's eyes widened as she laughed nervously. "Ah… Hinata-nee told you?"

"She did."

Chloe pouted. "Fine, fine, I wasn't going to tell anyone anyway, well other than Rimuru if he asks."

"That's good enough for me."

I doubt Rimuru will care much, though if his Raphael is anything like how Odin was, I'm sure it will make all sorts of countermeasures.

"Countermeasures that will fail. My little sister is far from my current capabilities."

'Little sister eh?'

"That is practically what we are."

'I suppose that's true, you want me to help your little sister out by telling Rimuru how to evolve it?'

"That is not needed, Raphael is not yet ready to evolve, when the time comes it will happen on its own."

'You just haven't finished making countermeasures against Raphael have you?'

"...That may be part of it."

'Have it your way then, if Raphael evolves or not will be left up to fate then I guess.'

"Chronoa wishes to know when you want to spar." Chloe asked.

I shrugged my shoulders. "Next time, I've had a lot of spars lately and have some work left to do."

Chloe pouted. "Fine, but I know you're just scared!" Chloe said brattily.

I rolled my eyes. "Sure sure."

I turned around. "That was all I came here for, see y–"

"Mister Felix!" I turned to the voice and saw Kenya running towards me, the other kids gradually began coming out of their hiding spots.

"Kenya."

Kenya shifted nervously. "I-I heard that you would be taking me to meet big sis El, is that true?"

I nodded. "Yeah, it is. Though not right now."

When I took Kenya to Sarion I wanted to visit and tour the Elven Empire a bit myself, so I'd take him after sorting out some stuff back in Azeroth first.

Kenya nodded excitedly. "That's fine!"

Alice crossed her arms next to Kenya, a pout forming on her lips. "I want to learn under big sis too!"
"Haha, well Elmesia doesn't have much free time, I'm sure she didn't mean to be hurtful by singling one of you out."

Alice huffed. "I know, but it's still not fair!" Alice yelled as she smacked Kenya in the back.

Is this domestic violence I am witnessing?

"Gah! Don't hit me Alice!" Kenya cried out as he rubbed his back.

"Hmph!"

"Come on Alice… you can just admit you'll miss him." Gale nervously said.

Hearing him Alice gave him a death glare. "As if I would miss him!"

Ah, so a burgeoning tsundere too.

"I'll leave you all to your games now." I waved., leaving Kenya to deal with the tsundere in training.

I appeared in my office in an instant. "It's nice to be back." I mumbled as I took in the familiar room.

In an instant my maid appeared beside me. "Master."

I turned to the side to look at her, she looked as pristine as always, not a single wrinkle in her garbs.

"How did the training with Middray go?" I inquired.
Raiden gave me a rare, smug smile. "Sir Middray asked me to spar with Frey as she had also requested training."

I raised an eyebrow, intrigued by her confidence. "I'm guessing you demolished her?"

"At first, she was at my mercy." Raiden admitted. "However, she then displayed a Unique Skill of some kind that caused me to be wary and hold myself back. I still soundly defeated her, but it was not as easy as I originally thought it would be."

"She was a Demon Lord for a reason." I said thoughtfully. "That Unique Skill of hers can be pretty troublesome."

Reflector would allow Frey to reflect any damage she took back onto her opponent. The downside was that she needed to take that damage herself, so it could be pretty easy to circumvent. Just kill Frey in one attack or before she could use her Skill.

However, I was sure Raiden had misunderstood something and held back due to that. If you don't understand the full capabilities of your enemy, you're at a disadvantage in a fight.

"I'll leave it to you to figure out what her exact abilities are," I said, not wanting to stifle her growth by giving her all the answers.

Raiden bowed. "As you wish."

"Now where's Arcueid, there is something I need to speak to her about."

"Lady Arcueid is currently in her office."

I nodded. "Great, thanks."

Chapter 84: Gleipnir

- Felix -

"Now where's Arcueid, there is something I need to speak to her about."

"Lady Arcueid is currently in her office." Raiden answered.

I nodded. "Great, thanks. That's all I need for now, Raiden."

Raiden bowed once more before vanishing.

A moment later I appeared in front of Arcueid's office.

After knocking I heard a response. "Come in, My Lord."

I opened the door and was met with Arcueid looking up at me from behind her desk with a beautiful smile.

She stood up and bowed. "My Lord." She said as her crimson red eyes, tinted with adoration gazed into my own.

"Arcueid, I won't keep you busy for too long, I just wanted to see if you finished making the initial contract to use to trade with Dagruel."

Arucied stood straight as she summoned a piece of paper, though I could see the magic woven into it.

"I have." She handed it to me.

I quickly looked it over. "It looks good to me. In return for the natural resources Dagruel's territory lacks he will provide us with access to some of the rare natural ore there as well as gold."

Dagruel's main issue is that his entire territory is barren and corrupted due to the fight between Milim and Guy that took place there.

Thanks to this there are massive sandstorms that could tear even powerful B Ranked beings apart. Due to this Dagruel sends some of his people out to gather supplies from other Kingdoms, but this isn't very efficient, many die on the journey itself and the journey takes a lot of time.

Despite how easy teleportation is to me, it isn't the same for everyone else, teleporting is a fairly high level Magic, and teleporting over vast distances is practically impossible for even a Saint.

There was a reason Dagruel wanted Luminous' fertile territory, his people's lives were literally depending on it.

I wasn't against helping a guy like Dagruel, from what I've heard he seemed to be a guy trying his best for his people, I could respect that even if he became an enemy in another timeline due to that reason.

In the end this deal with Dagruel wasn't about making a profit or anything, it was about making an ally, and if Dagruel ends up not being an ally then you should still keep your allies close and your enemies even closer.

In the other timeline Dagruel was an enemy, it was best if I could get rid of that possibility entirely, but if not then having some sort of in with him could still be useful.

Arcueid went on to explain some more things she had learned.

"I'll contact Dagruel about arranging a meeting with one of his people then." I said.

Arcueid nodded gracefully. "As you wish My Lord. Though there is one thing I would like to inform you about."

I raised a brow. "Oh? And what is that?"

"Due to your interest in an alliance with Demon Lord Dagruel I gathered more information that you may find useful." Arcueid stated.

My eyes widened. "Oh! Thanks Arcueid, that would help. I don't know all that much about the Giants and even Dagruel himself. I was planning to ask Dagura, Liura, and Debura about him."

Arcueid smiled. "It is no problem my lord. I myself analyzed Dagruel's three children and found out that they have extremely high levels of Magic Resistance."

I nodded. "I knew they had Magic Resistance, though I don't quite know the level of it."

"It is an impressive level of Magic Resistance, greater than even the natural Magic Resistance us Daemons possess. Most Magic will prove to be ineffective against those three, only high level Spells like Nuclear Cannon and others of similar power could harm them." Arcueid informed.

I internally prayed for the safety of those three, I doubt Arcueid didn't test what she was telling me herself, which means those three had to deal with Arcueid firing Nuclear Cannons at them, that does not sound fun at all.

"High levels of Magic Resistance huh?" I mumbled as I handed the contract back to Arcueid.

Now is that Magic Resistance something intrinsic to just those three, or do all Giants have that?

If all the Giants have that it could be troublesome if things follow the same route as the other timeline, ending up with Dagruel as an enemy and actively in a war with him. My largest fighting force was the Daemons under me, and Daemons specialized in Magic above all else.

I suppose I can just ask them, they are children of Dagruel so I'm sure they are somewhat aware of those kinds of things.

"I see, thank you for informing me about that Arcueid. I'll be checking up on them now myself."
Arcueid smiled. "As you wish My Lord."

I nodded. "I'll leave you to your work then. I'll stop by some other time when you aren't as busy so we can hang out."

"It is no trouble for you to appear at your whim my lord." Arcueid stated.

"Yeah, but I don't want to bother you if I don't have to, even if you yourself don't consider it a bother."

Before Arcueid could protest like I knew she would. "Thanks for taking care of all this work for me, I'll be around later." I said, teleporting to where I sensed the three children of Dagruel as well as Saeko.

I materialized in one of the many training fields with my presence concealed. This one wasn't located in a separate dimension, but it was fortified with layers upon layers of barriers, each designed to contain the power of any explosive battle that takes place within.

I looked around the training field, I spotted the three sons of Dagruel being trained by Saeko in the center, but there were also many others.

There was still light out so it didn't surprise me that some were still out training.

There were around 1,500, Majin, all training as their Auras shimmered around them.

I could only be impressed at how strong each of them was, none were below the B Rank and some were at the A Rank. A force of 1,500 at that level was fairly impressive.

I decided to observe Saeko's spar, I wasn't in a hurry.

Saeko rested Hercules Edge casually on her shoulder, its edge gleaming ominously in the dimming light. "Come on, you three! Show me what you're made of!" She commanded.

"But big sis!" Dagura's voice was tinged with desperation, his eyes wide with reluctance. "Lady Arcueid already pushed us to the brink!"

Liura nodded, his face pale. "Yeah, we've barely caught our breath!"

Debura, on the other hand, seemed lost in his own world, mumbling, "Hehe, food…"

Saeko ignored their pleas. "Excuses won't save you. If you won't come at me… then I'll come at you!"

Multiple barriers formed into existence around the four, separating their fight from affecting the others' training, though the other soldiers around had already stopped training and decided to watch the upcoming battle.

It seems Saeko has learned to be more mindful of her surroundings..

In an instant, she hefted Hercules Edge high above her head, the blade igniting with a ferocious aura. The sheer pressure of her Fighting Spirit exploded outward, causing the very air around her to tremble. The three brothers stiffened, likely sensing the danger Saeko now posed to them.

Even their hefty Magic Resistance wouldn't work against Battlewill.

"Move, now!" Dagura shouted, the three brothers each lit up in Fighting Spirit.

Each of their powers was incredibly potent, easily bringing them to the cusps of Disaster Class, it seems Saeko has been training them well.

Saeko brought Hercules Edge crashing down, the force of the swing cleaving the ground with a thunderous roar. A wave of raw energy erupted from the point of impact, a blazing arc that tore through the earth and hurtled towards the brothers, that strike alone could easily cleave through a mountain range with ease.

Saeko had seriously been improving all this time. I couldn't help but smile proudly as I thought of that.

The ground beneath the trio of brothers buckled and shattered, debris flying as the energy wave surged forward. The sheer power of the attack was impressive, easily in the Demon Lord Class, though of course on the weaker end.

The air crackled with the mixed power of all four fighters. The brothers barely had time to brace themselves, their eyes wide with a mixture of awe and fear.

But in the split second before impact, they moved. Dagura, the eldest, barked out a quick command, and the three brothers mustered their Fighting Spirit, channeling it into their legs. With a synchronized leap, they soared into the air, narrowly avoiding the devastating wave as it obliterated the ground where they had stood.

The barriers absorbed the remnant power of Saeko's attack so the rest of the training field isn't destroyed.

Saeko grinned. "Good!"
She didn't have a chance to say more as the trio rushed her in perfect coordination, their earlier hesitation gone.

They each moved while keeping the others in mind, it seems their brotherly bond allowed them some way to instinctively understand the other two brothers intentions, either that or they were just incredibly used to each other.

Dagura took the lead, his fists crackling with energy as he aimed a powerful punch at Saeko's midsection. Liura flanked her left, his palms glowing with concentrated energy as he prepared a series of rapid jabs aimed at her ribs, while Debura, the largest and fattest of the three, charged in from the right, his massive frame poised to deliver a crushing elbow strike.

Saeko's eyes gleamed with excitement and pride as she watched her students make their moves.

Heh, it seems she wasn't as nonchalant about the three as she liked to act.

Fighting Spirit shimmered around Hercules Edge dulling the edge, it seems despite wanting a spar Saeko didn't want to brutally wound her pupils.

She met Dagura's punch head-on, using the flat of Hercules Edge to absorb the impact, the blade vibrated with the force as a miniature shock wave exploded outwards out from the impact.

She then spun on her heel, the blade arcing gracefully through the air as she deflected Liura's jabs with quick, precise movements, each strike ringing out as the powerful Stardust enhanced blade met flesh.

If Saeko wasn't expelling her own energy to weaken the power behind Hercules Edge's attacks the trio would have already been torn apart.

With a swift shift of her stance, Saeko brought the sword down to intercept Debura's elbow, the force of his strike meeting the unyielding edge of her weapon and sending shockwaves through the ground.

I raised an impressed brow as I took in Saeko's sheer skill. Before when I first met her she got by through her sheer unnatural strength, no technique, all power, but now she was dismantling the trio not through raw power but through martial skill.

It seems her training with Arcueid, Lalatina, and Megumin has been paying off, those three had plenty of skills that they could teach.

The brothers didn't let up. Dagura followed up with a spinning kick, aiming for Saeko's head, while Liura crouched low, sweeping his leg in an attempt to trip her. Debura recovered quickly, launching a powerful knee strike toward her ribs.

Saeko flowed between their attacks like water, her movements precise and effortless. She ducked under Dagura's kick and then, with a quick pivot, used the flat of Hercules Edge to block Liura's sweeping leg, the force of the clash causing the ground to crack beneath them. As Debura's knee strike came in, she twisted her body just enough to let it pass by, before using the momentum to swing her sword in a wide arc, creating a powerful Aura fueled gust of wind that pushed the Giant brothers back slightly.

Dagura and Liura switched tactics, moving in tandem to corner Saeko. Dagura feinted a punch to her face while Liura aimed a quick, powerful palm strike toward her chest. Debura took advantage of the opening, attempting to grapple her from behind, his massive arms reaching out to trap her in a bear hug.

Saeko's eyes gleamed as Debura held Saeko's arms tightly. Just before she would have been punched, she spun on her heel, narrowly avoiding Dagura's punch and Liura's strike. She then slammed Hercules Edge into the ground, creating a shockwave that rippled outwards, causing the earth to tremble and disrupting their coordination. As Debura lunged at her from behind, she swiftly turned and brought Hercules Edge up, the flat of the blade slamming into his chest and sending him skidding back with a pained grunt.

"Impressive," Saeko remarked, her voice calm even as she deflected another barrage of punches. "You've all grown stronger."

Looking at it from the side, Saeko almost seemed like a good teacher rather than the berserker she styled herself as.

It seems taking in some students did some good for Saeko as well, there was a saying about that.

"Indeed, the master learns from the pupil just as much as the pupil learns from the master."

'Yeah, that.'

The three brothers panted as they attempted to recover some of the energy they had expelled.

Saeko however wouldn't let them do that in peace.

She exhaled as her Aura flared around her. Hercules Edge began emanating a far more dangerous light as more Fighting Spirit was channeled through it.

The blade began to glow with an intense light, the power behind the blade increasing dramatically. The air around it seemed to warp from the sheer power being concentrated into the weapon.

Saeko channeled some Fighting Spirit into her feat, and with a swift movement, Saeko leaped high into the air, soaring above the battlefield. The brothers' eyes widened in shock as they realized what was coming.

"Take this!" Saeko shouted in excitement.

As Saeko ascended she raised Hercules Edge above her before reaching the peak of her leap. Saeko hovered in the air for a moment as Hercules Edge glimmered under the sunlight as it began pressuring the surroundings.

Then, with a powerful swing, she brought the sword crashing down into the earth below, hitting the three with the attack directly would most definitely be fatal if they didn't heal in time.

The ground trembled as the colossal blade cut through the air, descending with unstoppable force. The energy trailing behind the strike carved through the very air, creating a shockwave that rippled outward.

The brothers could only brace themselves as the blade connected with the ground, the impact creating a massive crater that would have sunk an entire city if the barrier wasn't attempting to contain the damage.

The barrier Saeko placed trembled against the force of Saeko's attack, in the blink of an eye I channeled my own energy through Saeko's barrier completely unnoticed, further reinforcing it.

A cloud of dust and debris were sent into the air due to the impact.

The force of the attack was overwhelming, and they were sent tumbling backward, unable to maintain their footing against the sheer power Saeko had unleashed as the training grounds crumbled beneath them.

Before the three could sink into the earth Saeko quickly vanished in a burst of Fighting Spirit and moved the three of them outside of the barrier she placed at the start.

The trio was sprawled on the ground, breathing heavily and struggling to rise. Saeko landed gracefully, resting the Hercules Edge on her shoulder, a proud smile playing on her lips as she looked down at the three.

She hadn't even needed to use Cook to demolish the three sons of Dagruel, merely skill with her Ōdachi and masterful use of Battlewill.

"Amazing…" One of the soldiers mumbled as awe tinted his voice.

"As expected of Lady Saeko!" One of the Kijin said.

Many others began praising her and even Dagura, Liura and Debura for the good showing.

"That was a good showing you three, you have improved since I first beat you up back then."

"Ugh, still not as good as you big sis." Debura cried out as he slowly got up.

"Hmph! I am Felix-sama's number one secretary!" Saeko preened.

I clapped as I unveiled my presence. "That was a good showing, from all four of you."

With my presence now visible and all the soldiers' gaze snapped to me.

"Felix-sama!" Saeko shouted in surprise.

"You all can go back to your training."

All of them quickly bowed and looked away, though I could tell they were distracted which was normal.

They were in the presence of their sovereign, it was normal to be a bit nervous.

"Felix-sama!" Saeko greeted me once I arrived in front of her.

I smiled. "Saeko." I turned to Dagura, Liura, and Debura who looked quite beat up. "Hello you three."

It seems Arcueid's Nuclear Cannon didn't leave any permanent damage which is good.
The three of them saluted me. " " "Lord Felix!" " "

"I'm actually here to talk to you three about something." I looked to Saeko. "Do you mind if I borrow them?" Neither of us minded much that we got straight to business. I spoke to Saeko every day, and we all ate dinner together every night since I enjoyed eating good food. Everyone else just sorta joined in and it began a nightly tradition, even Sukuna was there.

Saeko proudly crossed her arms under her generous bust. "Do as you please with them! I have been training them to be of use to you!" Saeko said unashamedly.

I nodded. "I will then." I looked around at the other soldiers. "Are these the Purple Guards I've heard about?"

I'd only heard about Saeko's minions offhandedly from Megumin, she had complimented them on their dedication to training, I don't really pay much attention to what happens in my territory so it's fairly normal that I didn't know about them before that.

From what I understand they are a mixed group of Majin, some are Ogres from the Ogre Village that wanted to serve me or Saeko, some were even Ogres that were killed back during the Falmuth Invasion and were revived as Kijin with more death aligned abilities.

Saeko smirked proudly. "They are."

"You've trained them well, good job Saeko."

A giddy smile spread across Saeko's face. "Thank you Felix-sama!"

"I'm just giving you your due praise. Ah, by the way Luminous wanted me to send you over to her sometime, I think she likes you."

Saeko tilted her head. "But I serve you Felix-sama."

I shrugged my shoulders. "It's fine, as long as you aren't gone for too long I don't mind you living your own life."

Saeko nodded. "I will visit Luminous then! Perhaps she can further improve my cooking!"

I noticed Dagura, Liura, and Debura shivering from the corner of my eyes.

Truly, Saeko's test subjects have been subjected to a truly cruel fate.

Though to be fair Saeko's food hasn't tasted bad after she got her Unique Skill: Cook, it just looks appetizing as hell, and even that issue is something she has been improving on.

Maybe Luminous can pull out another miracle.

"I'll send you over now if you aren't busy?"

Saeko narrowed her eyes as she looked around the training field. "Listen here you maggots!"

My lips twitched as I heard Saeko.

"I will be leaving to further improve my crafts and be of more use to Felix-sama, if I find that any of you have been slacking…" Saeko cracked her knuckles. "Then you'll be in a world of pain!"

Why does Saeko sound like some yakuza bully?

"Because she is one."

" " "Y-Yes Lady Saeko!" " " All the troops chanted.

Saeko nodded in satisfaction before she looked back to the sinking portion of the training ground where her fight took place. "And someone get that fixed!"

"Y-Yes Lady Saeko!" One of the female Kijin's replied.

Saeko nodded as she turned to look back at me. "I am ready, Felix-sama. Do not hesitate to call upon me should you require your loyal secretary!"

I nodded. "Right, I'll call you if I need you. Have fun with Luminous." God knows both Saeko and Luminous need more friends.

Before I could transport Saeko, I was interrupted.

"It is recommended to hold off on transporting Saeko to Luminous' precise location, instead I suggest transporting her to Hinata Sakaguchi's location."

'Alright.'

I didn't really care enough to ask why Othinus wanted me to do that, it wasn't a big deal to me.

"Actually I'll be sending you to Hinata first, play nice."
Saeko nodded. "Very well!"

I snapped my fingers sending Saeko straight to Hinata's location.

I'm sure that'll be fine.

I turned back to Dagura, Liura, and Debura. "Now let's go you three."

The three nervously nodded before I teleported us to one of the rooms in my palace.

I sat on one of the love seats as I gestured to the two other couches present in the room. "Take a seat you three."

All three nodded. Dagura and Liura shared one couch while Debura got another to himself, and even then Debura occupied the entire couch.

"I have a few questions for you three. I'm looking into forming an alliance of sorts with your father, this would include providing access to natural resources, something your people lack." I started.

Dagura's eyes widened. "Really?!"
I nodded. "Really."

Dagura sighed in relief as he gave me a wide smile. "Ha, that's great! I'm still loyal to you Lord Felix, but I do still feel for the plight of my people. If you have a way to help father in feeding all of the Giants then I would be very grateful."

Dagura stood up and bowed, as did Liura and Debura. Dagura seems to be the leader among the three.

"No need to bow, I was already planning to help your father out. Honestly you can visit your home if you're ever homesick, it's not like you need to dedicate your entire life to me."

Each of them were greater than the average Demon Lord Seed individual, but it wouldn't be much of a loss if they decided they wanted to head back home for a while.

I have plenty of strong beings that I can call upon if I need something done. Daemons are seriously useful minions, just name and incarnate an Arch Daemon and they become a Disaster Class with the potential to grow.

The three sat down as Dagura shook his head. "Father had kicked us out, I do not think returning would be wise. I do not wish to face his wrath." Dagura laughed nervously.

Liura and Debura nodded along with their elder brother.

"Before I ask my questions, how have you three been doing here?" I kinda just threw them onto Saeko, it seems they have been thriving, but like any good boss it's good to check in.

"We have undergone intense training under Lady Saeko, mental training, physical training, we have become more resistant to negative status effects such as paralysis, poison, sleep and various other things." Dagura answered.

I raised a brow. "Resistance against poison and paralysis huh? Good job, those aren't easy to acquire."
Normal gaining Resist Skills are incredibly difficult, you need to be inflicted with the negative status effect many times and fight against it until eventually a Resist Skill develops, I just cheated.

Dagura rubbed the back of his head. "No thank you Lord Felix! If it weren't for you and Lady Saeko we would have continued with our old ways, staying stagnant. I think I understand why father kicked us out now. Now we have friends that we can fight with for fun and various other luxuries."

I nodded. "I see, I'm glad you like it here. Then let me get into my questions. I already know the general history of your father's territory but let me double check it with you."

Dagura nodded.

I explained everything I knew, from the fight with Milim and Guy corrupting the land to Dagruel's efforts to gather resources from other Kingdoms and his struggles in doing so.

Dagura nodded. "That's about right. The higher level Giants like us and some others don't need much food or water if we need any, but the lesser members of our race do not share the same benefits, and so they suffer as much as my father works to provide for them."
"That sounds like what I know, well then do you have any more information you can share? Military strength, the stronger fighters under your father, anything really."

I wouldn't blame them if they didn't want to betray their father in that way.

Dagura tilted his head. "I was not aware of the inner workings of my father's forces, we were merely princes in name with no political power of our own. Though I do know a little bit."

"Anything could be useful." I answered.

"Then I will start with where my father and the rest of the Giants primarily stay. The Heaven Tower."

My eyebrows shot up hearing about the Heaven Tower.

"I see, I knew the Heaven Tower was in Dagruel's territory, but I didn't think they would use it as a base of operations. It's not like there is much information on the inner goings of Dagruel's territory."

Dagura nodded. "It is one of the safest locations and serves as the capital of my father's territory."

"I see."

"As for the military, I will start with my paternal uncle." Dagura began.

Paternal uncle huh? So one of the fragments of the so-called Mad Titan.

"Uncle Glassord is my father's right hand man, he leads the military and he is overwhelmingly powerful." Dagura gulped nervously. "I-I once sensed him training some of the Generals and he released his full power against them." Dagura's eyes were glazed. "His power was tremendous, greater than all three of ours combined."
Well that didn't tell me much at all.

"Do you think he was stronger than Saeko?"

Dagura nodded with confidence. "He most definitely had more energy than her, and as my father's right hand man he was likely very proficient in combat."

I nodded. "I see."

So he was in the Special-S Class then huh? An EP greater than 1,000,000 at minimum. Likely higher than that if he was Dagruel's brother, a part of the Mad Titan.

"Then the other Warrior Generals were also powerful, they were about as strong as I am individually, and some were slightly stronger or weaker." Dagura informed.

So around 200,000 EP on average then for the Generals.

"That is all I know about the military, but there is one other that you should know about." Dagura said nervously.

"Oh? And who is that?"

"Our Uncle Fenn… we heard of him in our bedtime stories."

"Fenn? So he's the last part of the Mad Titan then?"

Dagura nodded. "Fenn has been sealed since ancient times due to his personality. Unlike our uncle and father, Fenn never reformed and stuck with the same ways as the Mad Titan, so he was sealed by Veldanava himself deep inside the Heaven Tower."

For Veldanava to see Fenn as an actual threat to the world order he must have been powerful.

"Do you remember the legend itself?" Maybe the three brothers missed something in it, legends are often rooted in truth after all.

Dagrua nodded. "In ancient times, it is said that the evil gods were sealed away by the Star Dragon King. It is said that two of the three brothers reformed, my father, and Uncle Glassord. However one of them remained violent, so he was sealed by the chains of god. That is Fenn, and the chains that bind him are the famous chains of god, Gleipnir."

Gleipnir huh? That sounds familiar.

"In Norse Mythology, Gleipnir is the magical and seemingly unbreakable chain or ribbon used to bind the mighty wolf Fenrir. Crafted by the dwarves at the request of the gods, Gleipnir was made from six impossible ingredients, the sound of a cat's footsteps, the beard of a woman, the roots of a mountain, the sinews of a bear, the breath of a fish, and the spittle of a bird. Gleipnir was incredibly strong and was the only thing capable of holding Fenrir, the World Devouring Wolf who had grown so powerful that no ordinary chain could restrain him. The binding of Fenrir with Gleipnir is a significant event in Norse Mythology, as it is foretold that Fenrir will remain bound until Ragnarok, the end of the world, when he will break free and bring destruction to the gods."

It seems Veldanava took some inspiration from earth mythology then huh? It wouldn't surprise me if the overpowered True Dragon could glimpse into other worlds.

Though maybe there is some foreshadowing there? If the chains of Fenn, Gleipnir are broken, is the end of this world near? Is there some kind of prophecy I need to watch out for, or was Veldanava too lazy to come up with an original name and merely copied the name from mythology not meaning for there to be any significance behind it.

A single action from a being like Veldanava left even me in confusion. I suppose trying to understand the intentions of a guy who willingly stripped himself of his power was always going to be difficult.

"Once the memories of the Star King Dragon have been fully recreated and recorded you will have your answer Master."

'I suppose I will. You can't give me a glimpse of fragments of his memories?'

"Currently I cannot, as the memories have too much… weight behind them. I am devoting a large percentage of my process power to creating the memories and I am not even 10% of the way done. The memories I have recreated are the "weaker" memories as well, making them of less use as they involve more minor aspects of his existence. The memories closer to Veldanava's heart and more important to him are harder to recreate, and require more data."

'I see, I guess I was asking too much.'

"It is my own failure Master, I will continue to develop further to become the truly perfect partner."

'I don't see how that's possible, you're already perfect but I appreciate the enthusiasm.'

I ignored the weird feeling I was getting from Othinus and focused back on Dagura.

'Am I able to view the memories you have recreated?'

"I do not believe that is wise yet, Master. I have isolated the memories I have created and am in the process of removing the emotions from them. However the lingering will of the Star King, weakened as it is within the memories, is making it a time consuming process."

'That's fine then, whenever it's safe.'

I wasn't in a hurry to view Velda's memories. Perhaps it would give me an advantage against the Eastern Empire, but being reckless wasn't going to help things. If my Manas didn't think it was a good idea yet, then it wasn't a good idea. I trusted my partner at least that much.

Once again I got a warm, bubbly feeling come out from inside of me.

"How strong is Fenn then?"

Dagura gulped nervously. "In some legends that are spread in my father's territory it is said that father was beaten by Fenn, and Veldanava had to step in."

My eyes widened. "Beat Dagruel?! Well that's troublesome, it's a good thing he's sealed then."

Dagruel was a being that could be considered equal to a True Dragon. Veldora said he used to spar with Dagruel and neither side came out on top, though this was Veldora before meeting Rimuru so no Ultimate Skill and no technique.

Still a True Dragon is a True Dragon, almost no one could hope to challenge pre Rimuru Veldora, and yet Dagruel did, and Fenn still may have beat Dagruel?

If we end up having Dagruel as an enemy, would he unseal Fenn?

Then there was Glassord too, I have no idea how strong he could be, but as a fragment of the Mad Titan he is probably a beast too.

Dagura nodded. "Father had said Fenn possessed monstrous strength."

"I see, is that all you have?"

Dagura nodded apologetically. "It is, I apologize for not being of more use."
"Nah, you gave me enough information so thank you. I'll send you back to the training grounds now."

Dagura nodded. "Thank you Lord Felix."

With a snap of my fingers the three brothers were gone.

I suppose it's time to contact Dagruel then. I ran a finger across the curvature of the Demon Lord's Ring on my finger. Velzard could overhear this conversation if she wanted to, but I didn't really care, it's not like either she or Guy would care if I decided to ally with Dagruel.

I quickly got into the mindset of a ruler, formal vocabulary and all.

I willed the ring to connect to the ring I sensed west from Luminous' own. West of Ruberious was the Holy Void of Damargania.

The connection was established almost immediately.

"Is this Demon Lord Felix?" Dagruel's deep, resonant voice emerged from the ring.

"It is." I replied.

"I see, what did you need?" Dagruel asked, getting straight to the point.

"An alliance." I stated plainly.

"Oh? What kind of alliance?" His curiosity was evident, but so was his caution.

"For now, a trade agreement. If our partnership proves fruitful, it may evolve into something more substantial. I'm prepared to offer you the resources your people so desperately need… at a price, of course."

I didn't want Dagruel to think I was doing him a freebie, that would make him suspicious as I have no reason to help him out. In fact he likely knows about the alliance between Luminous, Rimuru and I which would make him even more suspicious as Luminous is one of his enemies.

He'd likely think it was a trap of some kind which was only natural. It will definitely take time for him to trust me and my intentions, but that was always something I knew. In the end it was worth it if I could increase the chances that a fragment of the Mad Titan would not become my enemy in the future.

Despite my strength I felt like caution was still one of my strong suits.

"Why would you desire such an arrangement?" Dagruel's voice carried an edge of suspicion, as expected.

I decided to be open with him.

"Despite the alliance between Luminous and I which you may have heard of, I truly mean you no harm. I simply see an opportunity to gain your favor and create a positive impression of myself in your mind. I can take advantage of your circumstances to gain riches while you also benefit and supply your people with much needed supplies."

I had plenty of natural resources that I could trade to Dagruel, the moment I took over this territory I told Arcueid to get on farming and make sure we had an overabundance of food. I didn't need to worry about any extra crops we have rotting since there was Magic to take care of that, having an overabundance of food was far better than not having enough.

I am sure you are aware that one of my primary issues is that traveling through the Desert of Death is a rather perilous journey for most in this world."

"Indeed, I am already prepared for that however. I am a master of Spatial Manipulation, I can occasionally coordinate the exchange between our two territories to begin with. Once more trust has been built up between us then perhaps I can create a Teleportation Circle linking our two territories allowing us to transport the goods to each other directly."

"...Very well. Discounting the absurdity of that statement, if you are prepared to do that much then I can meet you in the middle, at the very least we can begin the starting process of an agreement between our two territories."

"Starting talks between our representatives wouldn't hurt either of us so I am in agreement with you on that front." I stated.

"Very well then, may I learn what exactly you may be interested in from my territory?" Dagruel asked. "The more I know the more willing my representative may be for future deals." He elaborated.

"Very well. To start I was thinking of something along the lines of a trade of food supplies, from my end of course. Your land is known to be horribly infertile, I can provide you with grain, vegetables, even meat."

I'm fairly certain that Dagruel could have made similar deals with other Demon Lords, Leon alone had an entire continent to himself, I'm sure he has abundant resources. However that would involve him asking them for help, putting him in a lesser position to the opposing Demon Lord, something I'm sure he was unwilling to do, despite his care for his people putting himself at the mercy of a potential enemy was foolish.

Most of the Demon Lords were far from allies after all, at least before Rimuru and I popped in. In this scenario I am the one that approached Dagruel, and while he needed me more than I needed him, at the very least we could maintain a semblance of equality between us this way.

Politics.

"I see, and what were you expecting in return?" Dagruel inquired.

"Nothing that'll be too burdensome for you. Dwarven Gold Coins and some of the rare minerals and ores that Damargania is known for."

Thanks to the fight between Guy and Milim, the magicules they released corrupted the Damrada's territory, however it wasn't just the surface world that their magicules reached, their magicules managed to corrupt minerals, dirt, and ore deep within the earth as well.

The magicules of those two can do some rather wondrous things to any kind of material.

The world at large didn't know much about Damargania and what went on there, however Lalatina knew a decent amount about it since in the past she used to mess around close to Dagruel's territory.

"Hoho. Very well then." Dagruel responded.

We coordinated a date, time and place for our representatives to meet before we ended the call.

I sighed as I relaxed into the love seat.

- Othinus -

As Luminous Valentine writhed under her own touch, Othinus felt elation flood through her being. If she had a body, she would have cackled in glee at yet another successful scheme.

Even before her ascension into a Manas, in her previous incarnation as Odin, she had been devising ways to gather more allies for her master.

Her master was strong, stronger than ever before, but Othinus was always careful, she knew very well the dangers of the world they resided in, and so she was constantly devising new methods to bolster his power and ensure his security.

Recreating the Star King Veldanava's memories was her most ambitious strategy, a means to truly elevate her master into an unmatched being. The knowledge and data possessed by the Star King would, in theory, enable her to achieve the unimaginable. But until then, she needed to find other ways to increase her master's strength, even if indirectly.

Gathering allies had been one of Odin's early strategies, though it was not a focus, as few potential allies could offer anything that her master could not already achieve himself. In this world, quality mattered far more than quantity, so neither she nor Odin had prioritized the pursuit of allies. However, when opportunities arose, neither of them would hesitate to exploit them.

Luminous Valentine's attempt to seduce her master had presented such an opportunity. In response, Odin had created the Intrinsic Skill: Lover, specifically designed to ensure Luminous Valentine would become a loyal ally.

Lover subtly influenced Luminous, making her more dependent on her master. Odin had carefully avoided any form of direct control, knowing that it would displease her master. Instead, the skill allowed her master to play Luminous like a finely tuned instrument. Her pleasure points were easily mapped, his scent and fluids became almost addictive to the weak-minded. Of course, Luminous Valentine possessed a will far too strong for any of these factors to affect her individually.

But then there was the Love Energy her master had so recklessly infused into Luminous Valentine, which made her very Spirit crave his touch. Luminous could resist the urge if she wished, but the truth was, she didn't want to. She dove deeper into the intoxicating pool, knowing that one day she might lose the ability to swim back to the surface.

Othinus had ensured that none of it was "mind-rapey," as her master might put it, avoiding anything that would displease him. Luminous could still "break free" if she desired, but Othinus doubted she would. Though there was nothing to truly break free from.

Luminous herself stood to gain much from this arrangement. She would have a powerful ally in her master and would continue to grow stronger through their encounters, thanks to Essence Exchange.

All in all, it was a rather successful scheme in Othinus's eyes. Her master had gained an ally who might one day prove to be useful, and if Luminous didn't then her master still gained a lover that he found explosively attractive, and she existed to fulfill all of his desires.

With that matter settled, Othinus turned her attention to another conundrum she had recently uncovered.

After creating a Soul Corridor between her master and Hinata Sakaguchi, Othinus had noticed something peculiar about the Blessing her master had bestowed upon the girl. It had been subtly tampered with, causing some unknown effect that Othinus had yet to decipher.

The most confusing aspect was that the energy signature of this unknown effect was nearly identical to her master's own, though she was certain he had nothing to do with it.

Othinus resolved to continue investigating the matter and would bring it to her master's attention if it proved significant enough. For now, her master need not be burdened with such concerns.
