Chapter 85: Hot Spring Date

- Arcueid -

"Moss." Arcueid's voice cut through the air, sharp and commanding.

In an instant, her lieutenant materialized before her desk, his appearance was swift as he existed to serve at her whims, as he always did. His presence was tightly wound up upon his tiny body, yet the shadows seemed to cling to his very body.

"Lady Arcueid." He bowed deeply.

She met his gaze, her crimson eyes glinting with an air of authority. "How goes the takeover of the Free Guild?" She inquired.

Moss straightened, his expression unreadable as he answered. "It is proceeding steadily, my Lady. The process is taking time, as expected, but I have already placed one of the Cult of White's more trusted members at the helm. He now serves as the figurehead of the Free Guild, allowing us to tighten our grip on the organization. Currently, I am purging those who stubbornly resist our rule, eliminating the last vestiges of opposition."

She allowed a satisfied smile to curve her lips.

After her Lord has spoken to her about killing the former Guildmaster of the Free Guild, she sensed an opportunity to secure more resources for her Lord to make use of at his leisure in the Western Nations.

Having control over the Free Guild would give her and her Lord a significant amount of soft power over the Western Nations. They now had an army of Adventurers to call upon should she or her Lord desire it.

Of course there were those that opposed her plans, such as the Guildmaster that took over after Yuuki Kagurazaka's death, but he had been… dealt with. She suspected that he was also a mere figurehead for another party.

Her mind raced ahead, planning the next steps. Once those who opposed her in the Free Guild were thoroughly dealt with, her objective would be to intertwine the Free Guild with Azeroth's influence so thoroughly that it would become inseparable from its operations.

The Western Council still retained some influence over the Free Guild due to the economic power they possessed, not to mention the Western Council funded the Free Guild. However she was taking steps to insure she had some hold over the Western Council as well. She had already uncovered the identities of the five elders who ruled the Western Council and had sent her subordinates to gather blackmail on each of them.

Soon she would know where their families lived, where their deepest and darkest secrets were buried.

The Guild's future would be bound to Azeroth's ambitions, ensuring that any attempt to distance themselves from him would be futile.

She knew her Lord did not have many ambitions for this world, he did not wish to conquer it, he merely wished to live his life and enjoy it, there were many in this world that would seek to disturb her Lord's life, having some form of control in the West would be useful to counteract these disturbances.

She had even begun cooperating with her Lord's friend, Lord Rimuru to ensure the success of her plan. He would be having a meeting with the Western Council in some weeks, during that time he would attempt to gather as much information as possible for her to make use of, of course on the condition that he also gained partial control over the Western Council, something she did not reject.

Her Lord and Lord Rimuru were quite close after all, so she did not mind giving him some of the influence she had snatched away from the Humans, she was well aware of his goals to create peace between Non Humans and Humans, he would need all the assistance he could get for such an aspiration.

However, she was well aware that her goals were not something that would be achieved overnight. It would require patience, and planning.

"And the Cult of White?" Her voice broke the silence again. "Any signs of rebellion among them?"

Ordinarily she wouldn't have cared for the members of her cult, she rarely if ever made use of them, however Moss had brought them up seeing as they could prove useful in this endeavor.

Some of them were somewhat useful, the leaders of her cult were of the A Rank, and they had wormed their way into some political influence. In their efforts to please her, their goddess, they had even managed to gain control of a few members of the Council of the West, no one too important, however they had managed to use the influence they had gathered to place one of their members at the helm of the Free Guild, with the other members of the Council of the West clueless.

Each of the Primordials had cults of their own that roamed this world, some choose to make use of them from time to time like she and Misery did, while others merely ignored their existence.

Moss shook his head, his response immediate. "None, my Lady. The Cult of White remains loyal and unwavering."

She nodded, pleased with the report. "Good. Continue to advance this operation steadily. I intend to present the Free Guild to our Lord as a gift, delivered on a silver platter."

Moss's expression hardened with resolve, his loyalty to her and Lord Felix was unshakable. He bowed once more before vanishing as swiftly as he had appeared, leaving her alone with her thoughts.

- Felix -

My thoughts wandered to the data Odin managed to acquire by analyzing Chloe's Chronos.

'Have you managed to learn anything new, Othinus?'

"I am still analyzing the way time flows between multiple worlds. Because time flows differently between different worlds, the duration of the process is taking longer. Even the data from Chronos is not enough as it is composed of data based on the time flow of this world."

'I see.'

I had asked Odin to begin working on a method to go to DxD a while ago, more specifically a way to travel to the past of DxD so I can yoink Ingvild's parents' souls after their demise and bring them to the present. That girl deserved to at least have her parents with her after the shit show she went through.

As things were now, the coordinates I had for DxD were after her parents' deaths to my knowledge. Her father's soul may be out there as he was a Human, however there is a cycle of life in that world, so he may have already reincarnated. As for Ingvild's mother, well Devils don't get an afterlife, their souls are gone once they die. At least that is what is said in the light novel, but realistically that was likely untrue. All souls that did not belong to an afterlife were thrown into the multiversal cycle of reincarnation to reincarnate.

That's what happened to me.

I could still travel to DxD with the coordinates from Ingvild's soul, I would just appear in the moment and place Ingvild herself disappeared.

This would also be in the future of this multiverse since in the present DxD doesn't exist, or Ingvild's world in particular doesn't exist. There may be other DxDs out there for all I know.

The multiverse was always growing and dying at the same time from what I understand. So new worlds being born in the future was believable, Ingvild was proof of that.

I was somewhat hesitant to travel to the future of the multiverse right now as I am, I had explained my reasoning to Ingvild and she was understanding.

Only one copy of a soul could exist at once, so I wasn't sure how my existence in that future would conflict with that of the future Felix's.

I needed to be stronger, stronger than I am now, and have a greater understanding about the rules Veldanava has set on his creation, I was still forced to abide by those rules after all, the Voice of the World was far greater than I was, and I had a feeling it wouldn't hesitate to enforce them on me if I did something I really shouldn't be.

All in all, there were simply too many unseen risks at this point when it came to traveling to DxD due to it only existing in the future.

However I still wanted Othinus to come up with a way to do it theoretically for when I was willing to make that jump.

I was hoping the data on Chronos may be enough for Othinus to have a breakthrough in that direction, but time travel is harder than it sounds.

Time was closely intertwined with Space, however it was still a very complex element to understand, even with my power and understanding over Time having been strengthened many folds, I still had much I did not comprehend.

"I currently need more data on the way time flows between different worlds so I can decipher the coordinates of the past of the world you wish to travel to."

More data huh.

I planned to go to another world after this whole Granbell fiasco is dealt with, I don't like leaving things half done so I've been waiting until after Granbell is dealt with to travel to another world.

'If I sync the time flow between the world I want to go to and this world would that give you the opportunity to gather more data on time flow?'

Planeswalker at the Ultimate level was truly an incredible ability. It didn't have much combat power directly, but it allowed me to venture to other dimensions which had their own Space-Time, I could even sync those Space-Times with the Cardinal World's Space Time due to the way my Skill functioned, though I usually didn't do that. And that was mostly due to an inbuilt feature of the Skill that sort of got the Voice of the World to do it for me, so it wouldn't be by my own power.

"I cannot give you an absolute answer, I do believe it would give me more valuable data but I could not tell you for sure until later on. Another solution is further recreating Veldanava's memories."

So more data on Veldanava would also work, of course I don't really have a good source of data on that guy at this point.

'Got it, then I'll sync the times up between this world and the one I want to go to.'

Anything for more data!

That's another reason to wait until everything is somewhat sorted out in this world, so I can have some time without any annoying events happening while I'm in another world.

Man why did DxD have to be such a complicated universe, it just had to be the land of tits.

Though Ingvild being summoned from the future is a miracle on its own, just sheer dumb luck. I'm guessing a Space-Time incursion happened at some point, which the summoning ritual sort of latched onto allowed the ritual to pull from the future.

Basically time bullshit.

I can think of many abilities from that universe that would be useful to have data on, but I need to wait until Othinus has more data on the way time flows, and on the rules Veldanava set. I seriously don't want the Voice of the World to go batshit and try to erase me like it tried to erase Chloe.

I sighed. At least the next world I planned to visit was a fun one.

I suppose I should tell Arcueid about my talk with Dagruel now.

It was always rather amusing to consider that the being in front of me was one from most beings' nightmares, yet in front of me she just seemed like a normal woman rather than the Primordial entity she was.

Divine Artifacts designed to sustain the world made a lot of sense in hindsight. This world would have crumbled long ago if not for some form of support. I had always assumed Veldanava made the world extraordinarily durable, but it seemed there was more to it.

The Divine Tree was responsible for regulating the magicules in the atmosphere as well as the magicules that were naturally released by beings such as myself.

"Now that I have begun truly focusing on the world itself, I can detect its subtle influence."

'Oh? How so?'

"Whenever you rip Space apart, the world quickly gets to work on mending it, which was something we both always knew, now that I am actively looking for something I can detect the presence of the world when it begins mending Space."

Huh, well that's something.

There was something I was wondering though.

From what I understand the world is an emotionless being that acts merely to secure its own survival, nothing more, nothing less. As long as you do not actively harm the world I do not believe it will bother you."

"Incomprehensibly. The amount of energy flowing through the world is immense. In terms of EP, perhaps billions or even trillions."

Well damn.

The world just casually made something that strong. Don't fuck with the world unless I have to, got it.

That timing would be just after Rimuru's meeting with the Western Council.

- Hinata Sakaguchi -

Her lips twitched as she took in the sight of Felix's Oni. Saeko had appeared out of nowhere, she had sensed the shifting of Space, but she couldn't prevent the teleportation with her own Space-Time Manipulation, but that was only natural since Felix's capabilities in that department dwarfed her own.

Saeko planted her hands on her hips, her gaze unwavering. "As expected of Felix-sama's student, you are strong." Saeko remarked with a nod.

Hinata suppressed a sigh, recalling the events leading up to this moment. She had been in the midst of training the Great Saints, focusing on giving them an auditory lesson on the various aspects of Fighting Spirit, and then Saeko had appeared without warning. The nine members of the Saints had immediately sprung into action, launching a coordinated attack on the perceived threat, already making use of the tips she had provided them.

Hinata couldn't blame them, Saeko had torn through the protective barriers she'd erected around the training grounds as though they were nothing which did make it seem as if a hostile was invading.

Yet, their efforts had been in vain against Saeko. She had dismantled their attacks with ease, even Saare, who was one of the stronger among them, had found himself helpless against her.

Saeko hadn't even made use of a Skill to accomplish this either, through sheer Battlewill Saeko beat down the so-called strongest in the West, which only went to show how foolish they were in the past, her included, for thinking themselves equal to some members of the Demon Lords Council.

They weren't even strong enough to take on a True Demon Lord's Lieutenant, though Felix's subordinates were far from the norm. Luminous herself had admitted that Felix's repertoire of subordinates was monstrous, he had multiple Demon Lord class subordinates, and even Primordials who scaled even higher due to their knowledge and experiences.

Ignorance could truly be bliss.

Of course, they had already been worn down by their earlier sparring session with her, but the outcome would likely have been the same even if they had been at full strength.

She sighed softly, addressing Saeko, "What are you doing here?"

She had been introduced to Saeko back during the Tempest Founding Festival. Back then she thought of Saeko as a powerful foe due to her power.

Saeko was suppressing the majority of her power, however her instincts warned her that Saeko was strong.

She was one of the most powerful figures in the Western Nations back then, Felix truly had impressive subordinates, for one of them to possibly be capable of matching her back then.

All of Felix's direct subordinates were around the Saint level or close to it from what she understood, while some others were even beyond the level of a normal Saint, though Saints were not normal by any definition of the word in the first place which went to show how strong some of Felix's subordinates were.

Enlightened likely made up 0.0001% of the population, while Saints were even more rare.

Thankfully with her evolution she had grown far more powerful than Saeko, her energy reserves had practically tripled from their previous state, not to mention her increased understanding of the world and the potency of her power.

Though she wouldn't be arrogant, she did not know what abilities Saeko may possess, underestimating her opponent could prove fatal.

"Felix-sama transported me here as Luminous had requested my presence." Saeko replied casually as she took in the sight of her downed foes.

Hinata's eyes narrowed slightly, her gaze shifting to Garde, who was sprawled on the ground, panting from exertion. Among the Ten Great Saints, he was the only one unaware of the true nature of the goddess they worshiped, a Demon Lord, one of the enemies of Humanity.

Though she doubted Saeko cared much for that secret, Saeko always struck Hinata as the type to act before thinking.

With a swift gesture, Hinata snapped her fingers, erecting a barrier around the two of them. "I see. I don't know why Felix sent you to me then."

Saeko shrugged. "I know not how Felix-sama makes his decisions, only that they are the correct ones." She said with a smug smile.

Hinata sighed. "I see."

Hinata nodded, her mind racing. An idea sparked. "While you wait, do you mind helping me train my subordinates?" She gestured toward the battered Saints, their breaths still ragged from their streak of recent defeats. First against her, and now against Saeko, she was sure the egos of all nine of them had taken a beating today.

Saeko glanced at the group before nodding. "Very well! I've been training my own subordinates, perhaps I can assist you." She puffed out her chest proudly, her enthusiasm almost childlike in its earnestness.

Hinata's eyes briefly flicked to Saeko's chest, an involuntary comparison to her own crossing her mind. She quickly shook her head, banishing the thought, and refocused. "Thank you, Saeko." She said genuinely.

With a wave of her hand, Hinata dispelled the barrier and addressed the Saints. "This is Saeko, one of Felix's strongest subordinates."

Saeko beamed at the introduction, clearly prideful at her earned power

"She will be your sparring partner for today."

She was originally planning to focus on lessons for today rather than actual combat practice. The eight were rather worn out and hadn't recovered a significant amount of their strength from their earlier spar. However there would not be many opportunities for them to face someone of Saeko's caliber, one that was a Majin and had a differing combat style to her own, she could teach them what she wanted another day, now she would take advantage of Saeko's appearance.

Saare groaned. "Ugh, I'm already running on fumes here…."

Saeko merely reached to the side, she seemed to be reaching into her Spatial Storage.

Saeko extracted multiple potions from her Spatial Storage and threw them to everyone who needed one.

Everyone immediately began drinking their respective potions, healing all their wounds and regenerating most of their magicules.

Her own eyes widened as she realized just what those potions were. "Full Potions?!"

The gazes of everyone snapped to Saeko as they realized just how valuable the potion they all so carelessly consumed was.

"Th-That was a Full Potion!" Leonard exclaimed, his voice trembling slightly. A single Full Potion could be diluted by one hundred times and would still be a potent elixir.

Saeko nodded, still beaming with pride. "Felix-sama provided me with plenty in case I needed them."

Hinata sighed. "I suppose that is expected of him."

She had known Tempest had figured out a way to mass produce the mythical Full Potion, but she didn't have access to many of them herself.

"I see, thank you then Saeko."

"It's no problem! I've always wanted to test myself against the Western Nations' so-called greatest warriors!" Saeko's eyes sparkled with excitement.

Hinata winced, she had a feeling Saeko would be disappointed. The myths behind the Ten Great Saints, now Nine Great Saints, had been rather exaggerated.

Garde smirked at Saeko, his arrogance still intact somehow despite his earlier streak of defeats. "Heh, I suppose even a Demon Lord's subordinate knows her place. I suppose I can take you on now that I am at full power."

Hinata held back a groan. She would need to discipline Garde later, his idiocy was going to get him killed one day.

Saeko's eyes narrowed dangerously as she began cracking her knuckles. "It seems you want a beating."

Before Garde could respond, Hinata stepped in. "All of you will be going at her at once." She announced.

Arnaud's gaze snapped to her. "Wh-What?! Is she just like you?!"

Hinata shrugged her shoulders, choosing not to directly answer. "She is the direct subordinate of a Demon Lord, it's about time you all realized how hopelessly outmatched you are against a True Demon Lord, understanding the strength of merely one of their subordinates will allow you to see a glimpse of the true power some of them possess."

The weakest True Demon Lord she knew of was Luminous herself who was in reality not weak at all. The current Demon Lord lineup was just filled with monsters.

Though perhaps Dino was weaker, she had not met the man so she did not have a good read on his power, and she did not count Ramiris to be part of their ilk.

Hinata felt like she could take Luminous on now with her ascension, but that did not mean that she could not pay respect to her friend's power.

In the end at this point she refused to accept Luminous' dominance over her, on her journey with Chloe one thing she had learned was that as a Spiritual Lifeform, half the fight was a mental one.

If a Spiritual Lifeform felt like they were inferior to their opponents they had already lost the fight due to the nature of Spiritual Lifeforms, with the Spirit influencing the flesh.

Hinata knew that was an issue she would have when facing Felix in the future. Felix had almost mythologized himself in her eyes, he always seemed to have some way out of any situation he was in, and he had power in spades.

If she ever wished to become his equal she would need to acknowledge herself as equal to Felix with a solid chance at beating him in combat, or else she would never stand a chance in the first place.

She focused back on her subordinates who were all reluctantly nodding. Even Saare, who had initially resisted, had grown to trust her judgment after their earlier sparring session. Only Garde seemed hesitant, a frown creasing his features. "Fine, we'll show this ogre her place together." He said as his blade lit up in flames.

Saeko ignored his taunt, instead reaching for the weapon strapped to her back. As she drew the blade from its sheath, Hinata's eyes were drawn to the weapon's ominous Aura. It was powerful, a Legend Grade weapon, if on the middle end of the scale.

The air around them seemed to tremble as the blade was fully revealed, its Aura no longer suppressed by the sheath. Saeko hefted it onto her shoulder, a smirk tugging at her lips. "Behold! Hercules Edge, one of Felix-sama's gifts to me!"

Hinata stepped to the side, raising multiple barriers around the training grounds.

"I will be serving as the referee. If the battle goes too far, I will step in." She stated firmly.

Both parties nodded. Hinata bent down and picked up a small rock from the ground. "Once this lands, you may begin."

She carelessly tossed the rock into the air, watching as it ascended before plummeting back down. The moment it touched the ground, the atmosphere around them shifted violently.

Hinata's senses flared as an oppressive pressure filled the air, a wave of malice that radiated from Saeko like a storm. The very ground beneath their feet cracked under the force of it, sending tremors through the earth.

She quickly realized what was happening. Saeko was utilizing a form of Haki, one she hadn't encountered before. The air was thick with the weight of it, as though the very world itself was recoiling in fear.

Hinata felt the pressure brush against her own Aura, attempting to force her to falter, but she countered with a surge of her Holy Haki, dispelling the effect with ease. Her eyes scanned the battlefield, assessing the state of the Saints.

She spotted Garde, who had been the most vocal, he seemed to have trouble breathing as his face pale in the face of Saeko's pressure. His confidence evaporated in an instant as he felt the cold grip of fear enveloping him. Saeko's Haki seemed to be meant to inspire fear in her foes over anything else.

Garde's hand was trembling as he gripped the hilt of his sword, his knuckles turning white, eyes wide with a terror he couldn't suppress.

The others were no better; they stood frozen, their wills crushed under the weight of Saeko's malevolent aura.

Hinata knew they were in for a brutal fight, but it was for their own good. Perhaps Garde may even grow as a person from this fight. He would achieve character development as Felix liked to say.

- Felix -

I stripped myself of my clothing as I took in the pleasant heat of the hotspring. The hotspring was fairly large, there were in fact multiple hotsprings present in my palace, this one is my personal one.

It's still fairly large, easily large enough to fit up to 10 people, but it isn't as large as the other ones.

I took in the pleasant scent of the hotspring, steam was wafting off the water.

The water came from an artificial waterfall I had created a while back, connected through spatial tunneling allowing a steady stream of fresh water even through a long distance, it was drained through the very same way to keep the water truly fresh. The water was instantly heated up to temperature with Magic as well, this hotspring was definitely built to be fancy.

There was even a wine cabinet in the corner. Arcueid went all out on the design of this place.

I let out a sigh as the hot water enveloped my form from the chest down. I placed my arms on the marble tiled floor as I let my head sink backwards. I closed my eyes and relaxed as I waited for Arcueid's arrival.

It didn't take long for me to hear the door opening, I opened one of my eyes and spotted Arcueid saunturing towards me. She was holding a plate filled with various fruits.

She was dressed in merely a white bathrobe which was left open allowing me to see a generous amount of side boob.

She picked up two glasses and a bottle of wine before she set them as well as the plate of fruits on the floor beside my head.

"Thanks."

Arcueid merely smiled. "It is no problem." Without any more prompting Arcueid kneeled behind my head causing me to stare at her in confusion. I was no longer confused once Arcueid gently lifted my head and placed it on her soft thighs, the only thing separating me from her skin directly was the very thin bathrobe, which didn't take away from my enjoyment of the sensation.

UUOOOOOOHHH, a lap pillow! I most definitely would not say no to being spoiled, especially by someone like Arcueid!

Ah, I have turned into a degenerate haven't I? Oh well, I'm a Demon Lord, I can be as lascivious as I want! At least I don't like kids like Leon does!

Arcueid seemingly sensed my delight as she warmly smiled at me. I had a perfect view of Arcueid's cleavage from her lap due to the way she wore her bathrobe, but I didn't focus on that, I merely enjoyed the sensation of Arcueid's pampering.

Arcueid reached to the side, picking up some of the fruits on it, once her hand was closer the fruit she chose revealed itself to be grapes.

She gently lowered them into my open mouth so I could eat them.

I quickly chewed on the crisp grapes, relishing in the taste. Magic could do a lot to further enhance some of the most basic foods. I will never have to eat a soggy grape every again, only the crispest!

As Arcueid fed me grapes I spoke up. "There is something I'm curious about, before you were ever summoned to this world, what did you used to do in the Daemon Realm for so long?"

Arcueid had been in the Daemon Realm for eons, I have no idea what she did to occupy that much time. Now was a good time to ask.

As I chewed on an orange slice, Arcueid answered. "I was the second oldest of all of my kin, Guy being the only one older than I am."

I nodded, that was something I already knew. Guy was the oldest and the strongest, then came Arcueid, after Arcueid Diablo was born, then Misery was born, after her came Megumin, then Lalatina, and then the youngest is Rain, which makes sense since she acts like a bratty, lazy younger sister.

"Once I was born a battle for supremacy immediately began in the Daemon Realm between Guy and I. He was more skilled than me at the time due to his greater age and experience, however he failed to put me down for good, and so we would continue to fight for quite some time until Diablo was born.

Guy lost interest in continuing his battles with me and moved on to fighting Diablo, while I found rivals of my own."

It was incredibly impressive that she managed to hold Guy off as practically a newborn. My Arcueid really was quite special.

"Megumin and Lalatina." I stated.

Arcueid nodded as she placed another grape in my mouth.

"The three of us would compete on anything that caught one of our attention, we were fairly bored so we did much. I of course also focused on building up my own court, gathering powerful subordinates as well." Arcueid said. "In the end we merely played around with each other until you summoned us My Lord." Arcueid finished.

"That sounds like a fun life, having fun with your friends for eons."

Arcueid clicked her tongue but reluctantly nodded. "I suppose they can be considered my closest friends."
By now the plate of fruit was finished. "Did you wish for more My Lord?"

I shook my head. "No I'm fine, why don't you join me now?"

"If that is what you wish." Arcueid happily replied as she set the plate aside.

I raised my head off her lap, though I noticed Arcueid pouting slightly. It seems she enjoyed being in the role of a caretaker, a mommy through and through.

Arcueid gently stepped into the water, her bathrobe still on. Arcueid sat down next to me. "This is quite nice."

I nodded. "It is."
Arcueid gently scooched closer to me, I wasn't going to say no to a bit of skinship, and it wasn't like I hadn't already seen what was under that robe of hers.

"What have you been doing recently My Lord?" Arcueid asked as she poured us both a glass of wine.

I took the glass from her hand before answering. "Hmm, well you already know about the Chronoa situation."

Arcueid nodded. A little while back I had another little group meeting where I told everyone who mattered to me about my plans for the future. This involved explaining Chronoa, Chloe, and Hinata's situation as well so thanks to that all my direct subordinates are aware of that entire mess.

The reactions were mixed, but in the end not many seemed to care that their alternates were erased from existence, they saw things differently I supposed.

"After dealing with the initial fallout of that mess, I had sparred with Hinata, she actually ended up evolving." I said before I took a sip of my wine. I had lowered my Poison Nullification so that I could get a bit of a buzz.

The wine was made from some berries that have been grown in a field of extremely highly concentrated magicules, my own magicules. Thanks to that it could even affect me if I allowed it to.

I let out a sigh of pleasure as a very subtle warmth spread through me.

Arcueid raised a brow. "Oh? Did the Human finally become a Complete Saint?"

Right, Arcueid doesn't know that right after I healed and upgraded Hinata's body she managed to reach Complete Sainthood.
I shook my head. "No, she went beyond that."

Arcueid's eyes narrowed. "She achieved Divinity then?"

I nodded. "She did, she even got an Ultimate Skill."

Arcueid's lips twitched. "I see, it seems she has become rather powerful then."

I nodded. "Yeah, she's pretty strong now."

She isn't a match for any of the current Demon Lords except Ramiris if she counts, though perhaps she can give Luminous a decent fight, but that doesn't mean Hinata is weak, the current line up of Demon Lords are just absurdly strong. I can't say how well she'd do against Dino since I only know that he hides his true power, but he was a Primordial Angel, I'm betting he's pretty strong.

Arcueid swirled her glass. "Perhaps I need to put more effort in regaining my former power."

Ah, that's right. The Primordials are basically degraded when they incarnate in the Cardinal World. In the Daemon Realm they reign as supreme Devil Lords, born from the Great Spirit of Darkness.

However when summoned they are degraded to mere Arch Daemons. Arch Daemons that can mop the floor with any other Arch Daemon, and perhaps even most Daemon Dukes, but Arch Daemons nonetheless.

The world really does not like Daemons.

"I do have a plan regarding that." I mentioned.

Arcuied looked at me with interest. "Oh?"

"I came up with a way to give you enough energy to push for an evolution, though this comes with risks of course."

"How does this method of yours work My Lord?" Arcueid asked, not doubting my words.

"Basically I use a bunch of souls and convert them all into energy, similar to the process of a Harvest Festival, and then I shove all that energy into your body. At that point it is up to you to control all that energy and use it to basically push yourself further. The soul energy will nourish your soul, your body, and your spirit."

Arcuied nodded with interest. "I see. I do not believe I will have an issue with such a method."

"I don't think you will either, I don't have the souls needed for this just yet though."

I need to visit Guy to see if I can get some souls for him. I don't want to use the favor he owes me for this, but if I can't think of some other way to get him to give me some souls then I may just have to. I wasn't going to just slaughter a country after all, even in another world.

Arcueid knew very well about the threats that were coming our way. The Eastern Empire which had a True Dragon, potentially Dagruel who was also a beast. The biggest threat was the Eastern Empire since I didn't know all that much about them.

I had Lalatina send some of her Daemon spies over but none of them have managed to gain any useful information, the Eastern Empire keeps its secrets well guarded.

I barely even knew about the military power they possessed, there were some things that Chloe and Chronoa knew of like tanks, and airships, but that didn't tell me much about the overall strength of the Eastern Empire's military.

"Just think of it as a gift from me."

Arcueid nodded.

Arcueid was especially interested in Hinata's growth, I think she was being competitive, she does still have her pride as a Primordial Daemon, I'm sure she doesn't like that Hinata has surpassed her in power.

"It seems you have been enjoying yourself then My Lord." Arcueid said.

"If you ever hear me say no to that you're with an imposter." I answered.

"Fufu~" Arcueid laughed as her hand snaked around my shaft.

Chapter 86: Interlude - Eastern Empire

- Kagali -

As Kagali surveyed the monsters that Misha had tamed, a smile crept up on her face. They were in one of their many bases scattered throughout the Western Nations, protected by powerful barriers that masked their location from any prying eyes.

In front of her, beasts of all kinds prowled in their cages.

Lesser and Medium Dragons snarled and snapped at the air, their fiery eyes glowing in the dim light. Horn Bears stamped their massive paws, their sharp tusks glinting menacingly. Chimeras, with their three heads, paced back and forth, while Grave Lizards and Poison Lizards hissed and flicked their forked tongues, the air around them thick with the scent of their venom.

Misha had used a combination of powerful drugs, relentless conditioning and Magic to bring these beasts to heel, forging a force that Kagali herself would have been hesitant to face in her prime.

The sheer might of this force was staggering, even the most seasoned warriors would think twice before challenging them. Kagali marveled at the thought that these creatures would soon be unleashed on Ruberious, that too only to serve as distractions.

She turned to her side, her gaze falling on Tear, who stood beside her with a mischievous grin. "This is quite something, is it not, Tear?"

Tear giggled, her voice bubbling with excitement. "Hehe~ yup! Those mean Demon Lords are not gonna have fun!"

Kagali nodded. "Come, let us check on the other experiments."

This particular facility was one of Yuuki's prized assets, where his various experiments were conducted in utmost secrecy.

Vega, the brute, had been subjected to countless tests and experiments here, though he remained unaware of the location of this facility due to Yuuki's tampering.

Vega was not aware of many things when it came to Cerberus, this facility was one such thing. Vega was always an unpredictable ally due to his nature, so Yuuki was very careful with the information he shared with Vega.

Her brow creased as she thought back to the mysterious circumstances around Vega's death.

No one spotted the killer, the crowd was thoroughly questioned, yet not a single person knew what had happened.

Kagali's leading theory was that Vega got on the bad side of someone and they took offense, but without more information Kagali could not say much. She could only hope that whoever was behind Vega's demise would not get in the way of their plan.

Damrada himself had said not to worry about the person behind Vega's death, only that it may have been an old friend who he had not seen in a long time. And that the killer likely would not take further action.

Kagali knew she was getting increasingly desperate, she lacked too much information and so she had to compromise, taking Damrada's word was one such compromise as she did not wish to alienate him now. He still commanded significant resources within Cerberus that she was incapable of taking away due to his influence.

Kagali sighed at her current circumstances.

"Something the matter, President?" Tear asked, her tone light but laced with genuine concern.

Kagali shook her head. "Nothing you can help with."

Tear shrugged her shoulders. "I'm here if ya need me!"

Kagali felt her lips curl up at Tear's support. Tear was the only one of her friends she had, Laplace may or may not be alive and it was tearing at her.

When did everything go so wrong?

She shook her head, there was no purpose in dwelling on those thoughts any longer.

As they continued their inspection, they were suddenly interrupted. "Miss Kagali!" A man hurried toward them, panting heavily from exertion. He was one of the many nameless subordinates that served Cerberus.

Kagali raised an eyebrow, her voice cool and commanding. "What is it?"
The man struggled to catch his breath before delivering his message. "W-We have received word from some of our spies… information about Demon Lord Felix White."

Her eyes narrowed. "What information?"

The man straightened, his composure slowly returning. "Our spy reported that The Dungeon was temporarily evacuated recently due to a fight that took place on the lower floors."

Kagali waited, her patience wearing thin. "And?"

The man gulped, clearly nervous about what he was about to say. "The fight… it was between the Storm Dragon and Felix White. According to our spy, the result was… a draw."

Kagali's breath caught in her throat. "What?!" She whispered, her disbelief mirrored in Tear's wide eyes.

She knew that Felix White was powerful, stronger than her in her prime. He had managed to defeat Footman and make Tear run for the hills after all. But to challenge a True Dragon? That was unheard of… the only ones she could think of that were capable of such a thing were the first Demon Lord, Guy Crimson, and Milim Nava, The Destroyer.

"Was there any more information?" She asked.

The man quickly shook his head.

"Leave us then."

The man bowed and practically sprinted away.

"This may complicate things." She mumbled.

"Will it really?" Tear asked, her tone uncharacteristically serious. "We were never planning to challenge the Demon Lord directly. That's what the Masked Hero is for, right? And she actually managed to defeat Veldora and seal him away. Not to mention Veldora should still be weakened after being unsealed so recently."

Kagali nodded slowly, considering Tear's words. "You're right. The plan remains unchanged."

Their strategy had always been to discreetly gain control of the Masked Hero while Granbell created a diversion. They had no intention of confronting Felix White or Rimuru Tempest head-on. Granbell would deal with the goddess Luminous, ensuring that the major players were occupied while they carried out their true objectives.

In the end it didn't matter that Felix White had managed to fight Veldora, even a weakened Veldora was a threat to take seriously. Chronoa had managed to seal a full power Veldora, something far more impressive.

Not to mention the spy's information could be wrong, it could be information deliberately spread to make Felix White look more powerful in the eyes of the public. The Daemon seemed to have an inflated ego, it would make sense that he wished to spread his "legend" and gain the worship and fear of the people.

"If that guy really got that strong in such a short period of time, then he'd be a real monster." Tear mumbled, her playful demeanor giving way to genuine concern.

"Indeed he would. He is not even one of those ancient Primordials yet he has already grown so powerful."

Even she would be nervous against a Primordial in her prime, even without a vessel, such was the might those ancient Daemons commanded.

"If he truly had managed to fight even a weakened Veldora to a draw then few can hope to match him." Kagali said.

She sighed. "Come, there is no use further thinking about this, the plan remains unchanged."

Granbell had already made his arrangements, the Guardian of the West was also prepared to offer his help.

While Rimuru Tempest was busy with his Council meeting, they would attack. Granbell still maintained some control over the Five Elders of the Council of the West, so he had arranged for the meeting to be attacked as well, partially to further distract Rimuru Tempest from their true targets. Felix White should not be within the bounds of Ruberious, teleportation from his territory all the way to Ruberious was unheard of, and so he would be helpless to help his ally.

The ones attacking the Council meeting would be Yuuki's Magic Inquisitor experiments, each of them were powerful, when they are all together even in her prime she would need to be very careful in a fight against them.

Kagali and Tear walked into the room where the Magic Inquisitors were being stored.

The room was dimly lit, with six large tanks lined up against the wall, each filled with a sedative that kept the Inquisitors in a state of unconsciousness. Each was carefully bound with a mental domination spell allowing her to control them.

Ordinarily she wouldn't have been able to exert enough power to control such powerful beings in her weak vessel, however she managed to bind the six before they became vessels to the power they now held.

Yuuki had not wished to hold their leash as he would not be available most times, however she would be available, and so she became the jailor of the Magic Inquisitors.

She carefully ran a hand along the glass of one of the tanks as her lips curled upwards. "Yes, they will do very nicely."

Even a Demon Lord like Rimuru Tempest would struggle against six Magic Inquisitors of this strength, she would have likely been defeated by such a number.

Magic Inquisitors were originally an experiment of the Kingdom of Ingrassia meant to give Humans access to magicules of their own, rather than merely making use of what was in the atmosphere.

Humans would absorb the Monster Factor of various Monsters and become strengthened due to the Factor inside of them. Their bodies would generally become ten times stronger with skin tougher than steel. Of course there were physical and mental strains when taking in the Factor of something distinctly Non Human.

Many became more beast than man, giving in to the foreign instincts that flooded their minds, only those of supreme willpower could truly take control of the power they were granted.

Due to this Ingrassia set their sights on incorporating more spiritual aspects into their Inquisitors. They never got far in this direction as the scientists involved in the experiment failed to understand how Daemons truly incarnated in this world, thus they continued to fail.

Yuuki never had that issue, and so the experiments moved forward under his direction.

Now, in front of her lay six Magic Inquisitors that had once been Human. Now, however, they were distinctly more. They had taken in the Factors of more demonic aligned Monsters and then been used as vessels for Daemons.

It had taken much experimenting to find Daemons compatible with the bodies, however they eventually succeeded and incarnated the Daemons inside the vessels.

All of these Daemons were merely Lesser Daemons or Greater Daemons. Due to this, they had practically zero ego, allowing the Human ego within the body to come out on top in the ego battle, giving the Magic Inquisitors the powers of the Daemons, but with a physical body to exert the entirety of that might.

In the case of the Greater Daemons, she had personally dominated them with a Domination Orb that Laplace had powered, giving her control over the Greater Daemons. She then forcefully suppressed their egos.

Lesser Daemons were weak. However, due to their incarnation, multiple evolved into Greater Daemons. In the case of the Greater Daemons that were summoned, they grew more powerful. A single one of them had even evolved into an Arch Daemon.

Each Magic Inquisitor was, at the minimum, a Special-A Rank. These six had gone even further beyond that level due to Yuuki's experiments.

Now, each was a bonafide Disaster Class being, and she retained control over each one of them. She could never allow the seals placed on them to break for fear of them seeking revenge. She was far too weak to take even a single one of them on at this point, and Tear would struggle against more than two of them at once.

During these moments, she missed Laplace. His overwhelming strength was always a comfort.

"The Boss really did something crazy here, huh?" Tear chippered excitedly.

Kagali nodded. No normal man would experiment on others like Yuuki had, but the results showed. The ends did justify the means in this case.

Even with Vega's loss they still remained powerful thanks to the foundation Yuuki had built up.

She felt a vicious smirk form on her face as she thought of Felix White's fate. Once she had the Masked Hero in her possession, the countdown for the Usurper of Black's death would begin. Her Domination Orb would be more than enough to enslave the comatose Heroine, even Milim Nava had been dominated by it, and had only been freed due to Clayman's own demise she suspected.

"Soon Tear… soon."

Tear nodded. "We'll avenge the Boss, don't ya worry!"

She clenched her fists and nodded.

- Tatsuya Kondou -

Under Emperor Rudra's orders, he traveled to Jistav and placed both Clayman and Eva under his control long ago. The Emperor wished to weaken the Great Jura Forest, and Clayman was a sufficient enough resource to accomplish that goal.

The entire attack on Tempest happened due to Kondou nudging Clayman in that direction, and it was why Clayman was getting more and more reckless as time went on. Clayman was already a man that sought power more than anything else, however he was wise enough not to be reckless about it before.

Of course, that situation did not go the way he wished it to. Instead, it led to the birth of two new Demon Lords, so he cut his losses and acquired Eva.

Eva was powerful in her own right. She was strong enough to be a powerful Imperial Guardian, and her technique was excellent. She would prove to be a useful asset to him and Emperor Rudra.

"It seems that they are recovering from the attack well enough." He mumbled to himself.

He was Tatsuya Kondou, a former lieutenant in the Imperial Japanese Navy, and now the Commander of the Imperial Guardians. He had many duties placed on his shoulders. His primary goal was to gather information on anything and everything so that the Emperor knew all about the state of the world.

He was not someone from this world, originally, he had been a humble pilot of the Great Japan Conquering Empire back in his original world. The history of his original world was rich, from stories about the ancient Bandit King who founded the first Empire, to the legendary figures of history that changed the world around them after the Bandit King.

He had delivered important information to his superior before embarking on a suicide mission to buy time for his comrades to escape, more specifically, a kamikaze attack, before he could perish though he fell through a crack in Space and Time.

He appeared in the Eastern Empire decades ago, specifically, he appeared in the Emperor's garden while the Emperor was there.

He then established an intelligence network to gather more information for his Emperor, and he has been doing so to this very day. Now, he had a comprehensive network of spies that extended even into the Western Nations.

Yuuki Kagurazaka's death did not come as a surprise. Kondou knew that he had been buttering up to the Rosso and making use of their influence to conduct illegal otherworlder summonings. Many of the otherworlders in the Empire were products of Yuuki's summonings.

Kondou guessed that Yuuki had sent the otherworders to build a life in the Eastern Empire so he could make use of them later down the line. Many of the otherworlders in the Composite Division, also known as the Mixed Corps, felt indebted to Yuuki after all.

Kondou tapped his finger on the desk as he considered the reasons why Yuuki may have been killed alongside Granbell's granddaughter.

The Armored Division specializes in making use of otherworlder technology. Seven hundred thousand soldiers had even undergone experiments to further strengthen themselves, allowing them to go up to a week without food or water.

Utilizing DNA analysis derived from otherworlder technology, the Empire had succeeded in nurturing and raising Magic Beasts known as Battle Chimeras, powerful creatures with immense destructive potential.

These beasts were not merely wild monsters but were engineered for war, each a product of meticulous genetic crafting. Their riders, chosen from a select pool of warriors, had powers awakened within them that were once the domain of ancient champions. The very DNA of champions from ages long gone had been imbued into these beasts.

This awakening was not left to chance. It was a calculated process, the result of rigorous experimentation and manipulation of genetic material.

The division was filled with lab-grown soldiers created by the fusion of Magic and knowledge from another world. Each beast knight, paired with their battle chimera, was a force to be reckoned with, with their combined strength often surpassing standard measurements. Despite the division's relatively small size of 30,000 members, it was one of the most elite and deadly forces in the Empire.

The Magic Beasts, combined with their riders, made for formidable foes. In dire circumstances, the riders could even fuse with their Magic Beasts. However, only approximately 1% would survive this process properly.

The rest would all be various levels of failures.

The leader of this division was also fairly powerful. He had to be for his place in the Imperial Guardians. He was the brother of the former Demon Lord Carrion, and was rather eager for revenge, which the Empire had used to gain his loyalty.

Eva went on to talk about the division he was most interested in. "A hierarchy is slowly being developed in the Composite Division."

The Composite Division was Emperor Rudra's personal experiment. He placed many powerful otherworlders and similarly powerful figures in one division with no clear hierarchy and let them go wild.

If Mai's abilities were insufficient, then the Scorch Dragon Velgrynd would assist.

Demon Lord Felix had powerful subordinates and a powerful military, which was why he was selected as the target of invasion for the Composite Division. The Emperor felt that he could give the surviving members of the Composite Division the push to awaken.

Once the first wave was done, the true fight would start. There was a chance of Demon Lord Felix underestimating their forces due to the strength of the Composite Division which would be a plus as the Demon Lord would least expect their true attack.

The initial attack on Veldora centuries ago was a plan of the Emperor to awaken more Saints. In fact, why else would the Emperor order a mortal army to take down a True Dragon?

Veldora may be the weakest but a True Dragon was a True Dragon. Sadly, almost the entire force sent to Veldora was wiped out, resulting in only losses for the Eastern Empire, not a single Awakening.

They were able to recuperate their numbers fairly easily due to the large population of otherworlders.

While one was more preferable than the other, otherworlders leaving offspring was still a boon, as those offspring would be more powerful than the norm. Born as Demi-Material Lifeforms, capable of holding an internal energy capacity similar to otherworlders if weaker, unlike the Humans of this world who were forced to use the magicules in the atmosphere.

Most chose to join the military once they found out that despite their power, they were nothing when compared to the stronger members of the Imperial Guardians.

Every single being wanted to feel powerful, to have some form of security in their lives. For the otherworlders who had been ripped from their homes, they needed more power to feel safe, and so they would join the military, it was only natural.

Many Imperial Guardians were otherworlders who had trained rigorously to get to their place. They were those who believed that power was everything in this world. Nationality and morals did not matter to them as long as they were strong.

Once they joined the Imperial Guardians, they would be gifted with status and power, and each member would be rewarded with Legendary Equipment, as well as a ranking equivalent to that of a senior officer.

To climb the ranks, an Imperial Guardian could challenge a higher number. If they defeated them, then they would rise to the position of the one they defeated. If they lost, however, the one who was challenged could kill the challenger.

There was a reason why the Imperial Guardians were considered the most powerful force in the Eastern Empire, they were each in constant competition with one another.

The Marshall was the only position greater than that of the Imperial Guardians. It was a sole position that was created for a single being by the Emperor, the Scorch Dragon Velgrynd who still served as the Marshall to this day.

Now the Eastern Empire had a little over a ten thousand otherworlders in the Capital alone. Less than 10% did not awaken a Unique Skill, and so they lived peacefully, and then a little over 10% awakened a combat-oriented Unique Skill.

After some training, those otherworlders tended to join the Imperial Guardians.

Thanks to this, the Eastern Empire had only grown more powerful throughout the centuries.

Power that would be put to use soon, as his Emperor had finally ordered supplies to be gathered, supplies for war.

Veldora's true power was still far beneath the Emperor's power. However, how long had the Daemon been around?

And the Emperor wished to get rid of this threat once and for all before he grew enough to become a thorn in his side. Kenya ooh'd and ahh'd as Elmesia led us through the streets of her city. Even I was enjoying the sites, as was Kurumi. The city was just so different from any city I had ever seen before.

The branches were large enough to house stores and streets for pedestrians to walk across.

"This is so cool!" Kenya exclaimed.

Elmesia preened. "Fufu, of course it is. The Divine Tree is the lifeline of this city, everything has been built for the purpose of making use of the natural resources the Divine Tree provides us."

There were homes nestled into the bark of the tree, there were districts where stores were lined up next to each other, bridges of intertwined vines connected different levels of the city. The air was filled with the scent of blooming flowers and the distant sound of flowing water, creating an atmosphere of tranquility and harmony.

When one thought of a city of Elves, they thought of this city. It just fulfilled the preconceived notions I had of the Elves due to various fictional works I had read.

There were various Elves pointing and whispering once they saw our group.

I raised a brow as a particularly bold child ran up to Elmesia and gave her a flower. Elmesia's smile was blooming as she thanked the child and placed a preservation Spell over the flower.

"It seems you're rather well liked." I said as I walked side by side with Elmesia, my arm still hooked with Kurumi's.

Elmesia smiled smugly. "Of course I am, unless you think there is something not to like?" Elmesia said as she flaunted herself.

I rolled my eyes. Woman would be woman. "No no, nothing like that. I just thought that you were the kind of ruler to laze in your palace and not interact much with your people, that's sure as hell what I do."

"I occasionally go out and interact with my subjects." Elmesia stated.

Kurumi, Elmesia and I continued to make small talk as she showed Kenya and I around. I was glad that Kurumi wasn't afraid to speak up, she was born and raised in this world, most people tend to respect hierarchy and annoying things like that way too much so they are afraid to be themselves around their so-called superiors.

Raiden was much the same in the past, however I had noticed a change within her recently, a change for the better. It seems Kurumi was following in Raiden's footsteps.

I was glad that the two women were growing into their own independent individuals. It boosted a guy's ego when he had women hanging off him sure, but I didn't really want something like that from those I cared about.

That would just be… boring. I would much rather them grow into their own people with their own unique quirks, life was far more exciting and enjoyable that way.

Kenya was suitably amazed at everything, I'm sure he'll enjoy his time here as Elmesia's student.

Before long Elmesia was wrapping up the tour, Erald was still trailing behind us all this time. Poor guy, he was probably overworked.

Elmesia had first teleported us to the residential district, where the homes of those important to Sarion lived. Nobles, relatives of Elmesia, those kinds of people.

Then she showed us around the market district, where people of all sorts of crafts displayed their work. Elmesia pointed out well-known restaurants, each one famous for a particular delicacy.

Then she showed us to the combat district which contained weapons, spell books, you could even rent a teacher for a certain amount of time. They would teach you whatever it is you could learn in that allotted time frame. If you wanted to learn Fire Magic they would teach you that, same with any other form of Magic the rentable teachers knew.

If you were trying to create your own Spell and were struggling the teachers could help you with that too. The culture of Sarion motivated competition and the advancement of Magic as it was one of the things the nation was well known for.

I planned to copy that idea for the rewards center. For an obscene amount of points I'd allow a member of my military to consult with either Arcueid, Lalatina, Megumin about their Magic difficulties for a certain amount of time. Then for Saeko she can assist in Battlewill, Raiden can assist with Battlewill and Holy Magic, Kurumi with Beast Taming, and Sukuna with just being a general menace to society.

He may be loyal to me now, but I have no doubt that Sukuna's original nature still remains somewhere in there.

Whoever bought the consultation could ask for help in learning a Spell or Art, they could ask for Magic that fit their fighting style, or they could even ask for direct training for the duration of their consulting session.

For an even more obscene amount they could directly consult me. I wasn't sure if anyone would ever reach the required amount of points, but it couldn't hurt, maybe it would motivate my minions further.

If anyone actually got enough points to consult me I'd genuinely try my best to help them in what they needed help in.

That meant someone could potentially ask me for a direct training session in which I would do all I could to help them grow stronger, maybe I'd even give them a training regimen to follow.

I would also ask Othinus for her opinion if needed too, I don't do things in half measures, even Hinata was trained properly by me, even if I was more brutal with her. The results did show, look at her, she's a Divine Human now.

It all sounded like a good idea to me.

As the tour was wrapping up Elmesia led us towards the top of the tree, I could see the palace from here.

We walked into a massive secure plaza where the trunk of the Divine Tree widened into a massive platform.

The moment we stepped foot into the plaza I could tell there was something different about this area. The presence of the Divine Tree was far more concentrated, it was almost as if I could feel the attention of the Divine Tree in this place in particular.

Kurumi was looking around in wonder.

I blinked as the wind brushed against my face gently, almost as if a soothing mother was greeting me.

Huh. It seems the Divine Tree was quite alive. If a weapon can have a tool spirit, then why can't a tree?

I looked to the center of the plaza where a fountain stood, its water sparkling with a soft, golden light.

The sheer magicule concentration in the water was honestly absurd. If a strong Greater Majin drank even a drop of it they'd likely die immediately due to magicule poisoning which said something since they were magicule based beings.

The entire area was cleared out before we arrived, I'm betting that Elmesia had it cleared out ahead of time for us.

"This is the center, the heart of Elmine." Elmesia explained with her back turned to us as she gazed up at the fountain. "The water comes from the Divine Tree itself, travels through the roots and to this spot where a fountain was built around it."

She turned around to face us, an uncharacteristic serious expression on her face. "What I am showing you now is a sacred place, even amongst the populace visitation is only allowed after waiting decades on a waitlist for approval."

Kenya stood beside me, a serious look on his face as he gazed at Elmesia. Kurumi nodded in respect to the Elven holy area we were now in.

"Thank you for showing us this then Elmesia."

I could tell this place was important to Elven culture, I may not understand its significance but I could pay respect to her beliefs.

Another gust of wind brushed through my hair, I could even feel the intent the Divine Tree was trying to convey. It seemed almost… happy at the presence of Kurumi, Kenya and I. It didn't truly feel emotions the same way beings like us did, however what it seemed to be conveying was the closest thing to happiness I could think of.

Elmesia accepted my thanks with a nod. "People often come here to meditate and find the center of their being. Some even connect with the Divine Tree's presence and manage to grow from the experience, when this happens it is not uncommon for a normal Elf to become an Enlightened." Elmesia continued.

Is this some cultivation bullshit? Because it sounds like some cultivation bullshit.

"Woah, seriously!" Kenya exclaimed, completely forgetting the atmosphere.

Elmesia however was not offended as she nodded at Kenya with a smile. "I often forget how children are." She sighed.

Heh, as a hag she probably hasn't interacted with young people in ages.

Elmesia shot a glare in my direction, due to some unseen slight no doubt. Kurumi glared back at Elmesia, for some other unseen slight.

Women.

She looked back to Kenya. "Perhaps one day you may be able to connect with the tree."

Kenya nodded with a determined expression on his face. "I'll work hard, teacher!"

Elmesia chuckled softly, clearly amused by his enthusiasm. "I'm sure you will, Kenya. Now, let us wrap this tour up. I am sure you will discover much during your stay here." Elmesia said to Kenya.

Elmesia looked at me. "As for you Felix, you too Kurumi, feel free to return if you wish to explore the Divine Tree more, I will give you both my seal allowing you to travel the Divine Tree freely."

I nodded in thanks. "Thank you Elmesia, I'll return at some point to explore this tree further. I doubt I'll be able to understand the tree in its entirety in the few days I'll be here."

I had gotten Elmesia's approval to stay here for as long as I wanted, though I would only be staying here for a few days.

"Thank you Elmesia." Kurumi said.

"Fufu, it is not often I make new friends whom I can chat with. Call me El from now on Kurumi!" Elmesia said.

Kurumi nodded, a small smile on her face. "El then."

Elmesia nodded. "Very well, come, let us go to my palace. You can stay in one of the guest rooms, Felix. We can further discuss other things tomorrow. I have another room prepared for you as well, Kurumi."

I nodded, as did Kurumi.

"Of course, unless you wish to share a room." Elmesia said with a teasing smirk.

Kurumi's fox ears stiffened. "W-Wah?!"

I laughed. "We'll take separate rooms." Kurumi and I weren't quite in that sort of relationship, and seeing as Kurumi seemed to be weak to Elmesia's teasing I answered in her place.

Through Lover I could tell Kurumi was open to something like that, but I wasn't going to push anything right now.

Kurumi's ears flopped down slightly as an aura of gloom emanated from her.

Oops? I'll have to reassure her later. I just didn't think it was the right time for that step yet.

This was turning out to be a rather enjoyable trip. Who knew learning about other cultures could be fun.

As Elmesia began preparing the teleportation spell, I looked up to the towering branches above us.

"Felix?" Elmesia called out.

Kurumi was also looking at me with curiosity.

"I know you can somewhat understand me. Do you mind giving me a leaf of yours or something?" I said, spreading out my intent throughout the surroundings through Information Particles.

The Divine Tree likely couldn't understand my words, but it could understand the general intent behind my words as well as the Infons I released. It was a tree that was who knows how old, the spirit that embodied it clearly had some level of intelligence.

I didn't want to take a piece of this tree without permission if possible, I would if I had to but the Divine Tree had been nothing but welcoming. I would try diplomacy out of respect for it.

I also had those two favors Elmesia owed me still, I'd rather use those to get a leaf of the Divine Tree than steal one.

A few moments later a gust of wind carried a human sized leaf to me.

I smiled. "Thanks." I said as I stored the large leaf in my Infinity Space.

"Beginning analysis."

I could feel the shock of Elmesia and Erald who was hidden in the shadows.

"The tree usually does not communicate with outsiders." She mumbled. "It rarely communicates with me and mother in fact, yet it seems to be almost… fawning upon you." Elmesia looked at me with a new light in her eye. "Just where do the mysteries end with you Felix? I feel I will have an enjoyable time dissecting you."

I felt a shiver through my body. "I for one do not want to be opened up and looked at."

Kurumi nodded beside me. "Umu! Even if you are now my friend I will not allow harm to come to my master!" Kurumi pouted.

She could tell that Elmesia was merely joking, or else I imagine she wouldn't be as casual about my safety. I knew Kurumi quite well after all, she had latched onto me after she had lost almost everything in her life.

Elmesia's lips curled up. "Of course, of course. Now come. I will show you to your rooms."

As Elmesia prepared her teleportation spell I thought back to her words.

'Any idea why the Divine Tree seems to like me?'

"I do have a guess. It is likely due to the Star King Factor within you, it has changed your Aura signature minutely. Perhaps the tree senses its long gone creator within you and likes you due to that?"

'That would make sense.'

With that mystery solved we were all teleported away.
