Chapter 108: Rain the Fraud!

- Rain -

She allowed a happy go lucky grin to form on her face once she had made enough distance with Lord Guy. If that guy knew she was having fun he'd probably call her back like the meanie he was, so she made sure to suppress her joy.

She had been the one to suggest they directly visit Lune once the little battle that had taken place was over. Lord Guy originally planned to send one of her Lieutenants who was now a Daemon Duke to investigate and perhaps initiate contact with Demon Lord Luminous to make sure that everything was alright in the West.

But that would be boring, she was already pretty bored and she wanted a chance to flex her new power! So she suggested to Lord Guy that he could personally check the situation out, maybe he'd meet someone new and interesting.

That was enough to convince Lord Guy, he was rather carefree like that. So he ordered her to teleport them to Ruberious. He could have done it himself but why was she there if he had to perform the basic tasks?

Despite everything she still prided herself in being one of the two maids of the Lord of Darkness. She'd rather keel over dead than have Lord Guy prepare his own meals or teleport himself like some peasant.

She raised a brow as she felt a decently moderately large aura quickly rush its way towards Lord Guy before shrugging. He would be fine, in fact something like that was the exact reason she was able to convince him to come to Lune in person.

Lord Guy was looking for something or someone interesting to entertain him. Every few centuries he was hit with a spurt of boredom and would sow some chaos in the West to entertain him.

It wouldn't be anything catastrophic of course, just enough to get Humanity a bit worried and change the status quo a bit. This time Lord Guy didn't even have to do anything!

This new generation of Demon Lords were really a fun bunch.

That Rimuru guy was roleplaying as a kingdom builder and was slowly expanding his empire which intrigued Guy. While Felix was just an overpowered bastard which also intrigued Guy. The older Demon Lords were getting caught up in all the change as well, like Luminous, Milim, Leon, and even Dagruel was making some moves behind the scenes.

She was super old so she was used to not having anything interesting happen for a long, long time. But it was still nice that she would get to stretch her legs a bit!

She was using the Hydra as a way to get Lord Guy a little interested but it seems that wasn't needed in the first place.

There was more than enough in this city to entertain Lord Guy somewhat if what she sensed was accurate. And she was a Primordial so of course her senses were accurate.

Though she wasn't lying when she said the person who killed the Hydra had to be quite strong. It was stronger than that guy Clayman, and he was a Demon Lord, though he was a faker. Not like her! She was a real Demon Lord now! Umu! Throughout heaven and earth, she alone was the honored one… or something.

Though she would never be able to call herself a real Demon Lord due to her service to Lord Guy, plus the world didn't actually see her as a Demon Lord, in the world's eyes she was a mere fraud.

She got the power boost but not the status the world gave True Demon Lords, but that was alright. That didn't mean she wouldn't take pride in her newfound power. She was grateful to Felix for that, it had been ages since she was a Devil Lord again.

She was still the one of the strongest people around, but the difference between her Daemon Duke self and Devil Lord self was vast. To the point that she could beat 10 of her old self rather easily now.

In return for Felix's gift she even put yet another good word in for him with Lord Guy! Her benevolence was truly astonishing, she should have been born as one of those pesky Angels instead of as a Daemon. Oh, she had destroyed hundreds of thousands of souls? Pish posh, that didn't count! She was still as pure as an Angel!

She clenched her first, releasing a pleasurable sigh as she felt the overwhelming power within her.

The sheer physical force she could exert now would be enough to punch Clayman away with ease!

She could do that before too, but she'd have to rely on her Aura for that, which was honestly just shameful as a Primordial. But what could she do? The world nerfed the Primordial Daemons whenever they entered the Cardinal World, even Lord Guy was subject to that, being a mere Arch Daemon when he was first summoned by that Jahil guy.

Talk about an idiot. When Lord Guy first summoned them after wiping out that kingdom she was stumped as to how someone could be so stupid. She quickly learned how stupid Humans could be.

After her Awakening she felt like the king of the world, or something. It had been a really long time since she was truly a Devil Lord, it was nice to feel her old power with her once more. Not to mention she was even stronger than she was when she originally left the Daemon Realm! That showed Lord Guy that she wasn't a slacker! So what if he said that she didn't improve much in the 20,000+ years she was in this world?

He was just jealous… yeah, sure, Lord Guy might have been stronger than her. But was he as irredeemably cute as her? Didn't think so. Could he paint women like they were one of his French girls? Nah, man, he couldn't. At least not now, he probably could steal all her years of painting by giving it a side eye. But he still couldn't do it right now, which was enough for her.

She would cope with that thought so she didn't cry.

She didn't acquire an Ultimate Skill, something Lord Guy verbally expressed his disappointment with, she wouldn't lie and say that his comments didn't hurt but Lord Guy was just like that. He cared for her in his own way. Maybe. Probably. Hopefully?

She would be sure to rub it in that pesky Noir's face about how she was stronger than him now though! Same with Arcueid, Megumin, and Lalatina, they always picked on her back in the Daemon Realm.

Sure she was one of the youngest among her kin but that didn't mean they could bully her! Sure they were older and more experienced, but she was a Devil Lord, she would show them their place! Umu! Right after she finished helping Lord Guy with his reconnaissance of course.

She definitely wasn't nervous, she totally wasn't stalling.

Anyways, after she and Misery evolved Lord Guy quickly requested a spar with them. She knew they stood no chance, she was one of the few individuals that had seen Lord Guy go all out on multiple occasions.

But she still thought he wouldn't completely destroy them as he had! As a Primordial she had always had Demon Lord's Haki, just as the rest of her kin had, but the potency of her Haki had increased with her Awakening, but Lord Guy just batted away her and Misery's combined force.

It really was not fair, Lord Guy was just too broken! Her Mist Illusions were seen through, her strengthened Demon Lord's Haki was negated, her Magic was dealt with. Lord Guy was just built different, but that was why she continued to serve him she supposed.

She was there for his first battle against Velzard which turned the Ice Continent into what it had become today. She was around for all his spars with Leon, Leon was seriously a monster for all the destruction he had wrought in those spars.

He was a scary dude, she would highly recommend against messing with him. She had her pride as a Primordial but she also had a sense of self preservation. She knew there were monsters out there far above her pay grade. Leon was one of them.

….Though she didn't even get paid… Even the most common of maids got paid…

She shook away the sad thoughts, today was a day of positivity! Who cared that she was poorer than even that clown Clayman? He was dead, she was not! He got killed in a rather brutal way from what she heard.

Felix was another monster, she had been around for some of his "spars" with Lord Guy, and man they were throwing things around that she would not want to touch with a ten foot pole. Seriously, he wasn't even a Primordial? The world was unfair! How did he get so strong while she only just became a Devil Lord!?

Ugh, he did have the favor of that nepo baby Milim Nava. Maybe that had something to do with it?

In one of the spars she had been observing some time ago she even saw Felix and Lord Guy blink in and out of existence.

It was super freaky, they were in one spot then a moment later they were in another, slightly wounded and laughing. It wasn't teleportation, she was experienced enough to know that.

In fact she recalled something similar happening during Lord Guy and Velzard's original fight. That just went to show that she had a lot more to learn. Her and Misery had been training together ever since their Awakening. Progress was slow but there was at least some progress. Their reserves had grown by a very slight amount at the very least.

She whistled in a carefree manner as she felt a shockwave pass through her, causing her skirt to flutter giving a pantie shot to any soul lucky enough. Though she was under an illusion so no one saw. Sucks to suck.

She was sure Lord Guy was having fun. She could feel a rather powerful Aura erupting from where she left Lord Guy. It was maybe just barely at the level of a Saint. Moments later a barrier was placed isolating that fight from the rest of the city, though many of Luminous' Paladins were panicking and heading to the area the shockwave originated from.

Uh oh, that probably wasn't good. She should probably stop them before they get in the way of Lord Guy's fun. Plus if lots of other people got involved it could send the situation spiraling out of control.

Lord Guy might just purge them all if they annoyed him.

Just before she was about to intervene to distract everyone another man appeared in front of her. Her presence was concealed so he didn't seem to notice her.

"Calm down everyone!" He began. "There was just a little mishap, Saare is handling it!" The man explained.

Saare? Was that the name of the guy who Lord Guy was having fun with? She pitied the guy. He seemed strong, but he really stood no chance. He might even die at the end if he didn't entertain Lord Guy enough. If anything though she could respect the balls on him.

One of the Paladins sighed in relief. "Sir Saare is handling it? Then we can rest assured. Thank you Sir Arnaud!"

She guessed that there were others calming down the Paladins on the other side of Lune. Though just why were the Paladins covering for Lord Guy?

As the Paladins backed off she approached Arnaud. She could tell he was a pretty strong Enlightened. Clayman would lose against him.

Huh, since when did she start using Clayman as a measure of strength? Poor guy, she would forever be using him as a strength measurement. Imagine dying and being so damn weak that even after death your meager strength is multiplied over and over to calculate someone else's strength.

Heh, she would be doing that now. For example, she was about 7 Clayman's strong.

She tapped Arnaud on the shoulder. He immediately stiffened up and swung his blade around at her as it erupted in flames. She had placed an illusion around them just before she tapped him as she expected something like this to happen.

She held the sword back with a single finger as the searing hot flames attempted to burn her alive. She merely raised a brow and gently blew out the flames. "That wasn't very nice!" She said with a playful grin.

Arnaud was looking at her with some fear in his eyes, but there was some determination in there as well. She missed talking to people who were weaker than her. She had been associating with absolute monsters so much that she forgot the looks of absolute terror people shot her.

Arnaud's grip on his weapon tightened as she placed a hand on her hip. "W-Who are you!?" He demanded.

She could tell he was reinforcing himself with his Aura, he was preparing for a fight which was smart. His eyes were quickly glancing through the surroundings, he was confused why the nearby Paladins were not doing anything. Illusions were handy for things like that.

She just waved him off. "Don't worry. I'm not here to cause trouble, just have a little fun!"
"Are you with the man that Saare is fighting?" Arnaud questioned.

She raised a brow but nodded. Oddly enough Arnaud relaxed at her confirmation. Now she was confused.

"Lady Luminous has informed me that we have a colleague of hers visiting today." Arnaud explained seeing his confusion.

"Luminous reacted quickly then." She mused out loud. "Why is that man named Saare fighting my Lord then?"

Arnaud's lips twitched. "Lady Luminous decided to not inform Saare as by the time she realized one of her colleagues had arrived, Saare had already begun clashing with them. She believed that Saare would not be harmed so she wished to have Saare test himself against her colleague."

Luminous was a sneaky one. Using Lord Guy as a sharpening tool for one of her own subordinates. She was sure Lord Guy had realized the same, he was probably just amused.

Though Luminous was being rather trusting if she expected Lord Guy not to kill her minion. Her bet paid off this time, but Lord Guy was rather whimsy at the best of times.

This Arnaud guy must also be pretty trusted by Luminous for her to bother explaining her reasoning to him.

She sighed. "Let's go then. It seems my fun time is going to be cut short today."

Arnaud nodded as he fully sheathed his sword. "May I ask for your name?"

"Hmm? Oh, you can call me Lady Rain."

Arnaud froze up. "Rain… one of the maids of Guy Crimson? Do you serve the Lord of Darkness?" He asked in a dead tone of voice.

"Mhmm!" She cheerfully nodded, grinning slightly at Arnaud's obvious fear. It was good to be her.

- Luminous Valentine -

She watched Saare's fight from above. She almost immediately recognized Guy's presence in Lune.

She was busy, but when the Lord of Darkness comes to pay a visit, you receive him. He wasn't here to cause trouble, if he was he would have already done something. Plus she had a significant amount of forces concentrated in Ruberious at the moment, not that she was deluded enough to believe that would mean anything to Guy, but the strong people present did matter.

Felix was still here, Hinata was still unconscious but Luminous still felt confident that with all the forces present even Guy would be hesitant to push his boundaries.

The power she felt from Felix that day was truly absurd, to the point that she felt confident that Guy would at the very least be careful of pushing his boundaries, similar to how he acted with Milim Nava.

Milim may have enjoyed playing the fool but all of the older Demon Lords were well aware that she mustn't be underestimated.

It only put into perspective how much more she had to work on herself, and she had been doing so. Her reserves had grown a fair portion, especially since she acquired Granbell's lifeforce which strengthened her fairly significantly.

Though she would not put herself down either, she was well aware that she was one of the most extraordinary individuals in existence.

In the end the "class" she most identified with was the support class. Her healing capabilities were second to none, and she felt confident that at her full power she could heal entire battlefields of millions in an instant.

Combat was simply not her main priority until recently.

Felix would likely be here in moments. Felix and Guy had a rather odd relationship from what she had observed, but to each's own. Personally she would not like a man such as Guy Crimson to be a friend, but that was her own personal opinion.

Just before she was about to greet and question Guy she felt Saare charge ahead. She was rather impressed that Saare managed to sense Guy's Aura. Saare likely believed Guy to be an enemy, so he attacked first and asked questions later. Something he would be reprimanded for. But for now she saw it as a potential learning opportunity for Saare.

Previously the majority of her attention was on Hinata as she believed Hinata had the most potential of the bunch. Saare was also rather impressive however, perhaps he would learn a thing or two from his… spar with Guy, if you could call what she was watching a spar.

She was rather surprised that Saare had continued his assault beyond the initial attack, Guy Crimson's general appearance was infamous throughout the Cardinal World. She had no doubt that Saare recognized Guy the moment he caught sight of him.

It went to show how much courage Saare had that he was willing to challenge Guy despite the obvious fear he must have been feeling.

She guessed that Saare perhaps thought the attack may have been a scheme caused by internal fighting among the Demon Lords. It wasn't as if she explained all the inner workings to her subordinates, only her closest subordinates such as Louis and Gunther were aware of what had happened.

Saare likely thought that Guy was perhaps here to finish the job, that was the only explanation she could consider as to why Saare was putting his everything on the line currently.

Despite everything, Saare was loyal to her, or at least to what she represented. He cared for the people who dwelled within her territory and he would fight tooth and nail to protect them.

Saare was unaware about the internal workings of the Nine Sovereigns, he likely thought Felix and Rimuru were the only Demon Lords he didn't have to worry about.

Whereas in reality none of the Demon Lords would challenge each other without warning or reason. Dagruel had the most reason to attack her, yet even he hadn't initiated any attacks just yet.

She had informed some of the other Nine Great Saints to divert any Paladins from entering the area as she did not wish to make a scene out of it. She further went on to place a barrier around Guy and Saare so the fight would remain isolated.

It was a shame, Felix had just remade the city, yet she had a feeling that there would be more damage that needed to be repaired.

For now she would watch.

"So what'd I miss?" Felix's voice echoed out from behind her, though she felt the presence of another man behind Felix.

"Nothing much." She responded, her thin lips curving into a smile.

- Guy Crimson -

He allowed a small grin to form on his face as he took on the white haired Saint's attacks. He merely tilted his head, allowing the young Saint's weapon to boom past his head leaving shockwaves in its wake.

Guy casually leaped backwards, creating some distance between him and his attacker. He could sense Luminous and Felix hovering above him. How kind of them to let him have his fun. Though he sensed someone else that he hadn't sensed in a long time. It had been so long that he was considering if his own senses failed him.

He had only met Damrada in passing once before, but Damrada was strong and so Guy had remembered him, even after all this time.

He supposed he'd get his questions answered soon enough.

He could also sense Rain making her way towards him with someone else. It seems she wouldn't be getting to have much fun after all.

Maybe he'd give her another vacation? She had been making progress, and good deeds ought to be rewarded.

Both Misery and Rain seemed to have finally taken a hint and began training themselves. They were stronger than they were back in the Daemon Realm, but that wouldn't be enough.

Neither had acquired Ultimate Skills but that wasn't unexpected for Guy. Even he hadn't acquired an Ultimate Skill after his Awakening, he was too Prideful, thinking his abilities would be enough to take on the entire world.

He had been humbled by Velda very quickly.

He had always been annoyed at Misery and Rain's lack of progress, but he wouldn't force them to train, that will had to come from within themselves.

He did still consider them close companions of his, he would even avenge them if they got themselves killed, but not much more than that.

Though he did have to wonder if he now had to consider the fact that each and every Primordial had been Awakened into Devil Lords. If Felix could Awaken Misery and Rain, then he could do so with the rest. Though the soul requirement would be rather troublesome to satisfy. Guy hadn't heard any reports of any kingdoms being destroyed so the soul issue still remained.

Of course Guy considered the possibility that Felix already had the souls, in which case there was nothing Guy could do except account for the new Devil Lords that had been thrown into the mix of his game with Rudra.

"What is your name?" Guy asked as he casually tucked his hands into his pockets. This man was far too weak for him to use even his fists, let alone draw his blade. That didn't mean that he wouldn't enjoy toying with him though.

The Saint's grip on his blade tightened. Guy could tell the man was terrified, yet he was still standing. Something like that was rather impressive, he has seen people terrify themselves into death when in his presence before.

"Saare. And you will walk no further. I will not allow you to." Saare declared with solemnity.

Guy laughed. "Pffft! Perhaps I have been too quiet if you Humans underestimate me so." Guy said mockingly.

It was ludicrous to even think that Saare could last a second against him if Guy wanted him dead. Saare was weak, he was merely stronger than most which was enough to entertain Guy for now. He had come to gather information after all. He had never been one for spying and sneaking around. He preferred to be direct.

"You're the one who's underestimating me!" Saare yelled as he dashed forwards leaving behind a sonic explosion.

Guy Crimson stood still, his grin widening as Saare surged forward, the sonic boom trailing behind him. The white-haired Saint's blade gleamed with holy energy, crackling with power as he brought it down in an arc meant to cleave him in two.

With a flick of his wrist, Guy conjured a barrier of crimson flames, the air around it warping from the intense heat. Saare's blade struck the barrier, sending a cascade of sparks and shockwaves in every direction. The collision of holy energy and his flames created an ear-splitting crackle, illuminating the battlefield in the process.

Guy hadn't been using anything Saare wasn't capable of handling. It would be too boring if he accidentally killed Saare. He was just trying to test this newbie Saint for now.

"Is that it?" Guy asked, his tone dripping with mockery. "If you're going to entertain me, you'll need to do better than that, weakling." Guy said as he mockingly yawned.

His words seemed to only tick Saare off more. It really was too fun messing with those beneath him.

With a casual motion, Guy waved his hand, and the flames of his barrier swirled outward, coiling like serpents toward the Saint. The surrounding temperatures would incinerate even an Enlightened in an instant, but not much more than that.

Guy lightly tapped on the ground with his foot. He was surprised the land around him wasn't melting, it seems it was enchanted to be able to last even in somewhat high level fights.

Saare reacted swiftly, channeling more holy energy into his blade, creating a radiant crescent of energy that sliced through the incoming fire. The two forces collided mid-air, resulting in a powerful explosion that shook the ground.

Saare didn't let up. He leaped into the air, raising his blade high as he chanted a spell. Golden runes spiraled around him, and a massive spear of light materialized above his head. With a shout, he hurled it toward Guy.

"Interesting." Guy mused, watching the spear descend with the force of a meteor. He raised a finger, and a glowing red sigil formed in the air. As the spear closed in, the sigil expanded and absorbed the attack, neutralizing it in a flash of crimson light. He had always enjoyed messing with runes.

Before Saare could react, Guy extended his hand, and the absorbed energy morphed into a barrage of crimson shards that rained down on the Saint. Saare dodged and parried as best he could, his movements a blur. Despite his skill, several shards found their mark, tearing into his armor and drawing some life blood.

Saare gritted his teeth, his aura flaring brighter. "I won't fall here!" He roared as he ignored his wounds.

"Ah, so there's more to you after all." Guy said, smiling slightly. He cracked his neck and finally pulled his hands from his pockets. He had yet to even take a step forward this entire fight. "Then perhaps I'll try just a teeny tiny bit more."

The air grew heavy as Guy unleashed a fraction of his true power. Crimson and black energy danced across his body, and the ground beneath him cracked and smoldered from the sheer intensity of his aura. This wasn't even 1/100,000 of his aura, but it was still fairly impressive that Saare was still standing.

"Let's see if your light can withstand my darkness, Saint." Guy taunted, but just before he could attack a single hand appeared on Saare's shoulder. All of Saare's wounds were instantly healed up.

"That would be enough, Saare." Guy grinned as Luminous stood behind Saare. She seemed no worse for wear despite the fights that had occurred in her home territory. If he knew one thing he knew Luminous had to have been ticked off, she was a prideful one.

She had grown stronger… far stronger. An Ultimate Skill?

"L-Lady Luminous!"

"Leave us." Luminous demanded.

"B-But!" Saare protested.

"Now." Luminous ordered.

Saare grit his teeth but nodded. Just as he was leaving, Luminous said, "I will be informing Hinata of your reckless actions."

"Yes." Saare mumbled as he walked away.

Guy didn't even blink as Felix appeared beside Luminous. "Ha! He looks like a kicked puppy, Luminous!" Felix chortled.

Luminous smirked slightly. "Indeed. It was a good fight however." Saare must have heard Luminous as he seemed to have gained a pep in his step.

Guy's eyes narrowed as he gazed at Felix, sensing his gaze Felix merely winked at him.

Guy sensed something… familiar from Felix. Felix may have been suppressing his Aura masterfully, but even then some taint of his Aura was left on Felix's body. That taint felt like that of Velda's Aura though different. It shared similarities with Velda's, Veldora's, and even Velzard's Aura but it was still entirely its own thing.

Just what had Felix done to himself? Guy sighed, he didn't think Felix would be answering that question, and Guy didn't think it wise to alienate Felix by trying to force the issue so he would let it be for now.

Still, he was rather curious.

It wasn't hidden from his view that Felix had chosen to stand next to Luminous. Felix was making his support of Luminous in this situation clear, he was telling Guy that if Guy was here to cause trouble, then he would be helping Luminous out. Guy didn't enjoy playing politics, but that didn't mean he didn't understand them.

Guy lightly stretched. It was an entertaining fight, nothing to write home about but it kept him entertained for a few moments. Saare did have some potential, and Guy was curious if Saare would ever reach his full potential, but nothing more than that.

He was able to confirm that Luminous did indeed acquire an Ultimate Skill. It was about time, if she hadn't been so lazy then perhaps she would have acquired one long ago. At least she got one now, she would be a useful piece to use against Rudra.

Guy's eyes wandered behind Felix, where Damrada was standing. "And I thought I was mistaken. It has been quite some time, Damrada."

Damrada nodded. "Indeed. It is an honor to see you again, Lord Guy." Damrada dipped his head.

Guy just nodded as he stepped forwards. He was here for a reason after all, work came before his fun. Though in this case his fun and work were one and the same. Before he could speak he was interrupted.

"Lord Guy~! Your wonderful maid has returned!" Rain yelled as she skipped towards him. She really was too childish.

Guy sighed, Felix shot him a sympathetic smile. Rain took her place beside him as the Paladin that she arrived with went to stand behind Luminous. "You may leave, Arnaud."

The man bowed. "Yes, Lady Luminous."

Now that they were mostly alone Luminous spoke up. "Why are you here, Guy?"

"Oh? Getting right into things?"

Rain stepped forwards, her hands on her hips as she pouted at Luminous. "Hey! At least serve us some tea or something!"

Guy raised a brow at Rain's uncharacteristic outburst.

She was acting far more confident than she usually did in front of his fellow True Demon Lords. Before she wouldn't exactly cower in front of them, but she would be wary of them which was fair.

Now however she was standing in front of Luminous as an equal. It seems that Awakening gave Rain a rather large confidence boost.

If it weren't for Luminous acquiring an Ultimate Skill of her own, then Guy believed that in a fight between Luminous and Rain the results were not as certain. Oh, Luminous would win by a land slide, but she would need to exert some more effort.

Luminous narrowed her eyes as a light pressure began to leak from her. Felix placed a hand on Luminous' shoulder. "Relax." Felix chided. "You know how Rain is."

"Tsk." Luminous clicked her tongue. "It seems that your Awakening has given you a bit of an ego." Luminous stated.

Rain puffed up her chest. "Hehe, I bet I'd be able to beat you up easy now!" Rain said as she began shadow boxing around. Had Rain been hanging out with Ramiris or something?

Guy sighed. Rain really had no sense of self preservation, but he'd let her dig her own grave. Luminous wouldn't go too hard on her, she knew the consequences if something fatal happened to Rain.

Luminous raised a brow. "Is that so? Then I suppose we can test that another time then." With that Luminous stopped paying Rain any attention, making his maid pout. She really was too needy. Even though he beat her up, that didn't seem to have been enough to put her ego in check. He really should have brought Misery instead, she was far more obedient.

"Let us go somewhere more private." Luminous said. She snapped her fingers, teleporting them into a meeting room of some sort. Guy didn't even blink as he took a seat, casually lounging back. Rain took her place behind him. Look at her, trying to be a proper maid.

Felix and Luminous took their seats with Damrada standing behind Felix. That alone was a message. Why had Damrada aligned himself with Felix? Last Guy heard Damrada was still serving Rudra, though that was a long time ago.

As Guy contemplated Damrada the door opened. Gunther walked in, a tray in hand. Gunther quickly went around the room and served each of them tea.

Gunther was a massive disappointment in Guy's eyes. He had a lot of potential, he was a Progenitor of an entire race, and was born strong enough to kill most Saints.

If he became a True Demon Lord Guy had no doubt that he would become a valuable pawn, but he wasted it all on playing butler.

Once Gunther left Guy finally leaned forwards. "It seems events worked out in your favor this time, Luminous." Guy began as he took a sip of his tea.

He didn't know whether Luminous had only just acquired her Ultimate Skill during the attack, or if she acquired it earlier. What he did know was that during the last Walpurgis she had no Ultimate Skill. Her total energy also had gone up by around 20%. A rather significant gain.

And that was even more impressive when considering the fact that forming an Ultimate Skill costed a significant amount of energy, more energy than what most Saints had.

If she had another few centuries perhaps she could become someone even he would need to take seriously, though with her attitude probably not.

Luminous lightly stirred her cup of tea. "Indeed. Quite a few annoyances were dealt with. I can only thank Felix for keeping your interference away. It would have been quite troublesome if you decided to attack the West with your Daemons… again."

Guy smirked. "Indeed." Luminous always did like to play these sorts of games, talking around the subject but never quite going into depth. She always managed to get what she wanted out of a Walpurgis through that method, at least until she swapped herself out for Roy.

Felix yawned as he leaned back against his seat, tilting it to balance on 2 out of the 4 legs. "Why're you here, Guy?" Felix asked casually.

Luminous turned to glare at him for interrupting the game she was playing, Felix just smirked at her which only seemed to annoy her more.

Guy tilted his cup of tea back and quickly guzzled it down, the tea was quite tasty after all. "Hmm, I just wanted to check up on some things. You said you'd handle it but it would be irresponsible for me if I just left it at that."

Felix nodded. "That's fair."

Guy's gaze wandered to Damrada who was staring ahead stone faced. "Why are you here, Damrada?" Guy asked. Damrada looked to Felix who nodded to Damrada.

"I have decided to serve Lord Felix wholeheartedly." Guy's eyes narrowed at his suspicions being confirmed.

Luminous' brows furrowed as she looked at Felix in confusion.

Felix noticed her gaze. "I'll tell you later."

She slowly nodded.

"Just why are you serving Felix? Last time I met you your loyalty to Rudra was overflowing, what changed?"

Damrada looked to Felix again. Felix just shrugged. "Tell him whatever you want to, I imagine he probably knows most of it."

Before Damrada could speak Guy gestured to an open chair. "Take a seat." Luminous' eyes narrowed at the clear powerplay he just made. This was Luminous' domain, yet he was acting as if it was his own home.

Damrada looked to Luminous for confirmation. "May I?"

Luminous nodded. "At least one of you has manners." She whispered under her breath.

Damrada took his seat and opened his mouth. "I am unsure if you are aware, but Emperor Rudra is dying." Luminous' eyes widened as she looked to Felix for confirmation. Felix subtly nodded, confirming Damrada's words to Luminous. A small smile spread across Luminous' face, one she quickly hid with her cup of tea.

Guy's smile wilted slightly. Of course he knew that Rudra's soul was degrading over time, he was the one who told Rudra about it. He wondered if Velda saw this coming? Who could tell with that guy?

"I'm aware, I'm the one who told him about his condition." Guy answered.

Damrada nodded. "I thought as much."

Damrada went on to explain that Rudra had ended up tasking Damrada to find someone capable of defeating him. Rudra was fearful that should he lose his battle against Michael, then his body would be forfeit to Michael, which Rudra did not want as he did not know what chaos Michael would unleash upon this world.

Luminous had some questions about Michael that Felix was able to answer.

"Hmm, I see." Guy responded simply. Guy could always take on Rudra on his own, in the past they were once equals, but over time the gap between them had widened ever so slightly.

When they first began their spars Guy had to use everything in his power to fight Rudra to a draw. But overtime Guy grew stronger or Rudra grew weaker, to the point that Rudra always placed barriers around them to weaken Guy before their spars. Without those barriers Guy would firmly be in the lead between the two of them.

Guy had always known that the game between him and Rudra would end in one of two ways.

Either Rudra would win and Guy would serve him as agreed upon, or Rudra would die and Guy would win their game.

Guy had stopped caring for their game long, long ago. But when he met Rudra after Velda and Lucia's death, Rudra was in a broken state. It hurt to see a once great man, a man Guy considered his equal to be in such a state, and so Guy reminded Rudra of their game. That if Rudra didn't get up off his ass, Guy would be the winner.

That seemed to have been enough to put a little bit of light in Rudra's eyes, and ever since then their game had been Rudra's purpose for living. The game was the only thing pushing Rudra forward, and so Guy had taken on the burden of keeping their game afloat, all so that Rudra could live for just another day. It was the least he could do for his best friend.

"And you chose… Felix for your goal?" Guy asked.

Guy could see Damrada's reasoning. Felix was strong, Guy would be the first to admit that. He was absurdly talented as well, more talented than Rudra.

He had prodded Milim a bit and learned that just a few short years ago Felix was a nameless Arch Daemon, one that Guy likely wouldn't have given a second look at.

Yet now he was a powerful Devil Lord that Guy could respect as a peer. The sheer rate of his progress was absurd. The strongest non Primordial Daemon previously was one of Arcueid's subordinates, and he was tens of thousands of years old, and even he couldn't touch a Primordial.

That truly put into perspective just how insane what Felix had done. He had done in not even 5 years what none had done in eons.

Felix had learned Time Stop, an ability Guy took a very long time to learn, and only managed due to copying Gabriel, Lord of Patience from Velzard.

Felix's control over his own power could rival Guy's own and he had much more experience. Felix's Arts were top notch, everything about him surpassed expectations, and Guy would give anything to figure out just how Felix ticked. But that was for another time.

Rudra hadn't become quite that strong that fast, and Rudra was the student of God and the most talented person Guy had ever met prior to Felix.

Rudra didn't even get his overpowered Ultimate Skill on his own merits, he traded Velda for it, though previously Rudra had Uriel, Lord of Vows which was incredibly powerful in its own right. Velda had also offered Guy an Ultimate Skill but he rejected Velda. He was too prideful to accept handouts like that. But he didn't blame those who did like Rudra, Velzard, and Velgrynd.

Damrada nodded. "He was not my first choice, but I do believe he has the potential."

"Aww, you're going to make me blush!" Felix laughed.

Luminous lightly slapped his shoulder. "Cease your arrogance." She then looked at Damrada. "And you, mind your words, Felix has a big enough head as it is."

Damrada's lips twitched. Guy was curious just how Felix and Damrada ended up meeting, but he didn't care enough to ask about that at the moment. He had bigger priorities.

"Now if you're done with your questions I'd like to ask you some of my own since you're here." Felix said.

Guy raised a brow. He had thought that Felix had already asked most of his questions. "Very well. What are your questions?" Guy had a feeling that this conversation would make or break his relationship with Felix, and he was all for it.

Life would be way too boring if there weren't oddballs thrown in here or there.

Story: I'm a Daemon, so what?

Chapter 109: Hinata Awakens

- Hinata Sakaguchi -

Hinata groggily opened her eyes, and within moments she processed the events that had recently occurred.

She could feel her new Ultimate Skill perfectly slotted within her soul, its powers hers to call upon. She would have to test it out a little bit later before she challenged Veldora to a fight. This time she would face him with her own abilities, and she was even looking forward to it.

But that was for later, when things calmed down a bit, she got more free time, and she had a chance to truly experiment.

With a sigh she sat up and looked around the room. Her lips twitched at the state of her room, and she knew only Felix could be responsible, but she would focus on that later.

She had no idea how long she had been out of it, but she hoped it wouldn't have been too long. She closed her eyes and expanded her senses only to let out a sigh of relief as she sensed Felix, Luminous… Damrada, and a Daemon of some kind all together in one room.

The accuracy of her senses had grown more potent through her awakening as a True Hero, she could tell that much.

She was curious who the last person with them was, perhaps she would go check on them, but first she clenched her fists.

The amount of physical power she had now was many times greater than the power she held previously. Awakening as a True Hero may not have evolved her or anything, but her physical power alone was enough to crush an Incomplete Saint in an instant.

Hinata flexed her fingers experimentally, feeling the raw power coursing through her body. Her muscles felt denser, there was more energy in them, and they felt more responsive, a stark reminder of her newfound strength. It was disorienting, but also exhilarating.

She could sense the difference in her own Aura, it was sharper, more refined, like a blade honed to perfection. She wouldn't have been able to tell before, but she could tell that there was a difference in people's Auras, based on their stage in evolution, age, mastery, etc.

She already possessed Divinity, but her Awakening refined it further as there were clear "tiers" within Divinity.

Felix's Divinity for example was more potent than hers, she wasn't quite sure why but her Awakening increased the potency of her own Divinity.

Divinity in general was not an authority or Skill of any kind, it was just another higher form of energy. It was of a higher quality and thus could do more with less, that was it.

Felix coated a stick in Divinity in the past and that increased the overall power and structure of the stick by an enormous extent. To the point that he was able to use that same stick to match and surpass her old Legend Grade rapier and soundly defeat her.

At its base Divinity was an enhancer to anything and everything it was applied to.

Hinata rose from the bed, her movements fluid and controlled despite her enhanced strength. She glanced at her reflection in a nearby mirror, her appearance had not changed as her evolution to Divine Human had already refined her to an incredible extent. She was in no way "perfect" as no one was, but her beauty was well within the supernatural category.

But there was no time for self-reflection. The presence of a Daemon in the same room as Felix, Luminous, and Damrada was troubling. She couldn't help but feel concerned despite knowing the strength of Felix and Luminous.

As for Damrada, she didn't know why exactly he was with them.

She wasn't quite sure how powerful the Daemon was as it was carefully controlling its power, only allowing a slight amount of Aura to emanate from his body. The Daemon would have to be a fool to be hostile, with the combined might of Luminous and Felix, not many if any would manage to get out of that alive.

She guessed Damrada and the Daemon were in league with one another, she knew Damrada was firmly on Yuuki's side and he had clearly made himself an enemy when he led her to attack Tempest.

The Daemon was likely involved in the attack in some way and Damrada and the Daemon were now possibly negotiating for something now that the attack had very clearly failed.

That was just her guess though, perhaps she was wrong. At least that gave her a general idea of just how much time had passed. If they were still dealing with the after effects of the attack then it couldn't have been that long since she fell unconscious.

Normally she wouldn't have even fallen unconscious, but her Awakening this time was different than most Awakenings.

Her power even before she Awakened was already incredibly potent, as a Divine Human she could take on some True Demon Lords and come out on top, she was in the same realm as True Heroes while not being one herself.

Yet she went and grew even stronger, such a drastic and sudden rise in energy can be dangerous if not handled properly. So her spirit forced her into unconsciousness so she could quickly adapt to the new level of power she possessed as well as use Fortuna to calculate the best way to control her power. Without Fortuna it would have taken even longer.

She brushed a strand of hair behind her ear before she gently rubbed a finger across the bracelet that housed her armor and rapier. Both had been given blessings of sorts from her Awakening. They were even stronger now and were in the process of stabilizing. She expected their total energy to at least increase by 50% which was a significant margin.

As she prepared to leave she spotted something from the corner of her eyes. Her eyes narrowed as she saw Granbell's longsword leaning harmlessly against the wall. No energy from it was leaking, it was as if it didn't exist to her perception.

Just what was it doing here?

She was grateful to Granbell for what he did for her so she was rather upset that despite everything he wasn't put to rest with his weapon at the very least. It was what she would have wanted were she to die. She thought Granbell was worthy of at least a proper death. The man was a Hero, he followed his beliefs even if they put him against the entire world. He did what he did because he believed it was right, and Hinata respected that immensely.
As she walked towards it she felt it start to release a subtle aura causing her to lift a brow. It was possible to imbue your intent within a weapon, though it was incredibly difficult. What she felt from Truth was that it wanted her to wield it as her weapon. Had Granbell wished to gift her Truth? Truly she was being spoiled.

If that was what Granbell wanted then she wouldn't reject it. Though she already had a weapon of choice, and she wouldn't just throw Divine Moonlight away, it was a gift from Felix.

She smirked slightly. She had always wanted to dual wield but could never find two weapons of similar high quality to wield. With her increased strength she could manage to put the same amount of force behind her strikes when she used two hands with one hand now, so her strength would not suffer for it.

Hinata reached out to Truth, the longsword radiating a faint pulse as her fingers brushed its hilt. It was subtle, but she felt the resonance between them, like a quiet acknowledgment.

It wasn't just a weapon, it was alive in its own way, imbued with Granbell's will and purpose. The intent was unmistakable, Truth recognized her, approved of her, and wanted to be wielded by her.

Truth was a powerful weapon, it had more energy than Divine Moonlight did, at least before Divine Moonlight was strengthened by her Awakening.

Truth was Granbell's weapon of choice for centuries so it made sense that it was a very high tier God Grade weapon. It had been through an unimaginable amount of bloodshed, of that she was certain.

She wrapped her fingers around the hilt, and as she lifted it, a wave of energy surged through her arm, rushing to meet her core. It was not overwhelming, but invigorating, as if the sword were testing her, gauging her worth. Tool spirits weren't quite alive per say but they had a will.

Hinata's smirk deepened. "So, this is how it is, huh? You want to see if I'm up to your standards?" She muttered, gripping the weapon more firmly. It was a rather arrogant weapon in her opinion, but that would just make it more satisfying when she inevitably tamed it.

Truth seemed to answer. The sword hummed faintly, its aura aligning with hers, amplifying her Divinity. It seems Truth's primary effect was that of "amplification". That explained why Granbell's Melt Strike was so powerful.

Truth was not domineering but cooperative, as if it had been waiting for her to wield it properly. The blade's edge shimmered faintly in the light, and Hinata could sense the immense potential it held.

"Fine." She said softly, giving the weapon a small flourish. The blade responded effortlessly, moving with her, an extension of her will. It felt...right. It wasn't quite as natural as Divine Moonlight, but Hinata felt it would reach that stage eventually.

Hinata turned her attention to Divine Moonlight, the rapier gifted by Felix. She summoned it from her bracelet, its sleek form materializing in her other hand. The two weapons radiated distinct energies, Divine Moonlight precise and graceful, Truth powerful and unyielding. Yet, when held together, they complemented each other perfectly, like two halves of a greater whole.

"How convenient." She muttered. "Granbell, if this was your intention, I'll honor it." She said quietly. She'd use his weapon alongside her own to protect Humanity in her own way.

Her grip on the swords tightened as she felt them synchronizing with her aura. The room seemed to respond to the convergence of their energies, a faint ripple spreading outward. Even without unleashing their full power, the potential was staggering.

She gave an experimental swing, the motions fluid and precise. The swords moved as if they had always been meant to be wielded together, and her body adjusted naturally to the new rhythm.

With two powerful blades, dual wielding wasn't just a pipedream for her anymore, it was a viable strategy, one that suited her newfound strength and agility. She didn't need a free hand to cast Magic or anything, she could do that chantlessly without any sort of gestures if she wanted to. Though she didn't use pure Magic much in the first place.

Hinata sheathed both weapons, returning Divine Moonlight to its bracelet as she made to carefully set Truth at her side, Truth itself reacted to her storage bracelet. Her brows shot up as she felt Truth connect with her storage bracelet. Previously the bracelet was designed with the sole function of storing her armor and rapier, Felix made it that way. Yet now she felt the bracelet changing to allow Truth to be stored in it as well.

How convenient. Truth was quickly stored within her bracelet.

Straightening her posture, she left the room, her steps echoing in the corridor. "Lady Hinata." She paused and turned around, unsurprised to see Gunther standing by.

In her experience Gunther was always around when he felt he was needed. She had already sensed his presence before he spoke up. His Aura was rather unmistakable after all, and despite his age he didn't have quite perfect control over his leaking Aura.

It was incredibly difficult to completely suppress your leaking Aura, in fact she thought it impossible for years until she realized just how weak she was in the grand scheme of things. Even Luminous originally radiated a slight amount of her Aura, though ever since Hinata had come back to the present she noticed that Luminous no longer leaked any Aura.

"Gunther." She nodded with a smile to the old butler. She wasn't really close with Gunther but she appreciated his service and reliability. Many times in the past he had prepared her delicious meals, both when she went to the past and after she joined Luminous' inner circle.

He was a strong fighter too, she remembered him helping in one of the Tenma Wars. It truly enlightened her on just how much strength he was hiding in his old visage. Safe to say, Gunther's mastery of his Vampiric abilities was absurd.

"I do believe that you should be resting." Gunther said in his grandfatherly tone.

She just smiled. "I'm fine, Gunther. I cannot afford to be lazing about during this trying period of time."

Gunther sighed as he adjusted his glasses. "Very well, I suppose I cannot convince you otherwise."

As she made to turn around and leave she paused. Perhaps Gunther could give her some more information about the situation.

"What is the situation like now?" She asked.

Gunther immediately knew what she was getting at. He went on to tell her about what happened after she fell unconscious. About Luminous killing Granbell, about the Monsters that had attacked Lune, about how her Paladins reacted to the attack, Gunther knew almost everything.

She was rather proud that her Paladins were able to react in a timely manner and deal with everything in an orderly fashion. She had trained them for such spontaneous events but drills and such did not totally prepare one for how to act in a catastrophic event. Drills did not capture the sheer range of emotions one felt during such catastrophes.

The fact that they maintained their composure and executed their duties flawlessly was a testament to their discipline and the leadership abilities the other Great Saints had displayed.

Saare was not around for the majority of the attack as he had been ordered by her to represent the Western Holy Church in the meeting between Tempest and the Council of the West, yet he still managed to return.

Saare had displayed a real change ever since she came back and she couldn't be happier. It wouldn't take long for him to completely spiritualize into a Complete Saint.

"Do we have confirmation of the other attackers' identities?" Hinata inquired, her tone sharp.

It wasn't as if Granbell acted alone, the Monsters he had somehow tamed couldn't all have been under his command while he simultaneously fought her. There was Kagali and her Moderate Harlequin Alliance, and then even Cerberus wasn't completely dismantled to her knowledge. While Yuuki was its head it wasn't as if the organization would immediately collapse without him.

There was Kagali, and Damrada still left as well as other higher ups of Cerberus.

Gunther nodded. "One lady known as Misha was taken care of by one of Lord Felix's subordinates. Razul, the Guardian of the West was also finished off by two of Lord Felix's subordinates."

She raised a brow. She didn't know much about Misha other than the fact that Misha was one of the three leaders of Cerberus alongside Damrada and Vega. That left only Damrada.

As for Razul, she knew that the Guardian of the West was an ally of Granbell's. She was honestly impressed by his strength. To hold off the Lord of Darkness' Daemons was no easy feat. She wondered which of Felix's subordinates took care of him?

"As for Kagali and her subordinate Tear, Lady Luminous took care of them." Gunther informed.

Hinata nodded. "Excellent." With Kagali likely dead that should mean that Cerberus would no longer be an issue. Damrada would be taken care of, he was in the same room as Felix and Luminous, she was sure they had something in mind to deal with him.

Perhaps Gunther would have an idea about the Daemon she sensed. For some reason the Daemon just seemed… off putting. She couldn't explain why but she just had a bad feeling even when just thinking about him. "What of the Daemon I sense with Luminous and Felix?" She asked.
For the first time Hinata saw a look of genuine fear and worry on Gunther's face. "The Daemon…." Gunther sighed. "Is Guy Crimson. He showed up for some reason, Lady Luminous and Lord Felix left to receive him."

Hinata didn't bother responding as she vanished, heading towards the meeting room. She hadn't ever met Guy Crimson in person, but if what Felix and Luminous said about him had even a grain of truth, then she should be there acting as some sort of reinforcement. After underestimating the Demon Lords once before, she would never do so again.

- Gadra -

As Gadra continued his reconnaissance, he felt a growing unease despite his skills and precautions. He had made every measure to make sure he remained undetected, he truly was not underestimating the Demon Lord's forces but he still felt something was off.

It was subtle, like a whisper at the edge of his awareness, but it lingered. His Extra Skills, Danger Sense and Presence Detection, had remained silent, yet the instinct honed over centuries of perilous encounters nudged at him.

He dismissed it for now, chalking it up to paranoia brought on by the high-stakes mission. However the longer his instincts warned him the more he realized he should arrange an escape plan immediately.

As he made his way through the city he quickly began thinking up the quickest and most efficient ways to evacuate himself. The Anti-Magic Area would be troublesome but he could think of a way around it in a pinch.

He continued to examine the city as he observed the guards. Their strength and competence was something the good Lieutenant would want to know. Gadra also hoped to get information on the military but he was beginning to feel like that may be too much of a risk.

The city's layout was meticulous, the streets forming a network that subtly guided the flow of people and goods. The placement of magical nodes and guard posts was designed not only for efficiency but also for redundancy, ensuring that no area was left vulnerable.

Even with his extensive knowledge of barriers and defenses, Gadra was begrudgingly impressed.

He eventually began making his way back closer to the palace. He wouldn't be getting too close, merely within its line of sight.

His focus sharpened as he neared the outer edges of the palace district. He took care to avoid the eyes of patrolling guards and the occasional hovering surveillance construct. Gadra paused by a market stall to blend into the crowd, pretending to examine an assortment of enchanted trinkets while covertly scanning the palace's defenses.

He noted the layers of protection, physical walls reinforced with runes, magical barriers that shimmered faintly in the air, and concealed sentries who blended seamlessly with their surroundings.

If the reports of Demon Lord Felix's strength were accurate, Gadra suspected that the Daemon needed none of these protections, but it was all about status. What would people think if the Demon Lord had to defend himself?

It would signify massive incompetence among the Demon Lord's guards, that was certain. Emperor Rudra had a similar arrangement, he had four personal guards, each Saints of obscene strength to protect him.

"This is more formidable than I expected." He muttered under his breath. The Empire's intelligence had underestimated Demon Lord Felix's defenses, though that was natural, Kondou had not managed to learn much. He would need to adjust his report accordingly.

Yet even as he observed, the unease returned, stronger this time. He cast a spell to heighten his perception, extending his senses outward in search of the source of his discomfort. The city hummed with life and magic, but nothing stood out as an immediate threat. Still, the feeling persisted, like a predator watching from the shadows.

With his reconnaissance conducted he decided to leave. He wanted to do more originally but he valued his life far more, he could always come back.

For now leaving the capital city of Azeroth was his priority. As he began casually leaving the palace district he once again attempted to expand his senses discreetly. Oftentimes if his instincts were warning him, then that meant something was amiss. He merely needed to figure out what was wrong, the more information he had the more informed of a decision he could make.

He was one of the strongest and most knowledgeable mages in the Cardinal World, there was not much he could handle, but he would rather overreact and be safe than underreact and be in danger.

- Lalatina -

Lalatina's grin widened as she watched Gadra subtly attempt to probe his surroundings. His instincts were sharp, she'd give him that much credit. But no amount of perception-enhancing magic would help him detect her presence. She was just too far above him for anything in his power to be capable of truly affecting her.

She hovered above him, her wings folding slightly as she deliberated. She could reveal herself now, perhaps play the part of an inquisitive local to gauge his intentions more directly. But that would be too easy, and far less entertaining. Besides, she doubted the man would actually tell some random stranger anything worthwhile. He was too old and experienced for that.

She continued to watch as Gadra began discreetly getting further and further away from the palace. He wasn't obvious, he went around to some shops, acted as if he was merely window shopping and he just happened to be getting further away, but she knew that it was all likely an act. It seems that Gadra was satisfied with the information he got.

She blinked as she felt Arcueid and Sukuna teleport in tow to the palace. It seems that things had wrapped up then. Arcueid had left to take care of some of the loose ends like Granbell's allies, though Lalatina wouldn't be surprised if Arcueid did some other things as well on the side.

"Lalatina." Arcueid said through a Thought Communication. "Megumin has already informed me of Gadra's presence, are you tailing him?" Arcueid asked curiously.

"Mhmm. Just watching him for now. He was just looking around, observing the people and the guards. Though it seems he has finished since he's beginning to get further and further away from the palace."

"Is that so? He did not take the proper channels to enter our Lord's territory despite the invitation he had been given. That alone deserves punishment. Are you able to take him in, Lalatina?"

She sighed. "Fine, fine. I wanted to watch him a bit more, see if I could freak him out but I'll deal with him now."

"Thank you." Arcueid said as the Thought Communication between them was ended.

She said she would bring Gadra in, but that didn't mean she wouldn't have some fun with him.

Her World System Skill was completely out of consideration, but she did want to have some more fun with her Ultimate Skill. She hadn't had many chances to use it yet, she had only used it against Arcueid and Megumin so far.

Due to that she felt her mastery over Samael was lacking, Ultimate Skills were instinctively wielded, but to truly master it she would need to practice with it and use it in live combat, especially if she wished to get a bit more creative with its uses.

Her Ultimate Skill was extremely powerful, she needed to gain perfect control over it sooner rather than later if she wished to be of use to her Master.

Even now she could feel the Multi-Dimensional Barrier her Master gifted her, enveloping her entire body.

Lalatina descended silently as her coat flickered in the wind, her presence still concealed. She landed in a shaded alley just ahead of him, folding her wings behind her back. A flick of her hand cloaked her in an unassuming aura, blending her into the surroundings as she stepped out into the bustling street.

She walked directly toward him, her every movement deliberate. Gadra was taking on the form of an old, old man. She didn't doubt that he could change his appearance, if he couldn't after all his so-called experience then he was a failure as a mage. He had long, white hair and a matching beard.

The moment Gadra's eyes met hers, she dropped her concealment, allowing her full power to be perceived by the tiny human.

She had already placed a barrier around them, one that was rather small on the outside but the inside was expanded using Space-Time Manipulation. There were no civilians within the barrier, and those around it wouldn't be affected at all. They wouldn't even know what was happening right next to them.

"Hello there." She said, her voice smooth and honeyed, a hint of amusement laced within.

Gadra immediately stiffened up, she could see the panic in his eyes.

He immediately began casting a teleportation spell, one that was powerful enough that it would tear most Anti-Magic Areas apart allowing the spell to be cast in the first place.

Anti-Magic Area prevented one from manipulating the Laws, but there were ways around this. For one, Anti-Magic Area only worked on the most basic method of Law Manipulation, that being through magicules.

If anyone used a higher form of energy such as spiritrons then it would fail to work, but there were countermeasures for each stage.

The total cast time of Gadra's spell would be less than a second, it was a shame though that she interrupted him using Space-Time Manipulation.

Realizing that his attempt to flee had failed, Gadra stood up straight, his expression betraying only a flicker of surprise before his mask of neutrality returned. "I don't believe we've met." He said carefully, his tone polite but guarded.

Lalatina tilted her head, a coy smile playing on her lips. "Oh, we haven't. But I've been watching you for a while. You're quite the careful one, aren't you?"

Gadra's lips twitched at her confirmation. "So I was being followed."
She could see the tension in his stance.

"Just an interested observer." She continued, stepping closer. "But you're leaving so soon? That's a shame. I thought we could chat a bit. I feel like you might have some information that my Master would love to hear."

Gadra's eyes narrowed. "I have no business here beyond sightseeing. If you'll excuse me—"

Lalatina laughed, the sound echoing with an unnatural edge that seemed to make the air around them vibrate. "Oh, you misunderstand. You do not have a choice in this matter. I am sure that you will serve as an amusing toy." Lalatina giggled maliciously as she stepped forwards.

Gadra's staff appeared within his hand. His instincts must have been screaming at him by now.

Gadra didn't waste a moment. His centuries of survival had most likely taught him the value of swift action in the face of danger. With a quick flourish of his staff, a shimmering dome of light enveloped him, crackling with energy. It was a high level defensive barrier, one that could reflect physical and magical attacks alike.

The Extra Skills Ranged Barrier, and Multilayer Barrier after all weren't the only barrier abilities out there. They were just the most convenient and optimized. Gadra swirled his staff, she could feel the energy around them shifting as Gadra began to cast his spells.

She held out both of her hands as the dual short swords her beloved Master gifted her appeared. She tightly gripped both as she felt her blades respond to her desires. Both had grown stronger from her own Awakening, each having more EP than most Saints.

Gadra used the time he had to begin his attack. Instead, he channeled his energy into the ground, activating a hidden glyph he had placed moments earlier, one that she allowed him to place out of curiosity. A surge of Earth Magic erupted, jagged stone spears shooting toward Lalatina from below.

Her movements were fluid, almost lazy, as she sidestepped the attack with ease. One blade flicked out, cleaving through the magic-infused stone as though it were paper. The other sword danced in her grip, catching a secondary wave of magical energy Gadra had layered into the attack.

It was dismantled effortlessly. It was strong, don't get her wrong, it was complex enough to catch even a powerful Enlightened and weaker Saint off guard due to how the attack was layered, but it just wasn't enough to deal with someone of her caliber.

"Cute." She remarked as she flourished her twin swords. Her Weakness Identification sub-skill had already pinged many of Gadra's supposed weaknesses.

It seems Gadra's soul was not quite damaged but it was not healthy, likely due to his repeated reincarnations. Something like that could be exploited by her poison with ease. She could easily create a poison tailor made to kill Gadra in particular now if she wished to do so.

Her twin swords glimmered as she began using Death Poison Refining, coating them in a poison that was especially made to take advantage of that weakness of Gadra's, though this one wouldn't kill him, merely put him in an artificial coma only she could wake him from.

Gadra didn't stop trying to attack her as he levitated himself into the air. She felt the shift in the air, a surge of spiritrons that were focused on the focal point above his staff.

The street seemed to dim as his spell took form, shadows stretching unnaturally while a fiery orb materialized, burning with a brilliance that rivaled the sun. She raised a brow, she was impressed with his attack.

Even now the effects of his spell could be felt and he hadn't even sent it at her. The surrounding temperatures increased drastically. The enchanted cobblestone beneath their feet began to crack and glow faintly red, unable to withstand the sheer intensity of the heat radiating from the orb. The enchanted wooden signposts along the street warped and smoldered, their edges curling as faint trails of smoke rose into the air. Glass windows in the nearby buildings fogged over before shattering under the rapid expansion and contraction of the heat's pressure.

The tendrils of flame flicked outward, searing through the air with a hiss, leaving lingering trails of heat that shimmered in their wake.

Though her Multi-Dimensional Barrier protected her from all the effects, not that she even needed her barrier to deal with it. Temperature of this level was far from enough to inconvenience her. Though she'd need to get someone to fix the mess Gadra was making. At least there were no civilians around, they were still going about their days outside of her barrier not realizing what was happening next to them.

"Impressive. For a mortal." She remarked with a cocky grin.

Gadra's eyes narrowed, sweat dripping down his brow despite his protective spells. The fiery orb continued to grow, its brilliance now near-blinding as it prepared to unleash its devastating energy.

Lalatina tilted her head, observing with a detached curiosity. She could sense his desperation in the way the spiritrons swirled chaotically around him. This was quite literally an all or nothing play for Gadra. It seems he rated her threat level rather highly and wished to not have a prolonged encounter with her.

Gadra's spell swirled above his staff as it slowly began destabilizing due to how long Gadra was taking in deploying it. "I know not your name." Gadra stated. "But hear me, I will unleash this catastrophe right here in the middle of this city if it ensures my survival." Gadra said with a grim smile. "No barrier can last against something of this caliber. However, should you allow me to leave, I will contain this spell."
She raised a brow at Gadra's certainty. Because she was sure that her barrier would last against Gadra's spell. She shrugged, she wouldn't be telling him just how wrong she was.

She blatantly yawned, cutting Gadra's words short. "Hurry up, I'll give you one shot before I have my turn." She said, treating it as if it were a game.

Gadra sighed. "Very well. Do not blame me for this."

She stored her twin blades in her Spatial Storage as she stood on top of Gadra. After he deployed his spell, unsurprisingly her barrier held up. Though all of the land within the barrier was scorched to smithereens.

Oops.

After using his spell Gadra got even more desperate, he was low on internal energy so she had an even easier time than she would have before. She didn't even really get to use Samael on him that much since he was that weak. He wasn't worthy of her Ultimate Skill, it was her mistake to think she would be able to learn a thing or two from this fight.

"Arcueid." She said through a Thought Communication.

"Are you done with your games?" Arcueid said in a fed up tone of voice.

It didn't surprise her whatsoever that Arcueid knew what she was doing. She took her job as her Lord's regent very seriously.

"Yup! He was weaker than I thought he would be."

"Hmm, I will keep that in mind then. I will send Sukuna to pick Gadra up." Sukuna was always really obedient to those stronger than him. He may have been one of the Seven Demonic Lords under her Master, but he knew his place.

"Mkay, by the way make sure to send someone to clean the area up."

Arcueid audibly sighed through the Thought Communication. "How much will need to be rebuilt?"

A sheepish smile grew on her face. "All of it? But it's Gadra's fault! No one asked him to throw a miniature sun at me!"

"Very well then. I will have the civilians in the area escorted away. Once that is done please dispel your barrier."

"Got it!"

While she waited she floated around as she kicked her legs back and forth. Before long she felt Sukuna's arrival outside of her barrier. She felt his incoming Thought Communication. "Would you mind dispelling your barrier, Lady Lalatina?" Sukuna requested.

Sukuna was a real formal guy surprisingly, at least he was to those that were stronger than him. Sukuna lived on the same mindset that almost all Daemons did. Those who were strong were right, and those who were weak deserved everything that happened to them. It was a simple and cruel mindset, but it was one many shared.

According to her Master he was rather similar even in his previous world, though in her Master's own words, Sukuna was more "unhinged". Her Master defeated Sukuna and then remade Sukuna in his image.

Ever since then Sukuna had always been trying to get stronger, perhaps it was an old holdover from his previous life, perhaps he merely wanted to be useful, but Lalatina was still interested in him nonetheless. He was stronger than almost every single Daemon in existence, when there were billions upon billions of them that was an impressive feat.

Not to mention his World System Skill was something she was interested in, that was before she acquired her own World System Skill.

Though one thing about Sukuna that she had noticed was an internal sort of conflict within. Her Master had told her about his story and how he was recruited, and Lalatina could only assume it was a small hold over from his previous life.

She shook her head, she was getting distracted. "It's dispelling now." Lalatina responded before cutting the Thought Communication.

The citizens had already been moved out according to her senses. Most of the people who resided here were aware that there would be times where they were expected to comply with the orders of her Master's representatives. It was only natural to follow the words of the Demon Lord who ruled the lands you called home.

Within moments Sukuna appeared in front of her, his hands clasped firmly behind his back. A look of scorn appeared on Sukuna's face as he took in the sight of the fallen Gadra. "This is him then? I must say, he seems rather disappointing."

Lalatina shrugged. "Maybe compared to the people you associate with, but in this world few would be able to match him."

She knew full well how abnormal the people she associated with were. Even the weakest of her Master's direct subordinates were capable of fighting Saints who were at around 0.000~1% of the population.

Even Sukuna could fight at that level, he may not have had the same raw power as most Saints had, but his Unique Skill and technique could help bridge the gap somewhat.

"Hmm, I suppose you are right." Sukuna conceded.

While he was here she decided to hear more about the overall situation, Sukuna was with Arcueid so he should know more.

"So how'd things go with the Council of the West?" She asked.

An evil grin grew on Sukuna's face. "Everything went as it should. Those weak Humans fell in line quickly and now live and serve at Lord Felix's whims."

She blinked in confusion before just writing it off as Arcueid being an overachiever. She didn't think her Master had once told Arcueid to try and gain control over the Western Council.

Though he didn't say anything about taking over the Free Guild either. She pouted as she realized that if she didn't do something Arcueid would surpass her in the race!

The race to what one may ask? Well Lalatina didn't know, but she didn't want to lose!

"And what about the attack on Ruberious?" She asked with interest.

"The attack was truly quite something, the amount of force present in one city was more than I could have understood in the past." Sukuna said with a dreamy sigh.

Sukuna went on to tell her about what happened in Lune while she was busy playing spy.

Apparently some Monsters were causing trouble, someone tamed them and set them loose on Lune. Even an Arch Dragon was tamed according to Sukuna, though right after he went on to say how disappointing the Dragon was in battle.

In reality even an Arch Daemon would likely lose against an Arch Dragon of the caliber that Sukuna described.

It went to show just how special her Master was to recruit such powerful beings with ease. Even his older subordinates were shaping up to be powerhouses.

Saeko and Raiden were swiftly catching up to her in power before she became a Devil Lord, while Kurumi was just a little bit further behind.

Ingvild did not like combat much so she was lagging behind, but even she was capable of fighting Moss to a draw, who was once the strongest Daemon under the Primordials.

After dealing with the Arch Dragon Sukuna met up with Kurumi and then her Master. It seems Hinata was fighting with Granbell. She would have to pay Hinata a visit sometime.

Lalatina didn't forget how Hinata had blocked her way when she had gone to Ruberious to have fun with Luminous. Back then she was restricted by the world so she could only use the power of an Arch Daemon leading to her defeat.

After that Sukuna was sent to support Arcueid who was taking control over the Western Council. It seems everything worked out perfectly.

"I see." She hummed to Sukuna.

"If that is all I will take this man to Lady Arcueid then." Sukuna said as he picked Gadra up.

Lalatina waved him along. "Feel free."
With that Sukuna vanished, teleporting away.

Story: I'm a Daemon, so what?
