Chapter 114: Reverse Jumping in The Dungeon!

- Shinji Tanimura -

The oppressive stillness of The Dungeon's air was unnerving. Shinji glanced over at his comrades, Shin and Mark, as they pressed forward cautiously through the narrow corridor. The eerie quiet was broken only by the faint crackle of the torches lining the walls.

This Rimuru guy seriously knew what he was doing when he designed this place. Shinji was getting more and more sure that either the Demon Lord himself was an otherworlder, or at the very least an otherworlder helped design The Dungeon. Many of the traps were textbook examples from the MMOs he used to play.

There were even a few easter eggs referencing pop culture from Earth; things only a fellow otherworlder would recognize. Just a few floors ago, they had come across a mural depicting what was unmistakably the One Ring from The Lord of the Rings. Shinji had nearly laughed out loud when he saw the inscription, though Mark and Shin had only given him puzzled looks. Both were rather uncultured on that, front it seemed, Shinji expected Shin's ignorance, but as an American, Mark's was a surprise.

Another room had featured a trap where they had to step on tiles to recreate a sequence. The sequence? The opening notes of the Super Mario Bros. theme. The fact that incorrect steps triggered a barrage of fireballs only made it feel more authentic.

"Seriously," Shinji muttered under his breath. "If the next room has a puzzle involving Tetris blocks, I'm calling it."

"Calling what?" Mark asked, his voice breaking the silence.

"Nothing." Shinji said with a shake of his head. He didn't want to jinx anything. He knew full well that the power of Murphy was everywhere.

All of a sudden Shin stiffened. "There's a powerful monster approaching, fast." Shin said as his hand quickly traveled to the hilt of his blade.

Shin's Unique Skill: Perceiver allowed him many detection abilities as well as other similar abilities. They were close comrades, so they trusted one another with the details of their Skills.

The Unique Skill: Perceiver was rather powerful in that it had multiple sub-skills, a rarity among Unique Skills. There was Instinct Evasion, which allowed Shin to hide from one's instincts, which made Shin a truly excellent assassin.

Then there was Danger Detection, which allowed Shin to sense any nearby danger with supernatural instinct. Trap and Monster Detection were rather self explanatory. Then there was Presence Detection, which allowed Shin to also sense Majin and Humans alike.

Perceiver made Shin the ideal scout, and it played a big part in why Shin was able to rise up in the Imperial Guardians so rapidly. Many of the higher ups took notice of such a useful Skill and worked to get Shin on their side. Shin had taken part in many espionage operations in the past. He has played a major part in conquering some of the kingdoms that are now part of the Eastern Empire.

So when Shin warned them of an incoming danger, they took him seriously.

But before Shinji could fully process Shin's warning, the monster burst from the darkness. Its movements were chaotic, flickering through the torchlight like an afterimage, the sharp edges of its shadowy limbs seemed to be able to slice through practically anything

Mark reacted first, his Thrower skill activating as he grabbed a chunk of rubble and hurling it at the monster with incredible accuracy. The stone flew with the force of a cannonball, aimed directly at the monster's chest. But before it could connect, the being contorted in the air, evading the attack with a sickeningly unnatural fluidity.

"Ugh what a pain."

Mark's Unique Skill: Thrower allowed him to throw anything as long as it's graspable, even a Monster or air itself. It was simple but useful in application, and it suited a brawn over brains type like Mark.

Mark was already prepared for the monster's avoidance. "Boomerang!" He yelled as the brick ricocheted off one of the walls of The Dungeon, smashing into the monster.

Yelling your attack name was unneeded, but it helped you focus and visualize the attack itself making the attack far more natural and instinctive.

The monster staggered, but the attack didn't seem to have done much to the monster. It lunged for Shin, perhaps sensing the danger Perceiver posed to it in its ambush.

Shinji was rather curious about the monster that had attacked him. He had overheard a few adventurers talking about a group of menacing monsters that would ambush adventurers in The Dungeon.

There was a shadowy monster, a pink imp, a skeletal warrior, a living armor, and a ghost mage. This group of monsters was responsible for the deaths of many adventurers, but Shinji never heard about the shadowy monster being powerful enough to contend against Enlightened like them for even a few moments.

The methods the group of monsters used against other adventurers was mostly trickery rather than raw power, yet it seemed to possess a fair amount of raw power. Why had it been holding back on the others? Something about the entire situation seemed off to him.

Shin's blade flashed as he moved, his blade cut through the air, deflecting the creature's strikes with relative ease. The attack was rather mechanical, if you asked Shinji, as if it was somehow programmed into the monster. It didn't seem to have a light of intelligence in its eyes, but it was still skilled and powerful.

It was most definitely a unique monster, as Shinji had never heard of such a monster existing. It was easily higher than an A Class threat, not due to its overall meager energy, but due to its wide scope of abilities it had already demonstrated and relatively mechanical skill.

The monster hissed as its shadowy body flickered. If Shinji were in a joking mood he'd comment about how chunni the monster they were fighting was. It was made out of shadows, seriously?

He blinked in confusion as the monster split into two, one seemed to be a shadowy illusion while the other was the real one.

"That's annoying!" Mark yelled, grabbing a handful of rubble. "I hate when bosses have add-ons!" He hurled the debris, forcing the now two monsters to scatter as they narrowly avoided his attacks.

Shinji was rather surprised that he had a hard time perceiving which one was real and which one was the illusion. He was no master mage, but he had a fair amount of experience and should normally be able to feel the magicules in the illusion, yet he could feel nothing.

Perhaps The Dungeon was protecting the monster to a certain extent?

Shinji stepped back, his mind racing. "Alright, my turn." He muttered, his hands glowing faintly as he activated his Unique Skill. His viral cloud expanded invisibly, spreading across the battlefield, he made sure his allies were not affected by the virus he spread.

His Unique Skill: Healer was one of the most terrifying Skills that existed, at least according to Yuuki. Healer allows him to manipulate viruses, it is simple, but could be overwhelming if used properly and with care. He could manipulate the air composition to spread viral poison, making him nigh-invincible against living creatures.

Of course, it could also be used to heal others just as it could be used to kill others.

He could wipe out entire kingdoms within days with his Unique Skill by spreading a virus. Of course, Healer was less effective the stronger his target was as Spiritual and Demi-Spiritual Lifeforms wouldn't be as severely affected by a mortal plague.

Still, his Unique Skill: Healer was a truly absurd power. According to Master Gadra, even Emperor Rudra was intrigued by it and had hypothesized that if Shinji managed to surpass his limits, he could create viruses capable of affecting even Spiritual Lifeforms.

The monster in front of him was no Demi-Spiritual Lifeform, let alone Spiritual Lifeform, yet it seemed to be resisting the virus somehow. Shinji could feel it affecting the creature, just not as much as he expected it to.

The virus he released was spread through the air and was meant to cause the magicules in one's body to go haywire. He was indeed capable of creating viruses that could cause supernatural illnesses as well.

The monster's movements began to slow as his viral poison began to take effect, within moments the illusion dissipated as it couldn't maintain itself leaving just their main target.

"Nice!" Mark cheered, launching another barrage of projectiles.

Mark's Unique Skill was simple, but it had tremendous potential. For now he could only throw material things and some immaterial things such as air. However, Shinji theorized that eventually, if Mark made a breakthrough, he could grow to throw other more esoteric forces such as gravity, or even space itself.

Shin cursed under his breath. "This thing's more than just fast; it's learning." He glanced at Shinji. "Can you keep it slowed?"

"I'll try." Shinji replied. He shifted tactics, altering the composition of the viral cloud to focus on paralysis.

The monster charged him, likely sensing that he was the source of the poison. Shin intercepted it mid-strike, his blade flashing as he parried and countered in a fluid motion.

Mark leapt forward; his hands glowing as he grabbed the air itself. With a grunt, he hurled an invisible mass directly at the creature. The impact sent shockwaves rippling through the corridor, forcing the monster to retreat momentarily.

Despite how well the battle was going, Shinji couldn't shake off the feeling that something wasn't right.

"Guys!" Shin called out. "I think it's holding back! My Danger Detection wouldn't be flaring up as much as it is if this is all the monster is capable of." Shin said as he gripped his weapon tightly.

"Just how strong do you think it is?" He asked, Shin had the experience to hopefully tell the threat level just from the feeling of danger he was getting.

Shin paused for a moment before answering. "The closest approximation I can place it at is… is at the level of Davis." Shin said with slight fear.

Shinji's eyes widened hearing that.

"For real!?" Mark yelled.

Davis was an Enlightened just like them, but the difference between them was vast. Davis was one of the ones responsible for sealing and defeating Blanc in the first place. He was Imperial Guardian #11 and served as an assistant to the Double 0 Numbers.

"We might be cooked." Mark mumbled.

Shinji shook his head. "Focus!"

This information alone would likely warrant them some merits back in the Eastern Empire. For The Dungeon to have monsters capable of fighting one of the strongest Imperial Guardians would be very troublesome for the Generals.

In front of their eyes, the monster's body began to shift form, the flickering shadow form started to solidify, and sharp, jagged edges extended from its limbs. It was as if it turned itself into one living weapon. Shinji would be fascinated if he wasn't so worried.

The creature lunged at Mark with speeds greater than what it had showed off so far. Mark barely had time to react, throwing a chunk of air at point-blank range. The attack connected, but the monster absorbed the impact, barely sliding back before sending a retaliatory attack with its claws.

"Get back!" Shin yelled, intercepting the monster mid-strike. His blade clashed against the creature's limb, sparks flying as their energies collided.

Shinji extended his hand, releasing a concentrated viral burst aimed directly at the creature's core. The air shimmered with the invisible poison, and the monster faltered for a moment before its form twisted unnaturally.

The monster staggered backwards as his virus began to take effect. Its movements were slowing and it seemed to be getting a bit more sluggish.

"Nice work, Shinji!" Mark grinned as he hurled another chunk of debris, the projectile smashing into the monster's shoulder. The force caused it to stumble, but not falter.

Within moments, the monster managed to recover somewhat, though there was still some sluggishness in its movement.

In the blink of an eye, it blitzed towards Shin who was closest to it. Its speed was such that the three of them could barely even react. They felt the shockwave of the sonic boom it left behind travel through them as he and Mark rushed to Shin's aid.

"Shit!" Shin yelled as he attempted to get out of the way. Shinji and Mark had both dashed forwards to try to cover Shin.

Mark raised his Unique Grade axe as he sent a slash of Fighting Spirit towards the monster.

Just as the slash was about to hit the monster, the creature's form seemed to almost twist unnaturally as its shadowy limbs elongated. The creature sliced its hand downwards in a cutting motion. Shinji felt all his instincts warn him of the attack the creature had sent.

Shinji's heart sank as he saw and felt the deadly precision and sheer power of the invisible slash the creature sent towards Shin.

When the fight first started, Shinji had quickly attempted to understand how strong the creature was. It had less energy than all three of them, and so Shinji was confident they would win. They were each bonafide, experienced Enlightened, yet it seems he had made a mistake.

Shinji sent a burst of poison towards the monster in the hopes of it managing to weaken the monster enough for Shin to manage to avoid the attack. He closed his eyes as he put a vast amount of his energy into the attack he sent towards the creature.

The creature staggered backward, its form twisting unnaturally. For a moment, Shinji thought the viral poison had finally taken a meaningful toll on the monster. But then, the air grew thick with an ominous pressure, and the shadowy figure began to shift. Its jagged edges shimmered, and a sharp, eerie hum filled the corridor.

Shin had managed to avoid the attack, but he had a feeling that maybe they were screwed either way.

The monster clearly wasn't intelligent, but there was some strategy within its head; some methods to its madness making it far harder to deal with than a normal monster as most lacked any semblance of intelligence.

"What's it doing?" Mark muttered, his voice tense as he gripped his axe tightly.

Without warning, the creature sprang into motion. It skittered across the walls and ceiling with unnatural speed, its jagged limbs clicking against the stone. One moment it was on the floor; the next, it was darting behind Shin, its movements too erratic to predict.

Shinji could barely trace its movements, and even then he could only keep pace with its afterimages. The creature was managing to move faster than he, an experienced Enlightened, could fully perceive.

Shin quickly fended off the monster's attacks. The moment Shin defended the creature would retreat, hopping from surface to surface making it impossible for them to land a solid hit on it. It was a master of using the environment against them.

The creature hissed, its shadowy form flickering as it poised for another attack. Shinji tightened his grip on his weapon, his eyes darting to Shin and Mark. They were still holding their ground, but the monster's movements were becoming harder to track.

"Keep your eyes on it!" Shinji shouted, his voice tense.

"I'm trying!" Mark growled, hurling another burst of projectiles. The creature dodged effortlessly, its form a blur as it twisted and leapt. The projectiles struck the walls, sending shards of debris raining down, but the creature was already elsewhere. He was sure that from an outside perspective, their fight looked right out of an anime, and was suitably badass. Perhaps he'd be enjoying himself more if he didn't feel like he was about to die.

Shinji barely had time to react as the monster lunged at him, its claw-like limb slashing downward. He twisted out of the way, but the attack sheared through the floor, leaving a gaping, smoldering gouge where he'd been standing.

"That thing's cutting through magicule infused material like butter." Shin gasped, clutching his side.

"It feels like it's playing with us." Mark muttered, his voice filled with frustration.

Shinji nodded in agreement. The longer the fight went on, the more abilities and power the monster revealed. It was sandbagging against them, hard.

With a guttural roar, the monster's jagged appendages struck the ground, creating a shockwave that rippled outward. The torches flickered violently, plunging the room into darkness. Shinji, Shin, and Mark struggled to maintain their footing as the ground beneath them trembled.

"Stay on your toes!" Shin barked, his blade poised.

Mark braced himself, but the monster was already moving. It blurred forward, its speed doubling. Mark swung with a chunk of rubble enhanced by Thrower, but the creature anticipated the attack, sidestepping and delivering a bone-crushing blow to his side. Mark slammed into the wall, groaning in pain.

"Mark!" Shinji shouted, but he had no time to assist as the monster pivoted, lunging for him next.

Shinji instinctively used one of the defensive applications of his Unique Skill, creating a viral barrier around himself. The barrier shimmered faintly, a deadly cloud meant to disintegrate anything organic or magical that came into contact with it. The monster slammed into it but barely faltered, its shadowy form resisting the viral decomposition with an unnatural resilience.

"This thing's insane!" Shinji cursed, his mind racing. He had killed other Enlightened with the barrier he created around him.

Shin darted in, his blade aiming for the creature's core, but the monster's reflexes were far superior. It twisted mid-air, deflecting the blade with its jagged limb, and retaliated with a slash that Shin narrowly avoided.

The creature quickly hopped to a wall. Crouched low, its glowing limbs poised like blades. Then it launched itself toward Shin once again with terrifying speed. He brought up his blade just in time to parry, but the force of the collision sent him sprawling. The creature didn't pause. It darted away, bouncing between walls like a chaotic pinball before lunging at Mark.

Mark threw up a makeshift barrier of compressed air as he had recovered from the monster's initial blow, but the creature's strike ripped through it as if it weren't there. It struck him in the chest, a sonic boom echoed the surroundings as Mark was sent crashing into the wall, again.

"Shit!" Shinji cursed as he quickly thought up a new attack to use on the spot. The viral cloud around the battlefield shifted, condensing into razor-thin strands of airborne contagion. "If it can't be slowed, I'll cut it to pieces!"

The viral strands slashed at the monster, slicing through its shadowy form. For a moment, it staggered, as though caught off guard. But the monster roared, its form solidifying further to repel the attacks. The strands were losing their efficiency with every second.

Shinji grit his teeth as he rapidly went through various plans in his head. He knew that they would respawn if they died, but he wouldn't leave his fate in the hands of The Dungeon if he didn't have to. Not to mention the fact that he was very concerned that they were attacked by such a powerful monster when they were only a little over half way through The Dungeon. Going by the way The Dungeon had scaled so far, it made no sense that they were attacked by such a strong Monster so soon.

Something like that happening only meant one thing: someone had deliberately sent the monster to them. Who could hope to command the monsters in The Dungeon except the higher ups of Tempest?

Shinji seriously did not want to stick around. He really should have trusted his instincts.

Shin growled in frustration. "It's too strong! If it's at Davis's level, we're just bugs to it!"

Mark, clutching his side, staggered back to his feet. "Then we've got to fight dirty." His eyes gleamed with determination as he reached into his pouch and pulled out an enchanted crystal. It was an artifact that Mark brought from the Eastern Empire. A one time use kind of thing. "Shinji, Shin, cover me!"

The monster seemed to sense the danger, its glowing eyes narrowing as it turned its full attention to Mark. Before it could act, Shin moved; his blade flashing in rapid arcs to intercept the monster's advance. Despite his best efforts, the creature battered through his defenses, forcing him to retreat with a deep gash across his arm.

Shinji could feel the hope bloom in his chest. They had a chance. If they made it out of this okay, he was totally going on a vacation! This was all way too much for him.

He unleashed another wave of viral constructs, this time focusing on its sensory perception. The air around the monster shimmered as the constructs distorted light and sound, creating a barrage of illusions.

Mark gritted his teeth, the crystal in his hand humming with raw power. "You want some of this, you overgrown shadow?" He growled, activating the artifact. He hurled it with all his might, the crystal glowing brighter as it arced toward the monster.

The explosion was blinding, a massive detonation that shook the entire floor of the dungeon. Dust and debris filled the air, and for a moment, there was silence.

But as the smoke cleared, their hearts sank.

The monster stood in the center of the blast zone. Oh it was wounded for sure, but it had somehow managed to evade the worst of the explosion. No it hadn't evaded, it was just regenerating from the wounds it was dealt.

Mark slumped against the wall, his face pale. "No way…"

The monster roared, its body radiating pure malice. It surged forward with a speed that none of them could follow, striking Shinji first. The viral barrier around him shattered under the force of the attack, and he was sent flying into a pile of rubble.

"Shinji!" Shin yelled. His vision was blurry but he could make out the figure of the monster raising his arm in Shin's direction before lowering it in a slicing motion. He felt the magicules around him fluctuate, and then within a moment he heard Shin's scream.

"Gah!"

Before he managed to lose consciousness he could see Shin's arm slide off his shoulder, crashing onto the floor below.

It was then that he realized that there was no hope from the beginning.

The last thing he heard was Mark's roar of rage before he lost consciousness.

- Chloe Aubert -

She tilted her head as she observed the fight between the Shadow Dancer and the group of spies. It was wrapping up now. One was unconscious, another was on the verge of collapsing and had lost an arm, and then the last was charging forth like a berserker.

The results of the fight were as she expected them to be, though the process was a bit different than she expected. She expected the Shadow Dancer to beat them up in the familiar reverse jumping pattern. It had been told to hold back, of course, so the three could be tested and they could get a better idea of their abilities, but they still put up more of a fight than she thought they would.

She supposed it was her own fault for underestimating someone in the Eastern Empire military, though to be fair, she didn't expect even the Enlightened to be a bit special.

All three of their Unique Skills were rather interesting. The virus one was especially dangerous. If Chronoa's theory was right, then his Unique Skill was the most dangerous of the bunch.

The three had fought rather well, each demonstrating some excellent combat skills and techniques that would have them revered as Champions in the Western Nations. Though to be fair, the West was sorely lacking in the Champion department. Anyone of sufficient skill and a shown tendency to help Humans in some way would be called as such.

She watched as Felix-nii's Shadow Dancer hopped from surface to surface, avoiding Mark's barrage of attacks. The guy seemed to really be getting desperate now, both of his allies were incapacitated, it seemed he realized that there was something off about the situation.

"Rah!" Mark yelled as he pulled his arm back, throwing the Unique Grade axe he got at the Shadow Dancer. The sound barrier was breached instantly, though the shockwaves of the sonic boom were absorbed by The Dungeon.

As for the axe, it whizzed through the air like a comet; the pressure from its flight distorting the surrounding space. The Shadow Dancer, nimble and unflinching, shifted its position with fluid grace. The axe missed its mark by mere inches, embedding itself deep into The Dungeon's wall with a thunderous crash.

"Incredible." Beretta muttered with awe in her voice.

Ramiris had arrived in the midst of the fight and was sitting on Beretta's head. "Felix's Avatar is pretty strong, but I'd solo him!" The Pixie said as she began shadowboxing around Beretta's head. "My Avatar is leagues stronger too!" Ramiris added.

Chloe's lips quirked up in amusement. It was pretty funny that Ramiris's Avatar had more EP than the current incarnation of Ramiris herself.

Mark's desperation reached its zenith as his breathing grew ragged. His eyes, now a mix of determination and fear, burned with a primal desire to overcome the odds, she had seen it in others in the past. He sprinted toward the Shadow Dancer, drawing on every ounce of his remaining strength.

She watched with interest as he pushed beyond his limits, Plus Ultra as Felix-nii liked to say sometimes. Through the projection she could see Mark pushing his Unique Skill past its limits. Skills often responded to the desires of their users, in the current situation Mark was rather desperate. In his mind he and his friends would likely be doomed if he lost here now, she doubted he was thinking much further than that, like how they could get out.

As Mark rushed towards the Shadow Dancer, he reached out in the same fashion he used to grip the air, except this time he gripped something else. She watched as Mark managed to grip space itself, condensing it into a ball, before throwing it at the Shadow Dancer at speeds surpassing that of sound.

The orb of compressed space shot forward; the air around it warping and shimmering violently. The force of its movement sent shockwaves throughout the Dungeon; the walls groaning under the strain of Mark's desperation-fueled attack.

The Shadow Dancer didn't flinch. Its unreadable form stood poised, as though waiting for this very moment. Shadows coiled tighter around it, and its eyes glinted. With a deft and familiar motion, it raised one hand and sliced downwards.

"Is that?" Beretta asked.

Ramiris nodded. "Ooh! That's Dismantle, I think, right?"

Veldora nodded. "Indeed! Cleave requires direct contact to be used, so it must have used Dismantle!"

The orb of compressed space unraveled mid-flight. The once-deadly sphere dissipated into harmless particles; the distortions vanishing in an instant. Mark staggered as the feedback from his failed attack slammed into him, nearly driving him to his knees. His energy reserves were practically exhausted now. While the Shadow Dancer had less reserves than Mark, it excelled at making the most of the limited energy it had. It was likely a carryover from Felix-nii, since he was rather energy efficient as well.

The Shadow Dancer, it seemed, had enough as it blitzed forwards at speeds the naked eye could not observe. In the blink of an eye the Shadow Dancer closed the distance between itself and Mark. Its movements were a seamless blend of fluid grace, reminiscent of Felix-nii's battle style, but not quite as refined. Mark barely had time to react, raising his arms in a feeble attempt to block the incoming assault.

The Shadow Dancer sent a single, fluid motion targeting his midsection. The impact was surgical, delivering just enough force to incapacitate without causing severe harm. Mark crumpled to the ground, his energy utterly spent. His body hit The Dungeon floor with a dull thud.

The Shadow Dancer didn't linger or show any sign of acknowledgment toward its fallen opponent. It pivoted sharply and retreated into the shadows, its form dissolving as though it had never existed.

It finished its orders, and so it was done. It had no real personality that would allow it to bask in its victory or anything. In the end, it was just a vessel for Felix-nii when he wanted to play around a bit. It had no autonomy. All of its actions were due to the extremely advanced orders programmed into it that allowed it to give off a semblance of sentience.

She heard Beretta sigh from behind her. "It is finally over then."

Beretta was always a real worry wart. Beretta already had taken many precautions to make sure that the three didn't escape despite that being basically impossible, but when you had to take care of someone as whimsical as Ramiris, then perhaps it was only expected.

Veldora yawned as he leaned back against his chair. "That was more boring than I thought it would be."
Ramiris fluttered around Beretta, clearly less impressed. "It wasn't even close! That Shadow Dancer barely broke a sweat. What's so great about these guys anyway? I bet I could beat them up easy!"

Chloe rolled her eyes at Ramiris theatrics. While the three chatted with each other, Chloe thought about Hinata. Through the soul connection she shared with Hinata, she could feel that Hinata had managed to Awaken as a True Hero. Chloe wasn't quite sure how since, as far as she knew, Ramiris hadn't helped Hinata get another Hero's Egg, but she was still glad that it all worked out in the end.

She had been feeling guilty that she inadvertently snatched away Hinata's opportunity to grow into a True Hero and had planned to ask Ramiris to help Hinata out later, but it seems that wasn't needed.

With Hinata becoming a True Hero, she was sure that she had grown a lot more powerful. Especially considering the fact that Hinata was already a Divine Human before even Awakening as a True Hero.

They had hung out a bit after Hinata evolved here and there, but both of them were rather busy. Still, they managed to make time to hang out as friends with Luminous. It was then that she learned Hinata had acquired an Ultimate Skill which was impressive.

With Hinata's Awakening, her EP must have multiplied. It wouldn't be on her own level, as she was an abnormality. She was self aware enough to know that. Awakening two Hero's Eggs was practically unfair and almost immediately threw her into the same league as True Dragons when it came to raw power. Still, she imagined that Hinata would be quite up there in power now.

"I attempted to reach out through the soul connection, but was rebuffed by something."

Chloe blinked in confusion as she took in Chronoa's words.

'Just who managed to block you?'

"I have no idea. However, I have some guesses." Chronoa said vaguely.

Chloe shrugged. She'd leave all that stuff to Chronoa. That was what she was there for, after all.

"I'm truly feeling your love…"

All of a sudden she froze as a smile formed on her face.

"Oho! It seems my brother is back!" Veldora said with a boisterous laugh.

It hadn't been that long since Rimuru had left for the meeting with the Council of the West. He had taken Benimaru and Souei with him, and now all three of them were back. Rimuru was already teleporting right to them. He was probably informed about what was happening by one of his subordinates that was meant to keep an eye on things. Since Souei was gone, it was probably that girl with a crush on Souei, Souka was her name.

After a moment, Rimuru appeared in front of them. "Guys? What the hell happened!?" He asked. "Souka said there were enemies of some kind in The Dungeon, and that you were handling them. Chloe?" He said as he looked right at her.
Before she could respond Rimuru grumbled. "Ugh, why does all of this have to be happening at once, right after the attack on Ruberious too…"

She blinked as she took in what Rimuru had said. "So it really happened?"

Chronoa had already predicted that the attack would happen when Rimuru went to meet with the Council of the West. The situation was the best it would be, and Granbell was one who would take advantage of the timing to launch the attack. Chronoa expected for there to be an attack on the Council as well to keep Rimuru busy, leaving Luminous and Ruberious with fewer allies he'd have to deal with in the short term.

Of course she was still confident that everything would turn out okay. She didn't believe that Granbell had access to anything that could cause Benimaru and Souei together much trouble, let alone if Rimuru himself was present. Luminous could also handle herself, Chloe knew full well that much

Rimuru sighed. "Yeah, Granbell attacked Ruberious with his allies, but it's been dealt with now."

Veldora snorted. "I bet if I was there, there would have been no attack at all! My magnificent presence would send them all away."

Chloe tilted her head. "You know, that's probably true."

Veldora preened. "See, she gets it!"

Rimuru rolled his eyes. "That would be a bad thing, you know? Then we wouldn't know when they would attack next." Rimuru said with a sigh. "The meeting with the Council of the West was attacked as well."

Chloe nodded, she had expected it after all.

"Wait, don't change the subject!" Rimuru said after a moment. "What happened here?"
She took the initiative to explain what was going on. She told him about her random meeting with the three spies and how she felt they were all Enlightened, which on its own wasn't that unusual in a growing city like Tempest, but they seemed different from the rest. Her instincts warned her that they were up to no good.

So she told Veldora about them and they came up with a plan to capture them and test their abilities so that they could have a better picture of what the three were capable of.

To do so, they got Felix-nii's Avatar to test them in a fight in The Dungeon.

Rimuru sighed as he ran a hand through his hair. "I suppose you all didn't act that recklessly."

Beretta looked at Rimuru in betrayal, as if she expected him to be the voice of reason.

Rimuru turned away from Beretta's betrayed look. "Did you guys retrieve the three then?"

Before she could answer Treyni entered the room with the three spies in tow. They were being transported by roots that ran along the floor.

"Ah, thanks Treyni!" Rimuru said as he looked over the three before wincing.

Treyni bowed. "It was my pleasure." She said before vanishing in a swirl of leaves.

"Felix's Avatar really did a number on these three." Rimuru said as he walked closer to them.

Veldora nodded. "It was an excellent battle. Sukuna would be impressed with the efficiency that the Shadow Dancer made use of with his abilities." Veldora praised.

"If you're done with your glazing session, could you tell me where Dino and Vesta are?" Rimuru said as he gestured to Beretta to handle the three spies. They'd probably be healed and everything before being forcefully awoken and questioned.

Ramiris flew closer to Rimuru. "They're taking a break today!"

Rimuru nodded. "I'll have to give them those Daemon things later then."

Daemon things? She shrugged, it wasn't any of her business.

Now that Rimuru was here and had dealt with the biggest upcoming thing that he had to deal with, maybe she could finally ask him for a date.

As she opened her mouth she was interrupted by space warping and Felix-nii appearing. The glare she sent at Felix-nii could have killed.

"Yo Rimuru!" Felix-nii waved before looking at her weirdly before shaking his head. "Sup Veldora, Ramiris, and Chloe." He said, brushing off her glare completely.

Rimuru raised his hand. "Yo, Felix. I wasn't expecting you."

"After you left some things happened, I thought I should fill you in."

Rimuru blinked. "Oh? Like what?"

"Well for starters Hinata and Guy fought."

She found herself freezing at Felix's words.

"What!?" Rimuru yelled, she was feeling something similar.

Chapter 115: Purple Meets Fist

- Damrada -

After his new Lord gave him the medallion he was meant to show if he was questioned, he appeared in Azeroth in the blink of an eye.

He looked around curiously. He had heard many things about Clayman's old nation, the Puppet Kingdom Jistav, and he had heard even more things about Azeroth.

None of his spies could get into the country to give him up to date information, but he still managed somewhat. It wasn't like he couldn't just ask the merchants that traveled in and out. Most had nothing but good things to say about the nation. Many commented on how strict many things were, but that was also what kept the merchants safe from various threats so they couldn't complain much.

They were treated fairly and were able to profit, and that was what mattered to them.

Damrada found himself in a meeting room; one of many he suspected in the expansive palace. He had expanded his senses almost right away to figure out where he was. The fact that he appeared in his new Lord's palace made things easier.

He would be able to meet the important members of his Lord's entourage that way and evaluate them. Despite relying on Felix to defeat Rudra, he still knew that his subordinates would also have a part to play. The stronger they were, the easier his and his new Lord's job would be. He had bet everything on Felix, now he needed to do his part.

He had tried to expand his senses further to surround the entire palace, but something was blocking his senses when he pushed too far. Likely a barrier meant to keep things from the common people. The Eastern Empire had a similar system in place.

He unfortunately did not know much about his Lord's subordinates. There was not much information on both Felix and his ally, Demon Lord Rimuru, both as individuals and who their most powerful and valued subordinates were.

The most he and his former allies knew about Felix was about his Dragon subordinate and his Oni subordinate. They were only known about due to the rather grandiose fashion Felix used when acquiring the Dragon.

Dwargon was keeping an eye on him when he first appeared due to his abnormal power, even back then. As for the Oni, she had accompanied him around quite a bit, so she was rather well known as well. The rest, and Damrada knew there were more, unfortunately mostly kept to themselves.

Felix, or a representative of his had released a notice to the world that his foremost lieutenants were dubbed the Eight Demonic Lords, though who exactly they were was never mentioned.

He also knew that Granbell had sent some of his subordinates to attack Felix in the past. More of as a test, but Granbell believed there was still a possibility of the attack succeeding. Glenda and that other girl, Ingvild.

He didn't know what happened to them other than the fact that they did not return to Granbell's service. It was a shame. Granbell had said Ingvild held potential.

Perhaps he would find them among Felix's subordinates as well. Both were fairly impressive and valuable resources, and Felix didn't seem to be the kind to waste potential. Emperor Rudra was like that as well.

Some of his aura was already leaking, he expected for someone to come meet him at any moment, and so he decided to wait until then. It probably would not be taken very well if he decided to venture off on his own and explore without first introducing himself, lest he be mistaken as a threat.

While he waited he decided to observe the surroundings. He walked towards a window that was situated nearby. He found that it was facing towards the palace training grounds.

Even now, there were some soldiers training on the training field. Quite a few seemed to have some talent as well. Nothing special, but if each member of the military put in the amount of work the soldiers below seemed to be, then that would be a fearsome mortal army.

They were of a variety of races, all Majin of course, but that is where the similarities between them ended. There were Ogres, Oni, Hobgoblins, Beastmen, and more. He was fairly certain he hadn't even seen the truly special factions within the military. With a force like the one he suspected Felix to have, it gave him hope that with his help, Felix could accomplish his promise to Rudra.

He observed quietly, noting the discipline and skill on display. The rhythmic clatter of their weapons and the shouts of the instructors echoed across the grounds. Amidst the controlled chaos of training, he sensed that all the soldiers below wholeheartedly wanted to be there.

As he stood there, a door creaked open behind him, signaling the arrival of someone. Turning slightly, Damrada was met face to face with a violet haired woman. Just from a quick glance, Damrada could tell she was an incredibly beautiful woman, in the same leagues as Velgrynd. She had purple hair tied into a side ponytail of sorts, and glowing yellow eyes that felt like they could see through him entirely.

There was surprisingly no power radiating from the woman which was rather incredible. It was incredibly difficult to conceal one's power in its entirety; he would know.

As the woman sauntered forwards she spoke up. "Now who could you be? You seem rather powerful. Are you here to cause trouble?" The woman asked calmly. "I hope you are, that fight with that mage wasn't all that relieving." She said as her lips curled up into a smile that Damrada would call demonic.

Still, there was information in her words. Had a mage attacked Azeroth? Damrada filed that information away for later.

"Nothing of the sort." He began. "I am one of Lord Felix's newest subordinates." He said as he handed her the medallion that had been given to him. Plus his reserves were still drained from his fight with Felix. He had a feeling that even a weaker Saint would be capable of defeating him now.

She raised a brow as she examined the medallion. "I do sense my master's aura on this, but he has never given such a thing before."

Damrada's lips twitched. Had Felix handed him a form of identification that was never seen before? That was what his closest subordinates were supposed to believe?

The woman shrugged. "Well it does feel like him so I guess that's fine. You appeared here out of nowhere. No one except my Master could do such a thing. Though, if you cause any trouble, I'll kill you!" She said with a cheery smile.

Damrada was already used to death threats so he merely smiled.

"I thank you." He said with a bow. "My name is Damrada, it is a pleasure to meet you."
The woman blinked in confusion. "Ah, Damrada you said? One of the heads of Cerberus."

Damrada nodded. "That would be me."

"I see." The woman nodded. "My name is Lalatina. I guess I'll show you around if you want?" Lalatina offered. He could tell she was a Daemon. All Daemons had a certain feeling about them and Lalatina had that.

It was not surprising that she was named. For her to be one of Felix's direct subordinates as a Daemon, having a name and vessel was a must.

He wondered just how powerful she was, though. She had to have been an Arch Daemon at minimum, though she could be one of the mythical higher evolutions of Daemons.

Perhaps she even knew about his old rival. It would be nice to learn what happened to that Daemon. He was the only Arch Duke of the Daemon Realm and a dependent of Blanc, while Lalatina seemed to be of Violet's lineage going by her hair color and the general feel of her presence.

He nodded. "I would appreciate it if you are not busy." If he was introduced to everyone by one of Felix's direct subordinates, that would help give credence to his presence and status. For some reason, he really didn't want to rely on a never before seen medallion as a form of identification from now on.

Lalatina grinned mischievously, her glowing yellow eyes glinting as she gestured toward the door. "Well then, follow me. Let's see if you can keep up." Without waiting for his response, she spun on her heel and began walking briskly down the ornate hallway, her heels clicking against the polished floor.

Damrada followed, his steps deliberate and composed, taking note of his surroundings. The palace was nothing short of breathtaking, with intricate carvings lining the walls, magical light fixtures glowing softly, and an air of sophistication that spoke of the care the palace had received. He could tell the place was well taken care of, likely by maids, if he got Felix's personality right.

"So, what brings a former head of Cerberus to serve my Master?" Lalatina asked over her shoulder, her tone casual but laced with curiosity.

Damrada focused his attention back on his guide. He was rather curious to ask about her history, but he could wait for that. "I had fought Lord Felix during the attack on Ruberious."

She raised a brow. "Oh? He spared you then, hmm?"

Damrada's lips twitched at Lalatina's confidence in Felix, but Emperor Rudra inspired that same level of confidence. Damrada couldn't imagine the Emperor losing in a fight, ever. Not even to Guy Crimson.

Though Lalatina's confidence was not misplaced, for he was in no way capable of harming Felix if the man came at him seriously. Even the wound he gave Felix with his newest Art, Galaxy Impact, was nothing impressive, and was healed instantly.

"Before I answer that, may I ask what your position with Lord Felix is? I do not wish to share anything that I should not be." Damrada stated.

Lalatina nodded. "Hmm, sure. I'm in charge of the intelligence department. I deal with spying on other countries, rooting out traitors within our own ranks, and all that. The only one who has a higher rank than me you could say would be my Master, no matter how much Arcueid likes to claim she ranks higher."

He nodded as he went through his memories, wondering if he had heard the name of Arcueid before.

"Oh, I'm also one of the Eight Demonic Lords." Lalatina mentioned off-handedly.

Damrada froze for a moment before he continued his pace behind Lalatina. The Eight Demonic Lords were Felix's lieutenants, his highest level subordinates.

Damrada expected each at minimum to be Demon Lord Seed level, especially with how powerful Felix himself was. A simple master-subordinate naming from Felix would likely boost one's level drastically. He had been present before when Rudra had named a simple Majin. A simple name from Rudra elevated that mediocre Majin to the level of the higher level Imperial Guardians, and that too with no training. Now that same Majin was number 17 of the Imperial Guardians, one of the strongest in the Eastern Empire.

"I see. You must be impressive then to have risen to such a position of power." He praised. A little flattery couldn't hurt. During his time as a merchant he knew full well how much sucking up a little bit to someone could help you long term.

Of course, it could also backfire depending on the person. They may think you were weak willed and not capable, but he had a feeling that after showing off his power, no one would think that of him.

Lalatina looked over her shoulder at him. "I suppose I am." She said with amusement. He had a feeling he was missing something.

They continued through a series of hallways and rooms; various meeting rooms where plans about the city and the kingdom itself were discussed, the throne room, Felix's personal office and room, and the library which held various magic tomes that Lalatina pointed out.

She told him about the rewards center which he was rather curious about. It was somewhat similar to the Eastern Empire's own system. However, rather than points, it was your rank that got you rewards. If you rose to Single Digit status you would be given Legend Grade equipment and an Alternative for example.

She had told him briefly about what rewards were available in the rewards center, and Damrada couldn't help but admire just how ingenious it was.

Craving strength was a natural feeling for those who dwelled in this world; it was only natural that people would go after it. Rather than go behind Felix's back for it or betray him for power, Felix made it clear that there was room for advancement, but not without a cost.

One would have to earn their right to gain more power. Once one managed to get enough points they could exchange it for an Art, Spell, or weapon, as well as other various things as they pleased.

This would inspire a sense of gratitude in them for the priceless reward they received as well as increase their desire for more power after getting a taste, driving them back to working hard by serving Felix's interests to acquire more points. It was all a loop that fed itself.

The rewards Lalatina mentioned were not half bad either. She didn't say what the top most rewards were, but even the mid-level ones were useful.

They had also walked past some of the maids that served in Felix's palace. On average, they were incredibly powerful, easily within the range of Calamity Class. Lalatina had noticed how impressed he was and commented that there were two maids above the rest who served directly under one of the Eight Demonic Lords.

According to Lalatina, both were at the Demon Lord Seed level, which had made him reevaluate his expectations for the Eight Demonic Lords as well.

For him though, the most interesting maid by far was not quite the strongest, though she was strong. It was a maid that Lalatina introduced as Evelyn. According to Lalatina, she was a bit of a pet project of Felix's, though she did not elaborate on the goal of said project.

When Lalatina told Evelyn that Felix would be returning and perhaps calling for her soon, the maid's reaction was rather interesting. She stiffened up as a slight heat gathered on her face before bowing to Lalatina.

He was not daft enough to not get the signals. It was not unusual for rulers to make use of maids in such a way and he wouldn't give it a second thought if the maid hadn't interested him. She seemed to be an elven homunculus of some kind, but it was rather abnormal for one to be so far from Sarion, and such a powerful one as well.

Evelyn had to be close to the crown in Sarion. Kagali's vessel was of the same variety, yet it could barely exercise the power of a Greater Majin, and even for that, Yuuki had to pull many strings for.

For Evelyn to have such a vastly superior vessel, she must have some rather powerful connections within Sarion. And that was why he was interested in her. For the Sorcerous Dynasty of Sarion was a powerful dynasty that could prove useful against Emperor Rudra. Perhaps he would advise Felix to attempt to draw the Sorcerous Dynasty of Sarion into the inevitable war that would take place.

Sarion would be attacked eventually, it was inevitable, but Emperor Rudra is likely to leave them for later.

Before he could continue his thoughts, he was interrupted. "There is only one more stop." Lalatina said towards the end of the tour. "I'll show you to the training grounds reserved for strong people like us."

He nodded, he wasn't surprised that there was a training ground separated for the more powerful, it only made sense. Most kingdoms didn't have that issue in the West since there were not many with a level of power that qualified for such treatment, but in the Eastern Empire it was common.

As Lalatina led him, they crossed paths with a purple haired woman. From a mere glance Damrada could tell she was powerful. She had tried hard to suppress her aura, but a slight amount of it continued to leak out of her, allowing him to read her like a book.

She was stronger than even his old rival, the Arch Duke of Blanc's. Felix truly had quite the force under him. The Single Digits were meticulously trained and handpicked for their power and station, yet Felix seemed to also have subordinates of that level. He suspected Lalatina to be at that level, and this other purple haired Daemon may have that same potential.

He hadn't heard of another Daemon on that level other than Felix and the Primordials. Just who was this woman? Could she be Violet? Violet was known to have purple hair, though she was also known to assume a more childlike appearance, but that could always change.

Her level of power could be explained if it was Violet standing in front of him. Damrada had never met Violet but he didn't imagine that she would radiate such an aura of… innocence if he had to describe it.

"Ah, hello miss Lalatina!" The girl spoke up with a smile. "Has everything been handled?" The woman asked. "Glen said you ordered her to return back to her quarters."

He raised a brow. Glen? Could that be short for Glenda? She was one of the two ordered to ambush Felix by Granbell.

Lalatina stopped to address the woman. Surprisingly a genuine smile seemed to be on her face. Throughout the whole interaction he had with Lalatina, he hadn't seen a genuine expression other than one of cold amusement and the like when she was observing him discreetly, so it was rather odd to see such an expression on a Daemon of all races, a race known for their heartless and vile behavior.

"Hello Ingvild." Lalatina greeted with familiarity.

His eyes widened hearing that name. So this was the girl Granbell had told him about? The Daemon with potential that he managed to practically enslave before foolishly throwing her away due to underestimating Felix.

So it wasn't Violet then. Still, she was rather powerful for a standard Daemon. Apparently she had been summoned using the otherworlder summoning ritual. Granbell was rather confused that a Daemon appeared when he had not used the Daemon summoning ritual, but he did not complain upon realizing that she would be a useful asset nonetheless.

"Yes, Master was victorious as expected. I saw no purpose in having Glenda scan the borders any further." Lalatina said.

So it was Glenda then. It was nice to hear that she was doing well. She had some potential, it would have been a shame if she met an early death due to Granbell pushing her too much. Glenda's Spatial Manipulation could prove to become rather powerful if she had the proper guidance.

Ingvild clapped excitedly. "That's excellent! Attacking a peaceful country like Ruberious is truly horrible. I'm glad that Felix was able to protect them."

His lips twitched as he heard Ingvild's way of referring to Ruberious. "Peaceful" was an odd way of describing that nation. Sure, they did not engage in war, but it still was not perfect.

The only thing that Damrada could admire about it was that it ran in a similar fashion as the world would under Emperor Rudra. In order to create a world of true peace, all conflict must be eliminated. Emperor Rudra knew this.

And so, he planned for everyone to have their roles to play, too busy to think of rebelling, and before long that obedience would be ingrained into them after a few generations, as they would have known nothing else.

Natural selection at its finest.

Cruel? Perhaps, but it would work. Though looking back on it, Damrada was not sure anymore if he wished to support such a plan. Would such a thing not take away what made Humanity what it was?

Ever since he joined Felix, he had been having some doubts about Emperor Rudra's methods. But the past was the past, there was no use dwelling on it. Emperor Rudra's goals had nothing to do with him ever since his friend asked him to act against him.

Emperor Rudra believed his loss to Michael would be inevitable, yet he would continue to march ever forward, always pursuing his goal despite the danger it would cause to the world. And so, he was tasked with ensuring Michael failed to take over Rudra's body, the only method Rudra knew of for that was death.

Lalatina turned back to Damrada. "While you're here, let me introduce you to Damrada. He is Master's newest subordinate. You may be seeing him around once Master decides what to do with him." She said as that familiar look of amusement shone in her yellow eyes.

Ingvild finally turned to him as she gave a light bow. "Nice to meet you!" She greeted him happily.

He slowly nodded. "Nice to meet you as well."

"She's also one of the Eight Demonic Generals." Lalatina added with a smirk.

Ingvild fidgeted slightly upon hearing that. It seems she was uncomfortable with the title, or the responsibilities that came with it? Or perhaps she did not see herself as worthy?
"Is that so?" He said. "She feels rather powerful, it must be deserved." He said, flattering Ingvild slightly.

Ingvild let a small smile blossom onto her face. "Thank you! But without Glen I wouldn't be as strong as I am now!"

Lalatina nodded towards Ingvild before turning around. "We must be going now, Ingvild."

Ingvild nodded as she stepped aside before they continued on. "It was nice to meet you, Mister Damrada!" Ingvild called out.

He nodded. "It was a pleasure to meet you as well." He said before he continued to follow behind Lalatina.

As Lalatina led him in silence, he found himself growing curious about the rest of the Eight Demonic Lords. "If you would not mind, would you mind informing me about who exactly the Eight Demonic Lords are? Not much information about them is publicly available I am afraid."

Lalatina paused as she looked over her shoulders at him, her yellow eyes gleaming eerily before a mischievous grin worked its way onto her face. "Heh, Arcueid is responsible for that, always trying to have some card in her pocket to play in case some other kingdoms get a bit uppity. Sure, I can tell you. I already confirmed with my Master that you were who you said you were."

He blinked in confusion. He hadn't felt the telltale signs of a Thought Communication from Lalatina.

As she continued to lead him she spoke about the Eight Demonic Generals. She said that it was generally ranked from strongest to weakest, but the top three of the Demonic Generals were rather even in power.

Though perhaps Lalatina was biased since she was included among the top three. Felix himself had apparently decided the rankings back during the Founding Festival of Tempest. According to Lalatina, the Eight Demonic Generals was a spontaneous idea of his.

The top three was filled with three women: Arcueid, Megumin, and Lalatina herself. All three were Daemons according to Lalatina. Lalatina had said that he'd meet the other two at some point.

Following those three was Saeko, the Oni he knew about, and Raiden, the Dragon Felix recruited on Mount Caanat who was also the Head Maid apparently.

According to Lalatina the two were also very close in power, and a fight between them could go either way. It was rather impressive for two weak Majins like those two to have grown as strong as they had.

According to the information he had, Saeko was once a mere Ogre, yet now she was an Oni, a Demon Lord Seed class Majin. And the Dragon, Raiden, as well. Arch Dragons were incredibly rare, Dragon Lords even more so, and yet from what he knew, Raiden did not start at that stage. No, she grew to that level under Felix.

After that was a man named Sukuna, who Lalatina called an "interesting Daemon" which confirmed his race for Damrada. Then after Sukuna was a woman named Kurumi, who was a Nine Tailed Fox according to Lalatina.

Nine Tailed Foxes were an incredibly rare and powerful species of Majin. Each being born with one Majin that lives inside each of their tails, besides the main one. Those Majins had the potential to be extremely powerful as well, and their total power would be added onto the power of the Nine Tailed Fox as well.

He had only ever heard of one other Nine Tailed Fox in existence, though he was sure there were more out there. It should theoretically be possible for one to evolve into one after all.

He wondered if the Nine Tailed Fox that Lalatina spoke of had any relation to the Nine Tailed Fox that Kanzis had resurrected as a shadow of his after killing off that village of Majins.

Kanzis was a powerful Enlightened and a hailed Champion of the Eastern Empire, one who now served in the military. He was an Imperial Guardian with a strong Unique Skill that allowed him to resurrect his defeated foes as shadows that served him.

His shadows maintained all their abilities, energy, and even Skills that they had in life. Of course, there were limits. If the ego of the one whose shadow Kanzis was trying to retrieve was too powerful for Kanzis to handle, then the Skill would fail to subordinate them as Shadows.

The village the Nine Tailed Fox under Kanzis was from was actually located close to Azeroth in the past before the Eastern Empire launched its attack on it, during which all the residents were massacred, with their leader, a powerful Nine Tailed Fox, being resurrected as one of Kanzis's shadows, or so Kanzis's report said.

Then finally, at the end of the Eight Demonic Generals, was Ingvild herself. She wasn't as strong as even the weakest Saint of the Eastern Empire in his perspective, but she was still powerful.

Felix had at least eight powerful fighters on his side then, not including his allies and Felix himself.

Felix had not even been a Demon Lord for 6 months, yet he already had such a powerful force under him. It could possibly compare to Emperor Rudra's subordinates, not in quantity but perhaps in quality, and the Emperor had spent centuries in his recruitment and refining of his subordinates.

Was Felix just lucky or did he have something that allowed for the birth of such powerful Majins?

"Lord Felix has gathered a rather impressive force. I take it the military is just as impressive?" Damrada probed lightly.

Lalatina shrugged. "They are adequate. Megumin is in charge of them, she's been training them up for a few months now to be of more use."

Damrada's lips twitched at her use of the word "adequate". If the soldiers he saw when he first arrived were only adequate, then he wasn't sure what excellent would truly be, but perhaps those ones were the elites.

"How strong are the common soldiers?" He asked.

Lalatina pursed her lips. "I'd say on average each common soldier has approximately 6,000-8,000 EP, while the commanders are even more powerful, some have an EP of upwards of 100,000, though those are the ones who put in the most hard work."

His eyes widened. He was familiar with the Existence Points system Tempest had released with their announcement of The Dungeon being open to all. It was a rather interesting concept all things considered, but not something he would put much stock in. While energy reserves were important, it was how you used that energy that mattered far more.

Still, even then, 6,000 EP was said to be equal to a higher level B Class Monster going by the Free Guild's way of ranking. B Class beings were capable of destroying entire villages with relative ease.

10,000 EP was classified as the level of Greater Majins. While to him Greater Majins were just slightly stronger insects to be stepped on, to the common people they may as well have been unstoppable deities. The common rabble were approaching that level.

Greater Majin were considered gods essentially in certain, more remote areas, and each common soldier was at that level? That was absurd. Not even the Eastern Empire could boast such a thing. Sure, they had many far above that level, but the common soldiers were far from that level, though perhaps the magi-tech that was being rapidly developed could allow common soldiers to fight at that level.

Not to mention she said some commanders had over 100,000 EP. While that was not even Enlightened level, it was still rather extraordinary. That level of strength was likely enough to wipe out weaker nations.

As he continued to ask Lalatina about the nation, they were interrupted by the appearance of another Daemon. Damrada sensed his teleportation long before he saw the Daemon appear. What he had not sensed was who exactly the Daemon was.

He met the grey eyes of a young boy, or rather, a Daemon who took on the appearance of a young boy. Damrada could recognize those grey eyes and ash grey hair anywhere. To think after so many centuries, he would meet him here, of all places.

Just as Damrada realized who the Daemon was, the Daemon realized who he was. Neither made any move to attack of course; both realized there was a reason for the other to be there.

"Oh?" Lalatina sounded out. "Do you two know each other?" Lalatina asked with curiosity as she saw the recognition in both of their eyes.

The Daemon looked away from Damrada to answer Lalatina. "I do know him, yes. He was an old foe not worth mentioning."

Damrada's lips twitched at the subtle jab to his pride. He took a deep breath. "Indeed, Miss Lalatina. That Daemon and I used to clash many times back in the Eastern Empire."

Lalatina raised an impressed brow. "Oho? To be able to clash with Moss, even before he incarnated and was named, is impressive." Lalatina praised.

Moss. So that was his name now. He could tell the moment Moss appeared in front of him that his old rival of sorts was incarnated now, something which likely took his level of power even further.

They had not clashed in quite some time, so Damrada did not know how strong Moss had become now, which was rather annoying. Moss's aura was perfectly concealed in his small form, making it impossible for him to get a read on Moss's power.

Moss nodded slightly. "I suppose he was an… adequate opponent."

Damrada's lips twitched again. Moss always knew how to get under his skin. He wasn't even sure if it was intentional or not at this point.

"You two can continue your conversation at another time then, I suppose. Why are you here, Moss?" Lalatina asked.

"My Mistress wished to be informed of who the new powerful presence was, so she sent me to inquire more." Moss stated simply.

Moss, the only Arch Duke in the Daemon Realm was referring to someone with a title such as 'Mistress'? Not to mention he was acting incredibly obedient and submissive towards Lalatina. He had never seen Moss act in such a fashion before.

There was only one woman that he could consider Moss calling his Mistress, and that was the Primordial of White, Blanc.

Lalatina hummed in understanding. "I'll go tell her myself, I want to see what she's doing with that mage anyway. Can you continue to give Damrada the tour?"

Moss bowed. "As you wish, Lady Lalatina."

Lalatina eyed him once more before vanishing.

"If you do not mind me asking, who exactly is your Mistress, Moss?" He asked.

Moss looked at him as if he were an idiot. "Who do you think?"

His lips twitched. That had been happening a lot today. "You mean to tell me that the Primordial of White serves Felix now?"
Moss nodded. "Indeed, and she is not the only one. Violet and Jaune also serve Lord Felix. In fact, one of them just left."

"You mean to tell me…."
"Lady Lalatina's true identity is the Primordial of Purple, Violet."

Damrada sighed. "I suppose I should have expected as much from Felix."

Moss nodded. "Which areas remain to be shown to you?"

"Just the training grounds."

Moss nodded, and with that his tour continued. Who would have thought he'd be having a peaceful conversation with a man such as Moss.

- Felix -

After answering Lalatina's Thought Communication about Damrada, I told Rimuru about what had happened after he left.

Chloe, Veldora, and Ramiris were present as well. Ramiris dismissed Beretta, leaving just us.

I told them about the talk I had with Damrada, the information that Damrada told me about Michael and Rudra, how Michael was basically rebelling against Rudra, and how Damrada was ordered to oppose Rudra and his dream, to find someone to counter him and deal the decisive blow when it became necessary.

I told them about Guy's arrival, his small spat with Saare, then the discussion we had with Luminous before Hinata jumped in due to a misunderstanding.

"Hehe, Hinata is always like that." Chloe giggled.

Rimuru joined in. "She does always seem to misunderstand things, doesn't she?"
I rolled my eyes, feeling the need to defend the honor of my student. "She's getting better! I think."

"Bhahaha!" Veldora laughed at our words. "I always knew something was up with her back when she def– back when she cheated her way to beating me!"

Rimuru and Chloe shot Veldora a look that made him wilt. "I'm pretty sure you're just coping, Veldora." Chloe said with a small grin.

Veldora crossed his arms with a pout that should not be on a face as masculine as Veldora's. "Fine, maybe she beat me fair and square, but I'm better now, I'm different! I've already had my training arc! I'm like post time skip Luffy now, except better!"

"But Felix said that Hinata fought Guy, could you do the same?" Rimuru asked teasingly, joining in on the bullying session.

Veldora froze before he shivered for a moment as if recalling some horrible memory. He coughed lightly. "O-Of course I can!"

Ramiris nodded atop from her perch on Veldora's head before she began shadow boxing around us. "Heh, Guy used to run from me whenever I showed up to have some fun with him before Milim was born! I could totally solo him too!"

It said something that I wasn't even sure if Ramiris was bullshitting us or not right now. I really didn't have a good idea of just how strong prime Spirit Queen Ramiris was. For all I know, maybe Guy really would run from her in a fight.

Still, I rolled my eyes at Veldora's bravado. "It's not like Hinata fought Guy to a standstill anyway. Guy was just testing her, if he went all out, Hinata wouldn't be able to win, even as a True Hero."

Veldora let out a sigh of relief. "That's good." Before he froze. "Ah, I mean, it wouldn't matter anyway, I would still win!" He said with a plastic grin on his face.

Ramiris let out a hum. "Still, you said that Hinata was given Granbell's Holy Spirit and Hero's Egg?" Ramiris asked.

I nodded. "Yeah, that's what happened."

"That's never happened before. Maybe Granbell's Elemental took a liking to Hinata then." Ramiris said with a nod.

"Eh, that's possible?" Rimuru asked.

Ramiris nodded. "Mhmm. If an Elemental finds another individual more worthy they can transfer the contract to them, if they wish to."
"Huh, I didn't know that." Rimuru said.

Ramiris sighed. "It's a shame though…"
"What is?" I asked.

"I was hoping you or Hinata would come ask me for another Elemental. Then I could exto– I mean ask for candy in return!" She said with a pout.

My lips twitched at Ramiris' words. I slowly approached her, which she noticed. "H-Hey! I know kung-fu! Don't come closer!" Ramiris said as she raised her hands in a mock fighting stance, clearly trying to look intimidating, but failing miserably. Her tiny fists were shaking, and her wings flapped nervously as I stopped just a foot away from her.

I crouched down, looking at her eye to eye with a grin. "Oh, really? Kung-fu, huh? Are you sure you're not bluffing, Ramiris?"

"Of course not!" She puffed up her chest, attempting to look confident. "I've been practicing for centuries! One wrong move and bam! You'll regret messing with me!" She jabbed the air, her movements about as threatening as a toddler swinging a toy sword.

This was actually kinda funny. There was a reason I liked messing with Ramiris so much. All of us here knew that it was all in good fun though, even Ramiris. She acted like a childish ditz but it was just that: an act, similar to Milim actually.

Speaking of Milim, I probably need to appease her for leaving her out of the fights. Knowing her, I'm sure she'll come to bug me at some point, asking about why she wasn't invited to the "fun".

I did want to invite her, but Milim and self control don't go that well together if she isn't taking things seriously. She'd make things too easy for our side, and while the attack was nothing special, it was still important that Luminous and her people be seen as the primary defenders of the attack.

Veldora couldn't hold it in any longer and burst into laughter. "Bhahaha! Ramiris, you're going to give everyone secondhand embarrassment! Stop embarrassing us mighty beings!" Veldora said with a grin.

"Shut up, you overgrown lizard!" Ramiris shot back, spinning around to glare at Veldora, though her small size made it look more comical than threatening. "I'm the Spirit Queen! Respect me!" She whined like a child.

Chloe giggled, hiding her smile behind her hand. "Ramiris, maybe you should stop before you hurt yourself."

Rimuru smirked, clearly enjoying the banter. "Alright, Ramiris, let's say you really do know kung-fu. Why don't you show us a demonstration?"

"Fine! Watch and be amazed!" Ramiris floated into the air, puffing her cheeks before launching into a bizarre routine of twirls, flips, and poorly coordinated punches. It was less martial arts and more interpretive dance, and the only thing amazing about it was how serious she looked while performing.

I crossed my arms and gave her a slow clap as she landed with a triumphant pose. "Bravo. Truly terrifying. I don't know how I'll recover."

Ramiris narrowed her eyes. "You're mocking me, aren't you?"

"Me? Mock you? Never." My lips twitched as I fought to keep a straight face. "But seriously, if you wanted candy, you could've just asked. No need to extort Hinata for Elementals."

Ramiris's wings fluttered with excitement. "Really? You'll give me candy?"

I summoned a pouch of candy from my Infinite Space and gave it to her. I always had appropriate bribes prepared if I needed them in a pinch.

Her eyes sparkled as she snatched the pouch. "You're the best, Felix!" She hugged the candy to her chest, her earlier bravado forgotten.

Rimuru rolled his eyes. "So what happened after Guy and Hinata finished their spar?" Rimuru asked.

It didn't take me long to finish summarizing the details of what the meeting was about, including Castle Guard. To say that the four were surprised would be an understatement.

"Hmm, so that's the current state of the Emperor, huh?" Chloe said.

"I can't say it is surprising. My elder brother's Ultimate Skill was said to be the strongest in existence." Veldora chimed in.

"Do you know anything more about it, Veldora, Ramiris?" Rimuru asked.

Ramiris was uncharacteristically looking serious as she sat on Veldora's head. "Hmm, I don't remember things perfectly, but I do remember some things about Michael."

"Oh?"

"Velda said that Michael, Lord of Justice could be considered the "King" of all Angelic Skills, and so it had authority matching that status." Ramiris said. She didn't remember a whole lot about the things that went on in her original incarnation, but she did still retain some things.

"The King?" Chloe said. "What does that mean?"
