Story: I'm a Daemon, so what?

Disclaimer: I do not own the original setting.

Chapter 121: Ultimate Arts?

- Felix -

"That's good then. If you need anything, you can always ask me." Despite not making much use of Gravity Manipulation, I had been capable of manipulating it for quite some time and had used it here and there.

It did also fall under my Law Domination, meaning I had nigh-absolute control over it to a certain point, and Kurumi had been specializing in Gravity Manipulation.

I may not make use of Gravity much, but it was a powerful force of the universe. Even ignoring its more overpowered applications like bending Space and Time, even just increasing the force and momentum behind your attacks could help you a lot up to a certain point.

"I have already begun constructing an Ultimate Skill that improves upon Kurumi's abilities, the data for which I will engrave into her soul so that it will awaken within her when the time comes."

'Thank you.'

"It is my duty, Master."

Kurumi's smile turned a little sharper. "Even if what I want is you, Master?"

I rolled my eyes, smirking. "Nice try."

She laughed, the tension in the air fading. "You can't blame a fox for trying."

I wanted to have a more casual relationship with Kurumi until I felt like I had put enough effort in to get to know her to the extent that I believed we would do well together. I had learned a bit after all the experience I accumulated in this world.

Shaking my head, I glanced back at her paintings, watching the tiny figures move as if they were real. It was like they were real beings that were captured inside of the painting, with no idea about the world outside their own. "You really do have a gift though, Kurumi."

A small but cute smile formed on her face as her fox ears twitched. "Thank you." She was always weak to compliments.

"They remind me of the art I have displayed in my office." I pointed out.

Kurumi's ears perked up slightly, clearly pleased by the comparison. "Oh? You noticed? As expected of you, Master." Kurumi nodded in a self-assured manner. "I was quite taken with those pieces, actually. They were a masterpiece in their own right, and I couldn't help but wonder… what if I could create something similar, but with my own touch?" She gestured toward one of the paintings, a tranquil lake reflecting a starry sky. The water rippled ever so slightly within the painting, as if a breeze had passed through it.

"I'm glad that you found a hobby like this you could devote yourself to."

Now if only Arcueid, Lalatina, and Megumin could follow in Kurumi's example. It was as if those three never heard of a hobby. Though maybe for them, their tasks were hobbies. After being alive for so long, as long as they found enjoyment in their tasks, then perhaps that was all they could wish for. I imagine most hobbies would get stale after so long, even if Spiritual Lifeforms were more immune to boredom than most.

"There was also one other thing I wanted to talk to you about."

Kurumi's tails swished from side to side. "Yes, Master?"

"It's something that can increase your power further. I didn't tell you about it beforehand, as I was not sure if you were capable of surviving the process. Now I'm confident you can."

I told her about Life Construction, about how I thought she was ready to handle the strenuous process and come out stronger for it. I explained the process to her, how it made use of souls, and how it was up to her to face the resentment of the souls while allowing Othinus to guide the energy within her to refine her being.

I made sure it was clear that she could reject me if she wasn't up for it. I was aware of how morally dark the operation could be considered, and I was willing to take that sin onto myself since I was the main driver behind the Life Construction.

I explained Othinus away as something that was going to help with the Life Reconstruction. I would tell those close to me about Othinus at some point, but I didn't want to get into that right now. Most of them would likely learn about her during the operation itself.

Othinus was basically responsible for guiding the energy into Kurumi in a steady fashion so that it was easier for her to gain control over the energy and refine herself with it, while also absorbing the resentment of the souls and refining herself with that as well.

Life Reconstruction was actually based on the Harvest Festival. In the Harvest Festival, you took in souls to basically nurture your Demon Lord Seed. These souls would have an ego and would try to kill you while you resisted against them, slowly refining them into energy to germinate your Demon Lord Seed.

Life Reconstruction was the same, except for instead of germinating your Demon Lord Seed, you'd germinate your entire being, refining everything. This could only be used once since, after that point, the amount of souls required would be absurd, and the process would take exponentially longer.

I was only having everyone undergo it to basically expand their potential, so that when they went through the Harvest Festival, it would be an even bigger multiplier to their strength, hopefully.

Life Reconstruction would definitely be considered a demonic Art by Humans, similar to Necromancy, and it was deserving of such a label.

Kurumi seemed all for it, seemingly not at all bothered, and even seemed happy at my confidence in her abilities.

I did wonder what the next evolution for Kurumi and Saeko would be. Though that was if they even evolved. The next stage of evolution for them was likely going to be obtaining Divinity, and part of that transformation involved reaching a stage of ascendance.

If they missed that, they wouldn't get Divinity, though they'd still receive a significant power up in EP at the very least. The rules of Divinity still confused me since there didn't seem to be a set condition to acquire it.

I got it after my Harvest Festival, as did Rimuru. True Dragons like Veldora were born with it, and then there was Hinata who reached a stage of enlightenment for it. She said that it was as if she reached a pivotal realization in that moment that transformed her world view, that was the catalyst for Divinity in her.

Yet a man like Damrada was still a Saint and not a Divine Human.

Arcueid, Megumin, and Lalatina likely only obtained Divinity so easily because they already had it once upon a time. In fact, I doubt they ever lost their Divinity. You can't really lose something like that; it's a piece of yourself. The likely scenario was that it was just deeply suppressed inside of them by the World itself, making it difficult for me to detect even when in my Infinity Space.

"I believe the same as well, Master. Whilst guiding them through their reconstruction, I felt the Divinity almost immediately sprout from within them, almost as if it was waiting for the opportunity."

Well that proves that then.

Raiden's next stage was obviously Divine Dragon. It was the highest state a Dragon could reach, as far as I knew, as there was no becoming a True Dragon ordinarily. Divinity in general marked the highest stage of evolution for the most part. Evolving again after gaining Divinity wasn't something I had ever heard of, but I wouldn't be that surprised if it had happened in the past.

The nature of this world was that the impossible was possible.

"If you're open to it, then I'll call you when Raiden and Saeko are undergoing the process, so that you can all go through it at once."

Those two were still fighting, which wasn't surprising. At this point, they had the stamina to keep going for days.

"Yes Master!" Kurumi yipped as her tails swished back and forth. She was really way too easy to read. She would have a completely neutral expression, but her tails would be wagging back and forth. It was honestly pretty cute.

I stood up from the seat I had taken. "I'll leave you to your art now. I'll be looking forward to seeing what you come up with next."

She smiled, and this time, there was no teasing in it. It was just pure, genuine happiness. "I won't disappoint you, Master."

I raised a hand, waving as I left. "I know you won't." Before I paused, just remembering what I came here for. "One last thing Kurumi."

"Hmm?" She purred.

"You've been doing good work, and so I want to reward you."

"Fufufu, I appreciate the gesture, Master, but it is a pet's duty to follow the orders of their owners."

I really never got the whole "pet" and "owner" thing Kurumi went on about. I guess it was just her culture. Well, that and it was partially a kink thing too; something I realized quite a while ago with Lover.

"Still, I want you to have something. It can be anything, and I won't stop bugging you until you tell me what."

Kurumi sighed. "Very well then, Master. There is one thing if you wouldn't mind my impudence."

I gestured her to go on. "I want you to arrange an opportunity for me to kill the man who murdered my mother." Kurumi said with a vicious smile on her face.

I nodded right away. "I'll arrange it. Do you mind waiting for when the Eastern Empire takes action? Things involving them will be easier at that time."

Kurumi nodded. "Thank you. As you wish, Master."

I nodded. "See ya later then."

As I left, I considered what to do with my time. I had some free time on my hands. Sure there was stuff I could be doing, but sometimes I let my laziness win out; it was nothing urgent.

My lips curved upwards as I figured out just what I had decided to do.

I used Instant Motion to immediately appear in one of the training dimensions with only a thought.

I took a deep breath of the magicule rich air. The dimension was empty, filled only with green hills and was about the size of a larger country.

Maintaining a dimension of this size would ordinarily be a bit bothersome, even for me. A single dimension wasn't going to do much to my reserves with Magicule Breeder Reactor, but with tens of them littered around, it would add up.

Even with Magicule Breeder Reactor needing only a moment to quickly refill my reserves, that single moment when I was at less than peak capacity could be taken advantage of if someone was competent and powerful enough.

So I had already enlisted Sasha to create magicule reactors. They wouldn't function to the same extent as my own, but they would be similar to nuclear reactors. A single one of them, in theory, should be able to power two or three of the training dimensions I was currently maintaining. They would absorb magicules from the air, and breed them together, as I had explained the mechanisms behind something like that to Sasha.

So it was only until those were ready that I would be maintaining these dimensions.

Now I was here to test a few theories of mine.

I had gotten a bit inspired after acquiring the data for Guy's Lucifer, Lord of Pride. The way he could basically "copy" Skills and other abilities was that he analyzed the phenomena in question in incredible detail.

Once he understood the phenomena in question, it was sort of logged into Lucifer for easy access in the future. They are basically tacked onto Lucifer for future use almost like Arts, but they still functioned like Skills. It was certainly unique.

This way, the Ultimate Skills he copied weren't weakened due to lacking a core, but were still able to be called upon quickly. However, there was a limit to how much Lucifer could store, as the Ultimate-level sub-skills he copied still occupied space in his soul.

I had asked Othinus to add the ability to "log" the data for Arts and such I used under Brahma as well, similar to what Lucifer did, so that I could also quickly call upon any Ultimate Skill I was able to replicate in Art form in the future.

Such a function was easy to create thanks to the data on Lucifer.

Lucifer's essence was basically complete reproduction of abilities the user has seen once, due to Guy being its wielder.

Lucifer most definitely buffed up his analytical abilities, but Guy's own still had to carry the majority of the weight. His calculative abilities had to be monstrous, maybe even approaching the level of a Manas if he can do it on sight like I suspect he can.

Using what I now knew, I wanted to improve upon Brahma. I had already been working on this, but hadn't been making much progress until I got the data on Lucifer, Lord of Pride.

Brahma, Lord of Creation was certifiably bullshit. With enough time, I could do almost anything with it. Create brand new never before seen Skills, putting Skills into weapons, putting knowledge into weapons so that the wielder immediately becomes a master combatant, manipulate the soul,. Hell, if I want to be a True Dragon, I can be one if given time.

All of that was theoretically possible if Othinus had enough time to analyze the processes and mechanisms behind what I was trying to do, which was why I couldn't just True Dragonify myself just like that. It wasn't even something I considered due to just how difficult something like that was.

True Dragons were born, not made. You could not just become a True Dragon because you wanted to, they were a pivotal aspect of existence, until their concepts died out, they would forever remain.

Othinus had already run through the odds of me successfully becoming a True Dragon; safe to say it was not likely. She had said it would theoretically be possible if I cannibalized a True Dragon, completely destroying and incorporating their being, which Othinus theorized would be enough for her to understand just how they were linked to the world and replicate such a process inside of me.

Even if it failed, she said she would still be able to strengthen my base attributes to the same levels of a True Dragon, including my soul. I would just be lacking the intrinsic ability all True Dragons possessed due to their concepts. My energy reserves were already at the level of a True Dragon, but there was more to it than that.

But essentially, Brahma breaks all the so-called rules over its knees.

And Yuuki was bullshit for having the potential to awaken something like that, but I wasn't going to spend much time considering the possibility of becoming a True Dragon and whatnot. If it happened, it happened. If not, no big deal. I was already as strong as a True Dragon.

With all that, there wasn't much I could actually improve upon Brahma, despite my desire to. At least as I was now, except for one thing. The Skill Retrieval sub-skill, which limited me to only being able to bring out 70% of the power of the Ultimate Skill in question.

This limitation was in place because what Skill Retrieval did was basically overlay whichever sub-skill I was trying to access over itself, giving me access to that specific sub-skill of an Ultimate Skill.

However, it wouldn't have the core of the original Ultimate Skill that was specifically meant to reinforce and empower its sub-skills, making Skill Retrieval slightly weaker than the real deal. Brahma's core by nature was adaptable, but it wasn't perfect.

After Guy's Lucifer, I got the idea that couldn't I just manually recreate the phenomena of the Ultimate Skill?

I was able to copy Metatron, Lord of Purity from him likely only because Metatron had a single ability that could be used in a variety of ways, but it still went to show Guy's sheer skill, that he could get Odin, Lord of Cursed Knowledge to misclassify the data as a full on Ultimate Skill, and it worked.

Doing this would involve my own processing and calculative ability just as much as it would Brahma's. Skills, at their core, were basically keybinds for automatically manipulating certain Laws of the World in a very specific way. They were extremely potent, but less flexible because of that very same function.

Arts could do everything a Skill could. It would just be more difficult, but it would also be more potentially flexible.

So why not mimic the phenomena of the Ultimate Skills I had data on through Arts? It was different from what Lucifer, Lord of Pride did, but that didn't change the fact that Guy's Ultimate Skill was what inspired me.

I decided to start off easy, with a few Unique Skills, despite there being no need to do so as Unique Skills could be perfectly used through Skill Retrieval.

In front of me, Space was cut apart in a fashion mimicking the Unique Skill: Spatial Severing. An illusion was placed over the world around me, one capable of deceiving the senses of other people around in a fashion similar to Falsifier.

I continued to cycle through various Unique Skills, managing to mimic their effects with relative ease. There were a large variety of Unique Skills I had data on, from various otherworlders, from Rimuru's people, from my own people, and the Unique Skills of other people I had come across.

Quite a lot of them were simple but potent. Raiden's Unique Skill: Thunder was a simple but potent Unique Skill. I could recreate its effects easily with Magic, as it just gave Raiden an instant and powerful control over Lightning and Thunder, and allowed her to temporarily spiritualize and turn into energy. More specifically, it turns her into a form of living lightning itself. That didn't make it weak; it just optimized her already powerful abilities in that department, making them easier to access and more powerful.

Then there were also some Unique Skills that could be very complicated. However, I had an extremely adept understanding of the world, making it rather simple to mimic them with the data I had.

I knew Ultimate Skills would be different, however. They were levels more complex in the Laws they utilized, as well as the finesse needed, to use them in a way similar to the Ultimate Skill in question.

Some Ultimate Skills were easier to recreate in the form of Arts than others, like Elmesia's Vayu, Lord of Heavenly Wind. It was just Wind Manipulation taken to the max, involving spiritrons in its manipulation. But what I wanted to do was to be capable of using some of the more innately complex Ultimate Skills without suffering the loss in potency.

I closed my eyes and took a deep breath.

The Ultimate Skill I would attempt to replicate was going to be Beelzebuth, Lord of Gluttony. It was one I was very familiar with seeing as I have used it quite a bit, even if it wasn't my own Ultimate Skill.

It was one of the more "straightforward" Ultimate Skills, in that its primary function was to consume and even assimilate anything, whether it was matter, energy, or even phenomena.

However, its underlying mechanisms were anything but simple. The way Beelzebuth functioned was through a complex series of Laws that dictated what could be consumed, how it was processed, and how the user could redistribute what they had taken in. The latter part wasn't difficult as I could just chuck whatever it is I ate into Infinity Space.

I extended my hand and focused.

First, I attempted the most basic application, the consumption of matter. A chunk of Hihi'irokane sat before me. It was one of the most durable and magically resistant materials in existence. It was the base of God Grade equipment, so it would do just fine as a test subject.

I focused on the Laws that Beelzebuth interacted with. After having and using it for so long, those Laws were somewhat familiar to me. It was why I chose to first attempt Beelzebuth, Lord of Gluttony, as it wasn't extremely easy, but it wouldn't be as hard as some of the Ultimate Skills I wasn't as familiar with. I had the data of various Ultimate Skills, but having the data alone wasn't enough. The data gave me a general understanding of the Laws used, but it was still more complex than that.

Guy was able to do what he did likely due to his experience. He was eons old and had far more experience than I did, so he just knew a lot of things. Not to mention, he's likely experimented a lot over the years.

I felt the Laws of the World. Most felt easily manipulatable to me, thanks to Law Domination, but many Ultimate Skills made use of multiple Laws, so I had to intertwine them very carefully to come up with the specific effect I wanted. I felt the drain of my energy, but it was less than expected.

I felt the shift, yet nothing happened. The chunk of divine steel remained inert, completely unaffected. My lips pursed as I went through the process in my head, trying to figure out what went wrong.

I raised my hand, deciding to observe the process of Beelzebuth's consumption again. I instantly consumed the Hihi'irokane with my Ultimate Skill version of Beelzebuth before spitting it back out.

Perhaps my attempts had been too simplistic? I needed to more accurately mimic the way Beelzebuth broke down matter on a conceptual level.

It was the Ultimate Skill representing Gluttony, an all encompassing desire to consume. Maybe I needed to call upon that desire a bit more.

I closed my eyes, taking a deep breath as I focused on the essence of Gluttony.

Beelzebuth wasn't just about consuming, it was about devouring completely, leaving nothing behind but what I wanted to remain. It was the representation of an endless hunger, a law that allowed the user to erase something from existence and claim it as their own. If I wanted to replicate it without losing potency, I needed to understand exactly how that process worked.

The world functioned on rules; layers of reality interwoven through cause and effect, pretty much. Beelzebuth functioned by bypassing the normal constraints of consumption, matter, energy, and even abilities, by enforcing a single event: that which is consumed belongs to me.

I extended my hand again, the chunk of Hihi'irokane still resting before me.

This time, I didn't just attempt to consume it like before. I poured my will into it, my desire to take it as my own. I reached out with my senses, I felt the structure of the metal, its energy, and everything else. I let that hunger manifest, not just an instinctual craving, but the absolute certainty that this object would be mine, even invoking some aspects of what Greed may call upon.

There was a subtle shift in the atmosphere.

I focused on the Laws, guiding them to interweave as carefully as possible. This was my first attempt, so I was going slow. Something at this speed would be useless in real combat.

The Laws Beelzebuth interacted with bent to my will. I wrapped them together, shaping them into an Art that would function identically to Beelzebuth. It was Beelzebuth's Predation in Art form.

After a few moments, a vortex of pure darkness and absorption formed, sucking the Hihi'irokane into my Infinity Space as if it were a black hole. The energy drain was larger than what Beelzebuth's Lord of Gluttony's would be, but that was because the Ultimate Skill form was more optimized. I could do the same with enough time.

I allowed my lips to curve upwards into a smug smirk as I dispelled the vortex. I had done it, or at least I had mostly done it. It wasn't as smooth as using Beelzebuth directly, but it proved that replicating an Ultimate Skill's function through an Art was possible, and that I could do it on my own, and that too without it losing potency, so long as I mastered the Art version enough.

"That was quite excellent, Master. I could not have done it better myself." Othinus finally spoke up.

'Thanks.'

This was my own little side project, so Othinus was refraining from helping me.

I went ahead and tested Predation a few more times on various objects, each time was smoother and quicker than the last. Before long, I was happy with the progress I had made with Beelzebuth. I didn't feel the need to work on Predation much, as I had an Ultimate Skill that I could wield at full power. Beelzebuth was just the test.

The main Ultimate Skill I wanted to master in Art form was Metatron, Lord of Purity. Even when operating at only 70% of its true capabilities, it could one shot True Dragons. I wanted it at 100%, if only for the raw destructive power it offered. I could only match that level of destruction with Hollow Purple. Hollow Purple was also something I've been experimenting with on the side.

I had managed to give it a beam form similar to Disintegration. The next step I wanted to do was coat it over Yamato, similar to Hinata's Melt Slash.

But that was for later. It had been a while since I had a real training arc, so I was a bit excited.

Metatron's essence was that of purification. It basically purifies all positive spiritual energy, physical matter, and magical energy like a water filter, but anything negative or not sourced in spiritrons it can't purify. Basically, those particles are too small and pass through the filter, but there weren't many energies not sourced from spiritrons. Only stardust and minus energy from the abyss of the Daemon Realm were the ones I knew of.

Essentially, someone with Metatron could no sell any and all attacks sent at them if they made use of any spiritron-based energy, as they could purify the attack down to the spiritron.

Literally everything was made of spiritrons in some way, shape, or form, so even the natural environment could be converted into spiritrons and used. There was also the fact that Metatron had internal functions as well, but I wasn't focused on those right now.

Of course, attempting to recreate Metatron in Art form would be tougher, as it was an extremely destructive Skill by nature. So without having the fine control over it that Brahma offered me, chances were I was going to blow shit up.

'Do you mind making sure the dimension doesn't blow up, Othinus?'

"As you wish."

And with that I got to work.

- Hinata Sakaguchi -

She looked at herself in the mirror, adjusting the collar of her blouse for what felt like the tenth time. Hinata Sakaguchi was not the type to fuss over appearances, but today was different. She had been in her room, going through her wardrobe for over an hour. When it took her a moment to swap between clothing… She had gone through quite a lot of outfits.

She sighed, brushing a lock of dark hair behind her ear before stepping back to examine the outfit she had settled on. It was a rather simple yet elegant dress that, while modest, still accentuated her figure.

It felt rather odd to wear such an outfit. She wasn't used to this kind of thing. She was usually in her Paladin's robes, but this wasn't a battlefield, and she wasn't preparing for combat, even though she felt like she was.

Or maybe she was? Maybe this could be considered a different kind of combat?

She nodded. Framing it like that made it no different than a monster slaying quest. She would succeed, as she always did.

Still, for some odd reason, it felt just as nerve-wracking, if not more than even her most dangerous monster slaying quest.

She felt less nervous when she set off to seal Veldora!

With a shake of her head, Hinata turned away and picked up another outfit; a more practical one, something she could move in without feeling restricted. She held it up against herself and frowned. No, that wouldn't do.

She didn't want to wear something practical. As Luminous had said, she wished to enjoy herself.

Her fingers brushed against the fabric of a third option. It was a sleek, fitted outfit that was a bit more balanced. It had both elegance and comfort, and did not show much skin.

Her heartbeat quickened. Was she really this concerned about what he'd think?

Truly, he had far too much control over her without even trying.

Perhaps something was wrong with her?

This was the first time she had felt anything like what she had felt for Felix. The thought of seeing him again is what pushed her through the centuries of acting as the Hero Chronoa. It wasn't that she did not enjoy helping people, but it felt like there was far more purpose when there was an end goal to be achieved.

Her end goal was seeing Felix again, to solve some regrets that she didn't even know she had, and to see her friends again.

She exhaled slowly, setting the rejected outfits aside and slipping into the one she had finally chosen. Taking one last glance at the mirror, she straightened her posture and steeled herself.

She had fought battles almost her entire life.

This was just another one.

Right?

Hinata smoothed the fabric of her dress with steady hands, but the tension in her shoulders betrayed her unease. The logical part of her mind scoffed at how ridiculous this was. She had stood unwavering before Demon Lords, had clashed blades with the mightiest of foes, she had met blades with Guy Crimson without hesitation!

And yet, here she was, hesitating over something as trivial as a date. She truly was pathetic.

She clenched her fist at her side, willing herself to calm down. She had already wasted too much time deliberating over her appearance. If she stalled any longer, she might start questioning herself again, and that was unacceptable. She was a True Hero, one of the strongest individuals in the Cardinal World.

She turned from the mirror and walked toward the door.

Her hand hesitated on the doorknob.

What if…

No.

She inhaled sharply, pushing the thought aside. There was no point in doubting herself now. Luminous had encouraged her to enjoy this moment, and for once, she would allow herself that luxury.

With one last glance at her reflection, she took a breath, and stepped out into the evening air.

She had been in her home in Lune, a home she had been given by Luminous long ago. She looked up to the clear sky, before looking back straight ahead. Civilians were in the process of reorganizing themselves after the attack.

She took a deep breath, calling upon Space-Time Manipulation, and teleporting herself to Felix's territory.

- Felix -

I sighed in frustration after a few hours of trying to replicate Metatron.

I wasn't quite successful in replicating the phenomena that Metatron invoked. It sounded simple, but it was anything but that. Stripping an energy source of all the extras, leaving only the spiritrons was extremely tough and required quite a lot of control. Especially since in combat, a lot of the energy being thrown around isn't going to be your own, making it even more difficult to purify it as an enemies' attributes would be mixed in making it more complex.

Metatron, Lord of Purity really was an incredible Skill.

I had managed to succeed to a certain extent, purifying magicules into pure spiritrons, but it was a time consuming process, far from the speeds Metatron did it at. So while I was getting there, I wasn't quite where I wanted to be on that front.

I understood in theory how Metatron worked as I had the data on it, I understood the Laws it functioned under, but I was having some trouble associating with the concept of "purity". I wasn't a very pure individual after all, but I'd get it down.

Not to mention that the sheer processing power one needed to replicate Metatron on their own was at the level of a Manas, easily. About a tenth of Othinus' processing power, I'd say, which went to show just how absurd Othinus was.

I was not Othinus, so I did not have the same level of calculative ability as she did. A Though Acceleration x10 from Othinus would get her a lot further than a Thought Acceleration at the same level for me.

So of course while the Thought Acceleration I had was extremely potent, it did not put me at the level of a Manas, though I was very close according to Othinus. I expected that Guy and Milim were at that level. They had been improving themselves for thousands of years, so it wasn't unexpected that even mentally, they were superior to the majority of the world.

I was getting there. I had been going through some exercises to increase my own computational ability as it wasn't something that could be upgraded like a Skill could, so it wasn't like I hadn't been developing it all this time.

After I got Metatron, Lord of Purity down, my goal was to master Faust's Probability Manipulation. It was a good ability that had been underused until this point, though I hadn't really needed to use it in any fights. But now I want to be prepared, just in case. Using it at 70% and 100% could just matter in the future.

I had made good progress, so I was satisfied enough for today. This was never going to be a one day training montage, it would take me time to get what I wanted to learn down.

With that I appeared back in my private room.

As I lounged on one of the loveseats in my large room I ran through the various things I had to do before going to the world of Solo Leveling. The times would be synced so that Othinus could get more data on the flow of time in different worlds, meaning time would flow at the same space in both worlds as the Voice of the World would sort of initiate that kind of connection between the worlds through my Planeswalker sub-skill of Ouroboros.

It was because of that that I didn't want to leave some things just hanging around. I wanted to speak with Elmesia to ensure her assistance with the upcoming war. I'll give her Laplace as a bribe of sorts for that reason as well. I was going to give her Laplace just like that, but I couldn't afford to just be nice now.

We might not even need the help of her, or her dynasty. We had the support of Guy, by extension that meant Velzard, I was no push over either. And then we had Veldora, Rimuru, Milim, Chloe, Hinata, Luminous, hopefully Dagruel, and many more allies, but I wanted to ensure all the cards were in our favor.

I may have been confident, but that didn't mean it had to be stupid confidence.

Not to mention the more leisure activities I wanted to have before leaving, like my date with Hinata, and Arcueid. Arranging Ingvild's concert would be pretty easy as I would just need to tell the right people to get on it. The interrogation with Gadra was also somewhat urgent as he may have more useful information on the Eastern Empire.

The spar with Chloe could wait for a little bit, as well as the spar that I had offered Arcueid, Megumin, and Lalatina. I had offered them to all come at me together, and they took it well and agreed. Perhaps they could learn some things in the spar, and learn to fight together better as well, since that wasn't something they really did, and it may just be needed in the future.

Before I could continue listing out what I wanted to get done, I felt space bend as a familiar presence appeared in my palace. I could have easily blocked the teleportation, but I had no reason to prevent my adorable Hinata from coming to see me.

We had a date to plan after all! Maybe I could even convince her to have one now. I had actually been looking forward to it quite a bit after all. If not, I would still be open to just hanging out with her for a little bit before she inevitably had to return to Ruberious. She was a hard worker, if nothing else.

I stood up from my chair, took a step forward, and appeared in front of Hinata.

My eyes widened upon looking at her state of dress. She wasn't dressed in anything super crazy, I just wasn't used to seeing her like this. She wore a sleek dress that hugged her curves, but not too tightly. Minimal skin was shown, but I wasn't going to complain. The dress suited Hinata.

A grin slowly spread on my lips. "You look great Hinata! It seems you're ready for our date then?" I could read between the lines; she wouldn't come here like this for no reason.

I am highly motivated by your guys' reviews and likes, so do that! I'll probably keep writing or something.

Chapter 122: Date with a True Hero

- Velzard -

A vicious scowl formed upon her face once Guy teleported away. He had planned to go to Tempest after he met with Dagruel to speak about a few things. Guy had said he wished to see what that Slime, Rimuru Tempest, was up to with taking control of the Council of the West.

Felix, and even Rimuru, were becoming new sources of… interest for Guy. Both had awakened their own Ultimate Skills, which was impressive, but she was not happy.

She had originally thought that Guy's interest in Felix would wane, and by extension Rimuru. They were no Rudras, after all. Guy had never even used half of his true power in any of his spars against Felix, making her think that Felix had fallen short of Rudra in Guy's mind.

She liked Felix. He was an interesting Daemon, and she was grateful to him for being her troublesome little brother's friend. Her and Velgrynd had tried many things in the past to get Veldora to cooperate. However, while he was born with incredible amounts of potential, all of it remained untapped due to his little ego.

His intelligence was so little back then, that the only thing he could think of and enjoy was causing wanton destruction. It was the mindset of an animal, nothing more. No matter how much they tried to explain, he would not listen, and so began the cycle of destruction for him.

Now, however, it seemed something had changed. Now his ego was strong; strong enough to acquire an Ultimate Skill, and she was happy for him.

Now she was willing to entertain Felix's company so long as he did not draw Guy's attention for long. But it had been long, and Guy could still be seen with his happy-go-lucky smirk. Perhaps a few mere months was not long in her total lifespan, but ordinarily nothing drew his attention for so long.

And she knew it was because of the new variables that had appeared, because of Felix. Because Felix would help Guy in his game against Rudra. Because Felix was strong.

She could admit to herself that she was worried once she heard that Guy gave the data of Lucifer, Lord of Pride over to Felix. That was something he hadn't done for anyone before, not even for her, not even Velda. Though her elder brother didn't ask.

Most importantly, even Rudra did not receive such an honor. Felix's abilities gave him an incredible amount of potential, as while compatibility played a part in how well one could wield an Ultimate Skill, copying them was still an extremely useful ability. It gave the user understanding over the Laws the Ultimate Skill manipulated, and in this world, knowledge was just as valuable as power.

It was how Guy had managed to fight her evenly. His sheer knowledge and skill alone allowed him to fight on the same level as True Dragons without the power of a True Dragon.

Though that changed once her brother gave him his weapon. After that, he could even match the raw power of her.

Lucifer, Lord of Pride was more than just any Ultimate Skill. It was the manifestation of Guy's pride, something that could tip the balance in ways even she couldn't fully predict. For Guy to hand over such data to Felix meant that he saw the Daemon as more than just an amusing distraction. He saw him as perhaps… an equal. Someone worthy of holding such an important piece of data, and someone he trusted with it.

For while what Felix did for Guy was something to be grateful for, it gave Guy two Devil Lords under his command. For him to give Lucifer, Lord of Pride over for it was something she would have never seen coming.

Two Devil Lords would assist Guy greatly in the upcoming war against Rudra. A single Primordial Devil Lord was far more valuable than the average True Demon Lord. The sheer breadth of knowledge each possessed could not be underestimated.

And that, more than anything, infuriated her. She envied Felix beyond measure. She wanted what he had. It was almost a desperate desire. He had managed to get Guy's respect. He had managed to gain Guy's interest and desire. It was always them and not her.

Her Unique Skill: Envy bubbled up to the surface, its own desire aligning with hers, her desire to want, and to take what they had.

A deep chill settled into Velzard's gut, something she rarely felt. She had always been confident in her own power, in her place by Guy's side. She was the Frost Dragon, one of the strongest beings in existence.

But things were changing.

You're deluding yourself, you always knew you weren't good enough

Her lips curved downwards as the voice in the back of her head made itself known.

Guy was always kind to her, and yet he wouldn't let her properly stand next to him.

Because you're weak.

No! She was the strongest of True Dragon-kind under her elder brother!

You are weak, that is why Guy does not truly acknowledge you.

No! I have the right to stand next to him too!!

Do you truly?

Of course!

If that's the case, then why did Guy only play with Rudra? Why does he only show interest in Felix and not you? Never you?

That's…

It's because you are weak. You have always been weak

Was she… weak?

If you were stronger, Guy would look at you.

He will look at me?

Yes, that's right. if you were stronger.

She'd be able to stand next to Guy…

She needed to ask Twilight for his advice. He had been a constant ally in her goals to stand next to Guy. Only right now, he was in an evolutionary sleep, less for evolutionary reasons and more because an experiment of his went wrong according to him. And now he needed to rest to recuperate some of his lost soul energy.

Her and Twilight's partnership went back thousands of years. He had come to her to ask for assistance in an experiment. She refused at first, but then Twilight offered to assist her in her goal of getting Guy to truly recognize her. With that, she agreed, as her only goal had been for Guy to truly recognize her.

Twilight wished for her to freeze his ego, merely out of his own curiosity to see what would happen. She succeeded in freezing his ego as she knew she would. She was not called the Frost Dragon for nothing. She could freeze anything she put her mind to; Information Particles, spiritrons, souls, soul corridors, and more.

Thanks to Twilight's ego being frozen, they discovered that he could no longer change as an individual. His personality was locked to the one he had when she froze his ego.

She went on to replicate this process in herself, so her ego would forever remain the same, her personality would remain steady.

Thanks to this, should she even die and reincarnate as all True Dragons were capable of, she would remain the exact same. As when True Dragons died, they retained most of their previous incarnations' memories. It was merely that the egos were different, which changed the personality. This would not apply to her.

At that point, Twilight was obsessed with the karmic fates of surpassing their parent and killing God, and so he stayed that way. His ambitions would remain the same from that day forth.

He wished to show her brother that it was possible for the child to surpass the parent; a desire that was engraved in Twilight since birth.

In fact, she would consider it a curse; a curse her elder brother engraved in a few individuals. One meant to compel them to surpass him, Veldanava, the creator of this world. One he placed in those who he believed were capable of it. An ambition that would remain unfulfilled.

She thought it was a foolish ambition, as her brother's will reigned supreme, but Twilight still persisted, as did the others her brother cursed with that ambition. Twilight dubbed the curse the "God Killing Curse".

This curse also had the possibility of passing onto one's child. Twilight wished to observe the curse in action as it had passed onto his daughter, Luminous. And so he arranged things so that Luminous would kill a version of him, a split consciousness, all while his true self inhabited her. With this, the curse on Luminous also faded away, satisfying the condition behind it, and Twilight got to observe it in action.

That was the story behind Twilight Valentine's death. It was all a mere hoax to satisfy his curiosity, and his daughter played her part perfectly.

And now, to this day, he remained inside of her, assisting her with her goals while he had his own things he did on the side through his parallel consciousness. No one knew of this, not even Guy.

He had become a new kind of lifeform, one she had not even heard about until Twilight told her about it. He was a Manas, a completely Digital Lifeform with the ability to freely manipulate Information Particles and exist as an Information Body.

Of course, due to her elder brother's death, the God Killer Curse remained unsatisfied, and so Twilight had to distract himself in other ways, or he would just put himself to sleep for sometime to recover from the strain of the curse.

It wasn't until recently that he began showing interest in the state of the world once more.

Even he was interested in the two new Demon Lords, both Felix and Rimuru.

Her fists clenched as the air around her grew even frostier. The frost thickened, forming an intricate pattern of ice along the grand chamber's ice floor.

The moisture crystallized into delicate snowflakes that drifted listlessly before vanishing into nothingness. Velzard's emotions stirred the very essence of her being, and the world responded in kind.

She let out a slow breath, watching it coil into a visible mist before her eyes. Even Twilight seemed more interested in Felix than in helping her. Just before he fell into his temporary coma, he had been laughing madly, saying that he had underestimated Felix before saying that he would need to go to sleep for some time. She wasn't even able to get a word in before she felt Twilight's presence vanish.

"Felix…" The name alone sent a pulse of ice outward, shattering the fragile frost into glistening shards.

What made him so special? Why had Guy placed such faith in him?

She closed her eyes, allowing the cold to seep into her core, into the deepest recesses of her mind where her Envy grew. Even her thoughts froze over, crystallizing into sharp, jagged doubts that cut her more than she cared to admit.

What should she do?

- Felix -

I stood up from my chair, took a step forward, and appeared in front of Hinata.

My eyes widened upon looking at her state of dress. She wasn't dressed in anything super crazy, I just wasn't used to seeing her like this. She wore a sleek dress that hugged her curves, but not too tightly. Minimal skin was shown, but I wasn't going to complain. The dress suited Hinata.

A grin slowly spread on my lips. "You look great Hinata! It seems you're ready for our date then?"

I originally expected for us to actually plan the date first, but it seems she wanted to just wing it, which I was fine with. There were still a few hours left in the day, which was rather absurd when you thought about it.

So much happened in the last two days. There was the attack, the discussion with Guy, the discussion I had in Tempest, speaking to Damrada again, and more.

Perhaps a normal person would be rather pressed about doing everything I had today, but I had a far higher tolerance for those kinds of things. It didn't hurt that I had an absurd amount of stamina, enough that I could fight for weeks at a time.

So the amount of events that happened today wasn't bothersome for me. Doing a bit of real work here and there wasn't bad when I spent most of my days doing what I wanted.

Raiden and Saeko's fight had already finished, and both were recovering from it. The fight was quite something. Raiden attempted a few new techniques that seemed to have a lot of potential while Saeko perfected what she had.

Saeko would have won if she was facing the Raiden from before she got the Unique Skill: Maid, since as it was, Raiden's Unique Skill helped her a lot in the fight. Saeko just had a more hax ability, making it difficult to face her on the same tier, but Raiden's new Maid Skill was also rather good.

In the end, Saeko used her Divine Berserker Unique Skill, which temporarily allowed her to spiritualize and dramatically elevated her combat power at the cost of a lot of energy. Raiden managed to mimic this to a certain degree by turning herself into physical lightning. As a being also completely made out of energy at that point, she was able to go toe-to-toe with a spiritualized Saeko.

In the end, the both of them had improved an incredible amount and I was proud of them.

I planned to have Raiden, Saeko, and Kurumi go through the Life Reconstruction soon. Since the process had been optimized by Othinus, it would only take 50,000 souls for each of them, 150,000 total.

After Arcueid, Megumin, and Lalatina's Life Reconstructions I still had 1,250,000 souls so I would have enough.

In theory, Life Reconstruction could scale pretty far. However, there was an issue of compatibility and potential with Arcueid, Megumin, Lalatina, Saeko, Raiden, and Kurumi.

The souls were of High Humans, so there was only a limited amount of improvement they could provide. If I had 1,000,000 Oni souls, then Saeko could theoretically infinitely go through Life Reconstruction until I ran out of Oni souls.

However, that's when potential came in. At a certain point, your soul and body won't be able to handle all that energy, which is when you have reached your potential so you cannot improve anymore. So while Life Reconstruction was broken, it was still a dangerous Art that could go wrong, and tended to be useless after a certain point.

Damrada seemed to be getting settled in just fine. He hadn't challenged anyone to a fight yet like I thought he would, but I knew he would eventually. Arcueid had informed me that she had decided on Damrada's role. He was basically going to be managing the Council of the West for her, so he would likely be away quite often which was fine with me.

The two seemingly had a fruitful discussion. At the very least, Arcueid seemed to approve of him, which was not easy.

Hinata rolled her eyes at my grin but didn't refute the compliment. That was progress. She shifted slightly, folding her arms beneath her chest as she let out a small huff.

"If I wasn't ready, I wouldn't be here." She said, her usual sharp tone softened just a little.

I chuckled. It was a classic Hinata maneuver. Even when she was clearly flustered, she maintained that unwavering confidence. But I could see the tiny hints of hesitation in the way she kept adjusting her stance; her fingers lightly brushing against the fabric of her dress. It must have been something to break through her control.

She was nervous.

And that was honestly adorable.

"Well, I'm honored." I said, extending a hand toward her with a playful smirk. "Since we're apparently just going with the flow, shall we get going?"

As I said that, I went through the various things I could do with her. Thought Acceleration really was great.

I promised to show her the Harry Potter movies when I mentioned the wall back in Lune being similar to the entrance to Diagon Alley, but that would take a few hours to properly get through, so we can do that another time. For a movie date, it wouldn't do to accelerate it even if we could understand it even at extremely high speeds.

Movies ought to be enjoyed the way they were made. I was a purist like that.

What would Hinata enjoy? She wasn't some delicate wallflower, but she was still feminine in nature, so I think she'd enjoy some more traditional date activities, and that wasn't me just stereotyping either. I'd like to say I knew her fairly well by this point, so I was pretty sure I was right.

At the very least, I don't think she'd look at me very fondly if I said we can just spar.

I had game! I wouldn't make that kind of rookie mistake!

Hinata gave me a look, but I caught the faintest hint of amusement in her eyes before she sighed and finally placed her hand in mine.

I squeezed her hand gently which seemed to fluster Hinata. "D-Don't squeeze so tightly!" She said as she turned her head to the side, attempting to hide her embarrassment.

Ah, she really was too much fun to tease.

I chuckled, loosening my grip slightly but not letting go. "My bad, my bad." I said, though I made no attempt to hide the grin on my face. "Didn't expect you to be this delicate, Hinata." I said, knowing my words would annoy her.

Her head snapped back toward me, eyes narrowing in that familiar glare. "I am not delicate."

I laughed outright at that. "Relax, I'm just messing with you."

She huffed, but I could tell she wasn't actually mad. If anything, I could see the tension in her shoulders slowly easing up, just as I hoped for. Messing with Hinata usually got her to ease up a bit. It would be no fun if she was stiff the entire date.

Now, back to the plan.

"I think I know what to do."

Hinata smiled. "I will leave it in your hands then."

Still holding her hand, I gave a light tug, leading her forward, she complied without resistance.

With Thought Acceleration still running, I quickly mapped out the best plan. Nothing too extravagant, as I didn't think Hinata would enjoy something too crazy to start out with. I think she'd like something simple and enjoyable.

I decided to take her to a city a little ways off from my capital city, one that had developed significantly since I took over this territory and had Arcueid begin improving the living situation of my citizens.

I had been to it once before, just to take a look at some other cities in my territory. It had a lively night market, a few nice restaurants, and, most importantly, good food.

Before she could question where we were going, I teleported us, and in an instant, we appeared right at the market's entrance.

It was evening now so the market was in full swing. There were lanterns that lit up the streets. The air was filled with the scent of sizzling meats and sweet pastries. A bunch of people were laughing and talking, just enjoying their lives. Merchants called out their best deals, and couples strolled past, some linking arms, others just enjoying the atmosphere.

I had placed the two of us under an illusion as I teleported us, so no one would recognize us.

Hinata blinked, momentarily thrown off by the sudden change in scenery. "You really don't waste time, do you?" She said as she looked around. I took note of what her eyes seemed to be drawn to.

"Why would I?" I shot her a grin. "Time is precious, and so is good food."

Hinata nodded seriously. "Indeed. Good food is important." She said. I smirked. Hinata was a foodie through-and-through.

I gave her hand a slight squeeze. Not enough to fluster her this time, but just enough to remind her I was still holding it. She glanced at our hands briefly but didn't pull away.

"Alright then," I continued, leading her into the market. "I figured we'd just go with the flow. Sample some food, take in the sights, stuff like that."

"A rather simple date."

"You don't like the plan?" I thought she'd enjoy something simple like this, but if she didn't I could arrange something else.

Hinata shook her head. "I didn't say that. I prefer more simple things like this."

"That's why I chose this based on your preferences."
Hearing me, a small smile grew on Hinata's face. "I see."

We strolled through the bustling market; the aroma of grilled skewers and freshly baked pastries filling the air. My senses picked up on everything; laughter from nearby stalls, the sizzling of meat, even the faint clink of coins being exchanged.

Events like this could really be a lot of fun from time to time. The food at these kinds of places was always amazing as well.

Hinata's attention was drawn to a nearby stand where a vendor was flipping some sort of deep-fried treat in hot oil. I smirked.

"Interested?"

She hesitated, then nodded slightly. "I've never seen this before."

"It's really rather good. Not all good food has to originate from earth." I said as I led us to the stall in question.

I walked up to the vendor and ordered two servings. The man handed us each a skewer with golden, crispy pastries drizzled with honey. I took a bite, humming in approval.

Hinata, ever the cautious one, examined hers first before taking a small bite.

Her eyes widened just a fraction.

I grinned. "Good?"

"Nn." She nodded as she took another bite.

We continued walking, stopping at various stalls. At one point, we passed by a game stand where people were trying (and mostly failing) to knock down stacked bottles with a small ball. I glanced at Hinata.

It was a cliche for a reason, and so I would fulfill the trope as I was obligated to.

There were prizes littered behind the stall, but when I read the stall owner's mind I found out that he had a special reward for couples that did exceptionally well so I changed my plan a bit.

Hinata seemed to have noticed my interest. "What?"

I knew just how to get her to play with me. "Think you can win?"

She scoffed. "Please."

The two of us stepped closer to the stall. I handed the vendor some coins. "Two rounds."

The vendor grinned, setting up the game while Hinata and I waited.

I tossed the ball in my hand as I examined the set up.

Once the game was all set up, I went first. I casually flicked the ball with just enough force to knock down every single bottle in one go. The vendor gawked, and a few bystanders murmured in surprise.

I turned to Hinata, grinning. "Your turn."

She exhaled, rolled her shoulders, and threw the ball.

It hit dead center, toppling all the bottles with precise accuracy.

The vendor blinked. "…Huh."

I let out a low whistle. "Not bad."

She crossed her arms, smug. "You sound surprised."

"Nah, I just didn't expect the Hinata Sakaguchi to be so competitive about a game like this." I said as I muffled my voice so no one but Hinata could hear.

She gave me a flat look. "Says the one who started this."

I chuckled. "Fair."

The vendor, still stunned by our performance, let out an awkward chuckle before rubbing the back of his head. "Well, I'd say you two definitely earned yourselves a prize. Since you both cleared the game flawlessly, I have a special reward for couples like you." He said with a wink.

I raised a brow, already aware of what he had in mind but playing along anyway. "Special reward, huh?"

Hinata gave the vendor a skeptical look but didn't object.

With a grin, he reached behind the counter and pulled out a small, ornate-looking box. "This is a charm said to bring good fortune to couples. Handmade by a skilled artisan, it's a one-of-a-kind piece." He said in a traditional salesmany tone.

He opened the box to reveal a beautifully crafted bracelet, adorned with a small gem that seemed to shimmer under the market's lantern light. With a quick glance I could tell that the vendor was just bullshitting. There was no sort of special effect on the bracelet, Hinata could tell as well.

I glanced at Hinata, who was staring at the bracelet, her expression unreadable. I could sense the slightest hesitation in her aura, though.

Ah, this was perfect.

I reached out and took the bracelet before turning to Hinata with a teasing smirk. "Well, we won it together, so I think it's only fair that you wear it."

She blinked at me, caught off guard. "Why me?"

"Because it'd suit you better." I said smoothly.

Her lips parted slightly as if she was about to argue, but then she shut them again. She let out a small sigh. "Fine."

I grinned and, before she could take it from me, gently took her wrist and clasped the bracelet around it myself.

Hinata tensed for a moment before relaxing into my grip.

"There." I said, stepping back slightly to admire my handiwork. "Looks good on you."

She stared down at the bracelet for a moment, her fingers brushing over the gem before she looked back up at me. "…Thanks."

I smiled. "See? That wasn't so hard, was it?"

Her eyes narrowed, and she lightly smacked my arm. "Shut up."

I laughed.

The vendor, now grinning like an old man witnessing young love, waved us off. "Enjoy the rest of your night, you two." He said as he winked at me in particular.

As Hinata and I were finishing up our last snack, I went through what we had done tonight. It was a rather successful date, all things considered.

After the game, we walked around, played a few more games, ate good food, and spoke about various things.

I didn't ask about anything related to Ruberious or anything, as that was a bit more work related and had no place on a date.

There was one more thing I had to talk to Hinata about, which I would do once we left.

This date was more of a test run, if you ask me. Something to give us both an idea of what the other was like in a romantic sense. One date was far from enough for something like that, but it did give both of us a general idea of the expectations of one another, and it was successful in that purpose. Not to mention the date itself was also pretty enjoyable.

It was rather simple, but sometimes it wasn't about what you did, but who you did it with.

It didn't take much longer for us to finish up both of our churros. The night market was winding down now, so there wasn't much left to do.

"Is there anything else you want to do?" I asked Hinata.

She shook her head, a slight rosy tint to her cheeks. "No, this was wonderful. Thank you Felix."
"I should be the one thanking you. It's not everyday I get to go on a date with a woman as wonderful as you."

Hinata's lips twitched. "Hmph!" Outwardly she seemed exasperated, but through Lover, I could tell she was happy at the compliment.

With that, I teleported the two of us back to my palace. More specifically, one of the studies that were littered around. I didn't take us to my room or anything. This was only the first date and Hinata was a more traditional type of woman and I didn't want to push her into doing something she wasn't committed to.

She looked around, examining the surroundings. I could sense some relief inside of her, but surprisingly there was also some disappointment. I ignored that for now.

"Take a seat." I said while gesturing to one of the love seats. As Hinata did so I walked over to the wine cupboard in the corner of the room, picked up two glasses and a bottle before taking my seat across from Hinata.

I served her a glass of wine before taking a glass for myself. After taking a sip I looked her in the eyes.

She took a sip, savoring the taste before setting the glass down. "So," She said, crossing one leg over the other. "What is it you wanted to discuss?"

I exhaled softly. "I won't beat around the bush." I met her gaze evenly. "You're aware that I already have other lovers." This was a talk to get out of the way at the start. If Hinata wasn't okay with such a thing then there was no point in going forward with whatever it was that was developing.

I did like and care for Hinata, despite the odds. When we first met I never would have considered such a thing happening. She just wasn't my type back then. But things change; people change.

Hinata didn't flinch, but I noticed her fingers subtly tightening around the stem of her glass.

"I did." She admitted.

I nodded. "I wanted to make it clear from the start, so that you are aware of what you are getting into before anything is taken too deep. I respect you too much to deceive you or let you think this was something different."

I sensed a spike of her emotions at my words. A complex mix of them, as well, making it hard to decipher. Joy at my respect for her, jealousy for not having my sole attention, appreciation for my honesty, and even a hint of adoration for just looking out for her.

The jealousy was strong, but her other emotions overpowered it.

Unlike all my other lovers, Hinata was not raised in this world. She may have spent more time on this world than her earth, but her early formative years still made her who she was. A part of her still had that lingering attachment to how things worked back on earth. Two people got married and had a monogamous relationship. That was just how it went generally. Not that there weren't those who defied the odds, but that was what you were "supposed" to do.

She sighed as her violet eyes studied me carefully. "Do you think I would be fine with that?" She asked.

I decided to be honest. "I don't expect anything. I don't expect you to accept right away or ever, this is definitely something unusual by your standards. But I want to be honest with you, Hinata. I care about you, and I don't want this, whatever it is between us, to be built on half-truths or unspoken expectations."

She swirled the wine in her glass, thinking. "You're lucky I already knew this about you." A small smirk played on her lips, though there was still something serious in her gaze. "If I didn't, I might have thrown this glass at you."

I chuckled. "Maybe that would have done something if my Infinity wouldn't have caught it."

Hinata's lips twitched as she held back her smile.

She let out a soft huff, setting her glass down on the table between us. "Felix, you're insufferable."

I smiled at returning to our usual byplay.

Things seemed to have gone as good as they could have, all things considered.

Hinata sighed, resting her elbow on the armrest and propping her chin against her hand. Her violet eyes studied me, as if searching for something. Doubt, insincerity, weakness; whatever it was, she wouldn't find it.

"I never expected to be having this type of conversation with you." Hinata said as she swirled her glass.

I smirked. "I didn't expect this either, you know. You were rather insufferable when we first met. I didn't really like you."

To be fair, she did have some admirable qualities back then, I just didn't like her because of what she did to Rimuru, or rather what she tried to do to him.

Hinata rolled her eyes. "I do believe I understood that from the moment you beat me to the ground with a stick." I still had that stick somewhere in my Infinity Space. Maybe I should bring it out whenever we fight next?

"Ah, good times." I said as I leaned back. Hinata shot me the middle finger, making me laugh. It seems her old Japanese politeness had faded quite a bit. Japanese people were all about manners. The culture emphasizes harmony, cooperation, and respect for authority, which worked for them.

"I won't lie and say I like it." She admitted. "The idea of sharing someone I care about… it was never something I expected in my life. Though I never expected something like this in the first place." She said honestly.

"That's fair." I nodded, allowing her the space to speak her mind. While polygamy was normal in this world among those with influence, I could still respect Hinata's hesitance to partake in something like that.

"When I came to this goal and developed my dream, I never considered any sort of companionship that would be lasting as possible. And it wouldn't have been if I hadn't been forced to confront some things after I was sent to the past with Chloe." She said honestly. "And with my history, I never thought I was worthy of such a thing either." She added.

"But," She continued, her voice softer. "I can't say I dislike you either. I think I would dislike it more if I were to allow any obstacles to get in the way at this point."

That caught my attention.

A smirk tugged at my lips. "Is that so?"

"Don't let it go to your head." She warned, pointing a finger at me.

"Me? I'd never." I said dramatically before I leaned forwards. "I don't need an answer now, Hinata. This is your choice, and I don't want you to feel forced into anything. I care about you, and I want you to be happy, whether that's with me or not."

Despite everything, I didn't want to become the kind of person who stopped caring for their close ones, the kind of person that prioritized themselves over everything that also mattered. I may be selfish, but that selfishness was balanced out by my other, more positive traits.

Hinata's eyes widened slightly before she looked to the side, a blush covering her cheeks. She quickly picked up her glass, taking a sip to hide her expression. Once she put it back down, she had regained her control.

I watched as she composed herself; a small smirk still tugging at the corners of my lips. Seeing Hinata embarrassed was always a treat. She was just so adorable about it, though her teaseability had gone down ever since she returned from the past as she had grown up a bit, making moments like this rare.

She cleared her throat. "I appreciate that, Felix."

I leaned back, giving her space. "No rush, I meant what I said."
