Chapter 144: Picking up a Nuke

- Felix -

I finished my wine and set the glass down. "I'll come to your little conference. I've been wanting to explore this world, so this is another good opportunity."

Plus I was curious about a few people. I did tell Gunhee to keep an eye on the other Ruler vessels, so maybe some of them will actually manage to survive.

Adam nodded. "I will arrange a tour for you upon arrival." He said, already shifting into professional mode.

He told me the details of the conference and said that he would return to Korea to pick me and the Korean Hunters Association's representative.

I had already confirmed that I could bring a few people with me if I wanted. That wasn't supposed to be allowed, but the American Hunters Association was hosting this event, so they had some leeway when it came to the rules.

Interestingly enough, he asked nothing about my otherworldly origin. I guess he knew that sometimes ignorance was bliss. He just came here, did his job, and that was that.

He didn't try to recruit me or anything like he did to Jin-Woo either. The United States was really playing it safe when it came to me.

"I thank you for your time." Adam said as he stood up.

I nodded. "I'll see you then."

Adam nodded and left.

Now I had some time to kill, and I had a few ideas on what I wanted to do.

It had only been a few days since I left the Cardinal World, but I was already missing the chaos and fun that came with my friends.

Rimuru was likely still busy with taking the kids to their home worlds, so I'd go back to pick him, Veldora, and Ramiris up in a few days.

I could still pick up Milim, Gaia, Hinata, and Luminous now, though.

Through the ring I gave each of them I began individually contacting them.

"Felix! Is it time?!" Milim's voice came through, bursting with energy and excitement.

I couldn't help but smile. "Yeah, I'll come to pick you up soon. Just wanted to check if you were ready."

"Yay! I'll go get Gaia!" She said, and just like that, the connection cut before I could even tell her when I'd be coming.

I couldn't help but smile in fondness at her antics. She may have seemed like a child, but she really was a good friend to have.

The next ring I willed my ring to connect to was Hinata's.

"Felix?" She asked with some surprise.

"Miss me?" I asked cheekily.

"If that is what you would like to imagine, then by all means do so." Hinata responded after a moment.

"I can feel the eyeroll even worlds away." I responded.

"Fufufu, I wonder why?" Hinata responded back cheekily.

After a moment we both laughed.

"So how have things been there?" I asked.

"Mostly fine. Not everything is back to normal after the attack but things are getting there. Luminous has used the incident as an excuse to clean up the higher ups of the Western Holy Church, and I am the one responsible for that."

It's not like Luminous couldn't just purge anyone she wanted, and that too while keeping it hidden, but in the long run it would make things a bit more annoying if she just killed whoever willy-nilly.

It would destabilize the carefully constructed hierarchy within the Western Church, those higher ups also had duties of their own so others would have to scramble to make sure those duties were still completed.

The reason Luminous killed the Luminaries almost right when she found an excuse to was because they just didn't offer anything more to the Western Holy Church as Luminous explained to me. They were close to her once upon a time, but they had betrayed her trust, and that was something Luminous wouldn't tolerate.

They rarely took any disciples and were content to lord their power over their underlings. That was about all they did in the recent centuries according to Luminous.

"I was going to ask if you were ready to come to this world, but if you're busy we can reschedule."

Hinata had agreed to come with me, but she was always someone who valued her duties, so I wouldn't blame her if she changed her mind.

After a brief pause Hinata replied. "I will be busy for the next couple days, but after that I believe I can leave for some time without my presence being needed back here."

"That works for me. Let me know if you need help."

I could feel Hinata's exasperation. "I am more than capable of dealing with some corrupt old bastards, Felix."

"I'm not doubting that, but the offer is open." I responded, understanding without her needing to directly tell me.

Hinata was a grown woman, older than I was mentally in fact. She didn't need me to baby her or anything; she was more than strong enough to handle pretty much any threat within the bounds of the Western Nations.

It was her way of saying 'I appreciate it but I can handle myself' without saying anything else.

"I know, and I thank you for that, Felix." After a brief pause she continued. "How have things been for you there? I admit that I am rather curious about another Earth. It has been so long since I have seen the culture of my own country, and I would like to see it once more since the opportunity has presented itself."

"I've enjoyed myself. There are some pretty strong people in this world, but they aren't impossible to deal with. I've already made somewhat friendly relations with one of the bigger factions in this world." I said, referring to the Rulers. "I'm more just enjoying meeting some of the people and visiting certain places."

I planned to visit all the other realms of this universe that interested me after meeting with the Rulers. After because perhaps they could help me by telling me a bit about each place and even give me the coordinates so I have an easier time finding each realm.

"Hmm, I see."

I went on to tell Hinata a bit more about this world. I gave her a brief summary in the Cardinal World, but didn't go into detail back then since it wasn't relevant.

I told her about the Monarchs, the Rulers, and what was at stake in this world. I also told her a bit more about Hunter society and how the world managed under the appearance of mana.

"It seems that society has managed to restructure itself to retain order then." Hinata said with some approval. She was always one that preferred order, as was clear due to her allegiance to Ruberious, one of the most orderly kingdoms in the Cardinal World.

"I suppose you could say that."

This world did react to everything that happened rather well all things considered. It was easy to figure out the history of this world through a quick online search, and while there were hiccups along the way with Hunters existing, beings with real tangible power, nothing ever devolved into chaos.

This was likely because of the Gates. With a common enemy, Humanity was far less prone to self-destructing.

"That world seems just as messed up as the Cardinal World's. A war beyond the scale Humanity is prepared for, beings who have been alive since the creation of the universe. Will the people of that universe be fine?" Hinata asked with some worry.

Well Hinata was a True Hero; it was just like her to worry about the common person. She may seem cruel to those who didn't know her, maybe even due to her being okay with how things in Ruberious were run, but she did care in her own way.

She had to be in order to have the approval of a Holy Spirit of Light.

"They'll manage just fine. The Rulers already have a large advantage since I took out three Monarchs, and if things go well their biggest threat, Antares, will be dealt with by the new Shadow Monarch."

"I will trust your judgment then." Hinata said with a sigh, though I could tell she'd definitely be lending a helping hand when she visited. I would lend a helping hand if it was needed, but I don't see my help being needed if things were mostly the same as the canon I read about.

"Who else did you bring with you?" Hinata eventually asked.

"Lalatina, Megumin, and Sukuna." I responded.

"How has Lalatina been?" Hinata asked after a moment.

I raised a brow at the odd question. "She's as normal as she can be. Why? I didn't think you two were particularly close."

"Maybe we aren't close, but I have interacted with her for quite a long time."

"Ah, right. Luminous told me how you fought Lalatina quite a bit in the past since she came to bother you."

After learning about Lalatina and Hinata's interactions in the past, I asked Lalatina more about it.

Apparently she and Luminous used to clash quite a bit in the past since Lalatina liked to play around in the Western Nations, and Luminous was establishing herself in the Western Nations.

One time when Lalatina went to go bother Luminous, Chronoa, or rather Hinata, was there.

Lalatina attacked Hinata since Luminous wasn't there, and then the rest was history.

Hinata sighed. "Indeed, she was incredibly persistent, and I had to hold back against her as I did not wish to cause any changes to the timeline."

"Are you implying that you'd win?" I asked teasingly.

"Of course." Hinata stated with certainty. "She was not even incarnated or named back then."

"Underestimating a Primordial is going to bite you in the ass someday."

I don't think Hinata even knew that Lalatina had an Ultimate Skill, and her mastery over it was rather high for the short period of time that she possessed it.

I was rather surprised that her Ultimate Skill was solely dedicated to combat pretty much due to her nature and her relationship with me, but after some thought, it did make sense.

She craved to be useful to me, and she was a Primordial. The biggest use in her eyes that she had was likely her combat power, so she elevated it further, especially since I made no move to dissuade her of that notion.

"I am aware of their danger. Now I must be leaving; Saare needs me." She said in a somewhat distracted manner.

"Good luck." Was all I said as I cut the communication.

After a moment I connected with the next person I wanted to speak with. "Hello Felix." Luminous said.

"How have things been, Luminous? I heard that you've kept Hinata busy."

"Of course. That girl and relaxing do not go together." Luminous said with a sigh. "I told her that the others could handle it, but she insisted on helping."

"That does sound like Hinata."

"Am I correct in assuming you are in this other world you told me about?" She asked.

"I am."

"How intriguing. I am rather curious about these other worlds."

Her curiosity and excitement did make sense. Due to her age, Luminous hadn't experienced anything new in who knows how long.

"Did you just think something about me?"

I blinked in confusion. Did the mythical 'woman's instinct' Skill apply even across dimensions?

"Ahem. Did you want me to come pick you up? I've already gotten things set up over here." I said, shifting the topic.

"Has Hinata agreed to come as well?" Luminous asked with some amusement as she let the topic go.

"She did, but she said in a couple of days as she was busy with her work."

"Very well then. When you come to pick her up, I will come. It would not do if I went to another world whilst she was here working."

"Sounds good then."

I doubt Luminous was actually doing much work, but it was the thought that counts.

After a brief moment, Luminous continued. "It has been rather quiet without you stirring up trouble everywhere." She said vaguely.

I smirked. "Oh my, is the great Luminous Valentine perhaps… missing her dear consort." I asked teasingly. She had called me her consort back on that date we had, and I enjoyed teasing her about it since she tended to get a bit embarrassed.

She was old, but she'd never had a consort before, her own words. But it was rapidly losing its effect on her as Luminous grew more used to the state of our relationship.

I could hear her huff through the communication. "Don't get too cocky. You are only a mere consort." She said haughtily.

"Well this mere consort is looking forward to accompanying you in this world."

"Oh?" Luminous purred, her voice laced with amusement. "Then I shall make sure to bring something appropriate for the occasion. I imagine you wouldn't want to be seen at my side unless I look the part."

I rolled my eyes. "You always look great." I replied smoothly. "But if you want to dress up for me, I won't complain."

"I wasn't going to dress up for you, per se." She countered, mock-serious tone of voice. "It is simply a matter of maintaining appearances."

"Sure, sure." I responded. Luminous enjoyed these conversations, as did I, so I wouldn't point out the holes in her argument.

She paused then sighed. "You are insufferable."

"Thanks! I pride myself in that fact, plus, aren't you here talking to me of your own volition?"

"Tch. Unfortunately for me, I've grown rather fond of my insufferable consort." She responded in a teasing manner, though there was sincerity behind it which made me smile.

"Likewise."

We then shifted into more casual topics. I asked about Saeko, and according to Luminous, she was somehow improving in her cooking abilities.

A true miracle.

Luminous asked a bit about the world itself, so I gave her the same story as Hinata, though unlike Hinata, Luminous didn't express any concern over the world. She trusted me enough to know that things were probably under control, which was sweet.

Our conversation didn't last much longer.

"Don't keep a lady waiting, Felix. I will see you."

"I won't. See ya."

With that, the connection between our rings ended. The next person I wanted to speak to before leaving to pick everyone up was Rimuru to see if he was busy or not.

I thought about speaking to Arcueid as well since I gave her a ring, but I planned to just stop by and see how she was in person.

"Felix? What's up? Things going well over there?" Rimuru asked.

"Yup, just calling to see if you, Veldora, and Ramiris are ready to visit."

Rimuru was rather excited since he could get a bunch of data on the modern inventions his people were trying to reinvent from scratch.

He told them what he wanted, but he wasn't an engineer in his old life, so the engineers under him were pretty much grasping at straws when it came to that stuff. Even Raphael didn't have data on a lot of the things that Rimuru described, so it came up with entirely new versions of what Rimuru wanted that needed to be made with various magical parts and have runes inscribed onto them which took time and resources.

Getting the data from this world would just make it easier for him.

"Uhh, I'm still managing the kids, explaining things to their parents, sealing their powers and whatnot, so I'll probably be busy for a few days."

"That's fine, Hinata said the same so I'll check back in when I go to pick her up then."

"How is the world? Is it anything like the manhwa?" Rimuru asked with excitement.

"So far it seems pretty much the same, though who knows if it'll stay that way."

"Has Sung Jin-Woo aura farmed in front of you yet?" Rimuru asked.

"He tried, but he can't really aura farm against any Monarchs in his current state."

"Monarchs? Just when did you arrive?" He asked with surprise.

"During the Jeju Island raid."

"And yet there were Monarchs? Weren't they supposed to show up later?"

"Yeah, they apparently sensed my arrival and followed me down to Earth. There was some dick measuring that resulted in a fight, and the death of three Monarchs."

"Yeah… I think you've changed things a lot then."

"Meh, in the grand scheme of things not really. The Rulers were pretty much set to win from the start so long as Jin-Woo becomes the Shadow Monarch."

"Yeah, whatever. I am excited to visit. I want to analyze all the dishes!"

I sighed. "Of course."

Rimuru made it seem like what he wanted was peace and whatnot, and he did. That was part of his dream, but what he was really after was a culture revolution in the Cardinal World.

He wanted all the modern amenities he enjoyed to be available to the people in his kingdom and the entire world. Peace was just part of that. Once that was all done, he'd be content with throwing all his authority away.

"Hey! Don't act as if you haven't been enjoying the fruits of my labor! It's because of me that you get to eat those tacos you like so much!" Rimuru protested.

"That's true. Keep doing what you're doing so I can enjoy the fruits of your labor while kicking back!"

"Bastard!" Was all Rimuru said as the connection was cut off.

I didn't even get to say my final piece. I was going to tell him that I had reconstructed Shizu's memories fully and with his help could place those memories into a pseudo soul to come up with a sort of pseudo revival.

I personally believed that the original Shizu, and this new Shizu that would be born would technically be different people, but Rimuru seemed fine with it, which I could understand.

One's memories and experiences made them who they were, and this Shizu would have all of those memories and experiences.

I suppose it was just a personal hang up that I had.

The issue I had with creating souls before was that despite having Brahma, Lord of Creation, souls were a bit too complex.

Even if I create a soul and imbue it with a person's memories with the intent of reviving them, in the end they would be more of a robot than truly autonomous, just following the guidelines the memories gave this new individual, they wouldn't really be capable of changing. There was some part of the soul that I was missing out on that allowed that continuous growth.

But that gap could be bridged by Rimuru's artificially created pseudo soul. The issue with this is that the soul would be overall way weaker. Shizu would not be able to call upon the power she held in her prime, all things considered she'd be as strong as a normal Human.

I was still working on creating a truly autonomous soul, a new living being. Though I wasn't dedicating that much time to it since, in the end, creating life the boring way was just a fun side project for me.

With that, I finally left the room I met Gunhee and Adam in. It didn't take me long to arrive back at the training ground where Megumin was chatting with Jin-Woo, Sukuna was speaking with Choi Jong-In, and Lalatina was with Min Byung-Gyu.

No more fighting was going on. From what I heard, the other Hunters approached Lalatina and Sukuna, and they merely responded.

They didn't particularly care for any of the Hunters, but that didn't mean they weren't willing to converse.

I overheard Lalatina's conversation. "Indeed! My Master is worthy of worship, I am glad that you are beginning to see the light!" She said with a proud smile. "It seems his mercy upon you was not wasted."

"Leave the poor man alone, Lalatina." I said as I appeared beside her.

"Master!" She said excitedly.

The entire room seemed to pause their conversations the moment I appeared.

Gunhee was the one who spoke first as he approached. "I assume the conversation with Adam went well?" He asked.

I lightly waved the invitation to the Hunters Conference. It wasn't the actual invitation, that was all digital, as most things were in this age, but the paper one had its uses as well, which was likely why it was given.

Gunhee nodded before looking at the rest of the Hunters present. "I believe this gathering of yours was a success. Feel free to stay as long as you wish, but I must be leaving now. The work of a Chairman never ends."

Gunhee gave me a final nod before leaving.

Jinchul approached me as some of the Hunters were leaving. "I can escort you out now if you have no more business at the Association."

"Feel free."

Megumin came over to me. I noticed Jin-Woo looking thoughtful behind her.

"What did you think?" I asked as Jinchul escorted us out of the Association.

"He has potential. You said he would become that new Shadow Monarch guy?"

Jinchul seemed to miss a step before he quickly began walking properly again.

That was information that was probably meant to be kept hidden, but eh, whatever it was no big deal.

"Yeah, once he does he might actually be able to challenge you."

The three Monarchs I fought could fight at the Ultimate level thanks to their Divinity. I imagine Ashborn's Divinity and his overall power are far higher than most of the other Monarchs.

Who knows how strong Jin-Woo would be with his powers, he was the strongest Shadow Monarch for a reason.

I imagine Jin-Woo would transform into a Spiritual Lifeform once he became the true Shadow Monarch as well.

Both had the same level of power, though Jin-Woo likely kept growing through manual training since the System would no longer be capable of easily powering him up due to its nature. The main difference didn't come from their power level, but the ways in which both Shadow Monarchs used their power.

Jin-Woo seemed to prefer to use his power in focused bursts. Basically, he concentrated it for a higher output but with a smaller scale. But thanks to that, he could create stronger attacks for less energy.

Megumin laughed cockily. "I doubt it."

"Heh, he just might if you get lazy!" Lalatina chimed in with a bratty smile.

I rolled my eyes. She enjoyed messing with Megumin too much, and going by Megumin's pursed lips, she had succeeded.

"I do believe that he is far from matching your might, Lady Megumin." Sukuna said humbly from my side.

I had pretty much gotten completely used to this new Sukuna. It was easier to just think of him as a different person, but with the name and body of Sukuna.

As Jinchul drove us home I placed a barrier around the four of us so Jinchul wouldn't overhear.

"I plan to return to the Cardinal World to pick Milim and Gaia up once we return. Do any of you want to come with me?"

"How long will you be gone for, Master?" Lalatina asked with some worry.

"Shouldn't be long at all; a few hours at most as I want to catch up with some people as well."

"That's fine then! I can survive a few hours without your presence!" Lalatina said proudly.

"I'll be fine. Sukuna can keep me company, won't you?" Megumin said with a grin.

A bloodthirsty smile formed on Sukuna's face. He's lost to Megumin an uncountable number of times, but it was in fights like those that his true nature as Sukuna began to show.

"It would be my honor." Sukuna responded.

Once that was settled I dispersed the barrier, with Jinchul unaware entirely.

It didn't take us much longer to arrive back at the place we were staying. As Jinchul was escorting us inside, he said, "Should you desire anything, feel free to contact me through the phone the Chairman gave you. The Chairman has already informed me that you have agreed to attend the Global Hunters Conference as well, so I will help arrange everything for you."

Lalatina looked at me questioningly hearing that, but I'd tell her later.

"Did you require a proper suit for the occasion?" Jinchul asked.

My casual wear consisted of a collared t-shirt and pants normally. Sometimes I threw a coat on as well, so it was normal to ask that.

"No, I have plenty." The suits Shuna made for me are likely of far higher quality than anything in this world.

Jinchul nodded. "Very well." With that, he left.

"See ya, Milord!" Megumin shouted as she led Sukuna away into another dimension I added onto the place we were staying, one that should be able to handle their fight without affecting the world.

"Tell Arcueid I said hi!" Lalatina said as she followed the two of them, probably to watch them.

With that, I was alone. After a moment, I created a portal in front of me leading to the Cardinal World. More specifically, Milim's territory.

She was probably already getting impatient. It was best to pick her up first so she didn't get the random idea of bugging Arcueid or something as she waited for me.

Once I stepped through, I closed my eyes and took a deep breath of the air. I preferred the air of this world over any other. It was far more rich in energy, and thus more nourishing.

"Felix!" I heard a tiny nuclear missile in the distance yell.

After a moment she was in front of me with Gaia in her hand, and an excited grin on her face. "Are we going yet!?" She asked quickly.

"Nice to see you too, Milim."

She blinked before grinning again. "Yeah! Nice to see you too, bestie!"

Since time between the two worlds was synced up, not too much time had passed, but Milim and I hadn't had a quality "hang out" in a while.

"To answer your question, no. I want to stop by my territory and speak to Arcueid, and Raiden. Then I'll go to Ruberious to see Saeko, Luminous, and Hinata."

Hinata had said she didn't need my help, and I'd respect that, but stopping by to say hello was fine.

Then finally I wanted to visit Tempest.

Milim pouted, but she nodded nonetheless.

"You can stay at my territory if you want?" I offered.

Milim looked thoughtful for a moment before nodding. "Okay! I'll meet Middray since he's there training that dragon of yours!"
"That's fine then."

All of a sudden she blinked in confusion. "Eh? Why are you so weak, bestie?"

It was just like her to call my current level of power weak. This was stronger than most beings would ever get in their lives, stronger than most Saints, and she calls me weak.

"I'm using another vessel that limits my power in the other world so I can have more fun."

Her eyes widened in realization as she summoned the gloves I gave her what felt like a long time ago.

"Ah, so like these then!"

I nodded. "Similar, yes."

The gloves were meant to restrict her own power so she could also have more fun.

"Mou, I wish I could do what you're doing then!"

"Haha, I don't think this kind of ability would suit you."

She pouted but nodded.

I placed a hand on her shoulder and then teleported us to my territory. More specifically, the entrance to the training ground that Raiden and Middray were using.

Since they were created using my Small World and I was so close in range to the dimension, I could sense just what was going on. I let out an appreciative whistle as Raiden just unleashed a continent shaking lightning bolt, but in a condensed form aimed solely at Middray. That way he was the one who would be damaged, but the environment would not.

"They're in that dimension." I said, gesturing Milim forward. I didn't bother to warn her. She was Milim fucking Nava; she could handle what was going on inside without even trying.

Milim just skipped forwards, Gaia still in her arms as she went into the training room in which world ending attacks were likely being thrown around.

I decided to meet Raiden later, but before we leave, since she seemed to be in a spar.

A moment later, I felt space bending around me as my Demoness appeared in front of me.

"My Lord!" Arcueid greeted with widened eyes. "I was not expecting you, but I am happy to see you." She said with a giddy smile.

I smiled back. "Arcueid. I just stopped by to pick Milim up and wanted to check on you."

She blushed lightly. "Ara, to check on me hmm? I am fine, but I appreciate the gesture."

We moved to another room to speak.

It hadn't been that long, so I didn't stay long to catch up. Though I could tell that Arcueid missed me.

She said that the arrival of Dagruel's representative was set to arrive in two days. I asked if she wanted me here, but she refused, saying that she would handle everything.

She really was great. Because of her, I could handle my life pretty much worry free.

She expected everything to go well with his representative. We were offering Dagruel a good deal, and had no previous hostilities with him, so he had no real reason to fuck us over.

The deal itself was also good. We would give resources his people needed desperately in exchange for material that he had so much of. I even offered to set up teleportation circles so he didn't have to lose people on the journey to bring the resources back to his territory.

The only possible variable was his relationship with Luminous. My alliance with her was well known among certain circles, but Luminous said that despite her thoughts on him, he was a good ruler. He'd put his people before his own issues, so chances were he wouldn't do anything.

These were all things that Arcueid also knew of and had accounted for, so I still wasn't worried.

Dagruel was a big variable I wanted to deal with, as according to Chloe, he took advantage of all the chaos in the world to launch his own attack. He was fuck off levels of strong. I was also fuck off levels of strong, but I didn't want to have him as an enemy if there were other alternatives.

I knew none of his movesets or abilities. Him becoming an enemy would be troublesome since I'd be distracted with him while at war with the Eastern Empire.

A war on one front was way easier than one on two fronts.

I could sense that Kurumi wasn't within the bounds of my territory. When I asked, Arcueid said that she had sent Kurumi out as a diplomat of sorts to the Beast Kingdom of Eurazania.

Since Carrion had become my subordinate, Arcueid wanted to regularly check in on his territory to see how his people were doing, what resources they had, and to remind his people of my existence.

Kurumi was serving as more of an inspector, and Kurumi had wanted to visit his territory too, so it all worked out nicely. Arcueid had also been keeping tabs with Suphia who was stationed at the border outpost next to the Eastern Empire.

There were more reports of strange things going on the other side, but no precise reports as we couldn't get anyone into the Eastern Empire.

As for Suphia, she had also been growing stronger according to Arcueid, and that was something I agreed with. I had met Suphia around after all. It wasn't like she was exiled to the border outpost, so she came to my capital via a teleportation circle that I set up somewhat often.

Raiden had apparently been regularly training with Middray. She wasn't doing it all day of course, something I made sure of as that was no way to live, but she had been spending quite a few hours inside the training dimension. With the time dilation, that added up.

She seemed to take my words that she should get better control over her power to heart.

Still, I would make sure to remind Raiden to enjoy her other hobbies too. She seemingly enjoyed training up the Maid Corps as well as flying around the territory I gave her.

Arcueid similarly asked about why I seemed weaker to her perception.

Once I caught up with Arcueid, I left for Ruberious.

"Ara, I was not expecting you, Felix." I heard Luminous say from behind me. I had teleported to her lounge that she liked to laze around in.

Once I turned around to face her I wasn't surprised to see her lazing on her couch with a smile on her face.

"I came to pick up Milim and wanted to visit."
Luminous nodded as she sat up and patted the newly available space beside her.

Once I was sitting next to her, she laid back down, except this time her legs were draped over my thighs. I could only roll my eyes at her laziness, something that she saw.

"Since you are here, then it is only your duty as my consort to serve as my foot rest." She said haughtily.

I smirked. "You just like an excuse to touch me, Luminous." I said in an equally haughty manner. "It's understandable really."

She tilted her head. "I do believe that this imaginary scenario you have concocted up is just that: imaginary."

I didn't answer, just leaned back, casually letting my hand rest on the smooth curve of her shin, something she didn't protest at all.

After a moment of silence, I glanced at her as I pushed some love energy into her at a low ebb. Her leg shifted slightly as the energy entered her, but there was no other visible reaction, which was expected.

A large portion of her skillset was based on love energy. If she is that weak to it, then she wouldn't be such a master of it in the first place.

Love energy at its core was not a type of energy used for pleasure, but it was the energy of life, and so it could be repurposed for that based on one's mastery over it.

With it I could sort of guide the energy into and throughout Luminous, causing certain changes in her Spirit to induce more pleasure in her.

It may have been cheating, but as I like to say; if you aren't cheating, then you aren't trying.

In the first place, to bring any real amount of pleasure in a Spiritual Lifeform requires cheating.

"You know, if you wanted my attention that badly, you could've just said so. Sprawling across me like this… kind of makes it seem like you missed me." I said teasingly.

A lot of our relationship was founded on this odd relationship of ours that consisted of us just messing with each other and enjoying one another's company. I enjoyed it, so did she, so there was no need to change anything even if we had become lovers. Though I also enjoyed the sprinkle of love-dovey stuff we did as well.

She raised a brow. "Is this what Hinata explained as 'coping'?"

"She needs to stop telling you about these things." I said with a laugh, though I didn't mean it. For some reason it was pretty amusing to hear Luminous use modern slang.

Luminous merely smirked in response.

She leaned back again. "It was rather amusing watching you attempt to get a reaction out of me, feel free to continue."

My eyes narrowed, she had challenged my pride!

"I'm not trying at all." I retorted as I let my hand slowly trace idle circles on her skin, slowly imbuing a little more love energy into her. "If I was trying you'd already be moaning out my name." I said smugly.

Luminous's lips twitched. "Ara, do you think this meager amount of energy can affect me?"

She had to have been doing this on purpose. It wasn't my fault that she knew how to rage bait me!

I narrowed my eyes as I actually began to try. This time I began to use Lover to guide the love energy throughout her body, stimulating her Spiritual Body in just the way I knew her to like.

Luminous was a master of love energy, but I knew her.

For a few moments she continued to give me that amused smile as if nothing was wrong, but it didn't take long for her to react.

I watched as the flow of energy spiraled across her core, curling around her before stopping all of a sudden.

Luminous blinked in confusion as she quickly realized what happened. "Tch. I will not be seduced by a man whose idea of romance involves smug comments and casual groping."

"Who said anything about romance? If you want romance I can do way better." I responded, my pride insulted. I did more than just make comments and grope!

Luminous ignored me. "You are getting better with that."

"Of course I am. How else am I to toy with my lewd True Ancestor."

Her lips twitched as her body shivered slightly, but she didn't deny it. She enjoyed a different relationship in the bedroom when compared to other settings, and I was all for it.

We continued to speak a bit more, with Luminous asking some questions about the world I'd be taking her to.

I asked a bit about how her training was going as well since she had told me she had been working on creating her own Domain Expansion since the ability interested her. Though I suppose it would be a World System Skill in this world.

She had achieved some success, though nothing grand enough to be considered a true World System Skill, but she would get there some day if she kept working at it. That wasn't the only thing she was focusing on either. At this rate by the time the Eastern Empire attacked, which I expected to be in a few months, she'd be a whole different powerhouse.

I asked about Saeko again as well. I planned to meet her and Hinata after Luminous since the two of them were apparently together right now.

Saeko had been helping Hinata purge the corrupt officials because Hinata asked Saeko for help. I doubted she needed it, but Saeko's abilities were rather good to send a message.

The ability of Certain Outcome was well known. Just seeing that someone with that ability was on the side of the Paladins would make the Church officials more cooperative.

We chatted a bit more before I left, telling Luminous that we'd save any 'fun' that we would have for when I brought her to the world of Solo Leveling. Just like everyone else, Luminous also asked about my apparent weakness, but was relieved to know that I was weak by choice.

It was rather heartwarming how she started by saying that if I was so weak now she'd take care of me. Of course she said it in a smug and haughty manner, but it was the thought that counted.

It didn't take me long to find Hinata and Saeko, who were leaving some big official building with a few of the Great Saints.

As I flew towards them, I looked around the city of Lune. The people seemed to be mostly back to normal. They were going about their days, doing their jobs and whatnot.

They still seemed to have that unwavering faith in Luminous due to everything being handled with what looked like complete ease.

I appeared in front of Hinata's group in a flash. Arnaud and Saare, the two Great Saints Hinata seemed to bring, have stiffened up before relaxing.

"Felix-sama!" Saeko yelled while running towards me all teary eyed before glomping me. I easily caught her. "I thought you were going to be gone longer!"

I gently patted her on the back as I set her back down. "I'm just visiting."

"Felix." Hinata greeted me. "I was not aware you would be coming."
I shrugged. "I came to pick up Milim and wanted to catch up a bit in person. I've already seen Luminous."

She nodded. "Very well." She turned to Saare and Arnaud who still seemed a bit nervous. "I will leave the next one to you."

"How have you been, Saeko?" I asked as Hinata spoke to her subordinates.

Saeko nodded proudly. "I have improved my cooking!" She said with confidence.

I smiled. "I heard, I'll try some when I get back."

Saeko grinned. "Of course! It will be the best meal of your life!" She said with confidence.

Saeko's cooking was already really good, though that was due to cheating with Cook. If she managed to fix the texture and look, it would be even better.

By now, Hinata had finished her conversation with her subordinates.

She stepped toward me, her usual composed demeanor softening just a touch. "Felix." She greeted with a nod.

"How have things been?" I asked as I walked, the two of them moving to walk with me.

Hinata shrugged. "It's been a bit of work since I can't just kill them all just like that. I need to find proof of their misdeeds, which isn't that hard to begin with, and make sure all their peers realize why they are being purged so they do not follow in their footsteps. It is not hard, merely time consuming."

I shrugged. "That's what you get when you choose to not be a tyrant." It was way easier to be a tyrant. As I always said, I wasn't a good person.

Saeko nodded beside me. "Umu! It would be much easier if Lady Luminous was treated like Felix-sama in his territory. None would oppose any of his actions in Azeroth."

Hinata gave Saeko a look. "It would be easier, yes, but this country would not be what it was if that was the case."

Saeko just shrugged in response.

"How did you two begin working together?" I asked.

"I wanted to use her to send a message as Certain Outcome's effects are rather… memorable."

I snorted. Memorable… right. I've seen Saeko turn normal looking people into things distinctly not Human while still keeping them alive. Certain people have had Certain Outcome in its Extra Skill form so it had a reputation.

"I agreed since she agreed to spar with me." Saeko responded. Saeko was someone who was always chasing after strength, so that wasn't surprising. Even before I ever met her, she was like that.

The three of us continued to chat for a little longer before I left. Saeko seemed to be doing fine, so I was glad.

Now for the last stop before going back to the world of Solo Leveling, Tempest.

Chapter 145: Milim Goes for a Walk

- Felix -

The three of us continued to chat for a little longer before I left. Saeko seemed to be doing fine, so I was glad.

Now for the last stop before going back to the world of Solo Leveling, Tempest.

I had already let Rimuru know that I was stopping by earlier since he didn't give me a chance to on the call. I decided to keep the reason a surprise though.

From what he told me, he and Shizu hadn't known each other long, but she was close to him. She was part of what inspired him to do what he was doing in this world. She was why he was taking such a hard stance against otherworlder summonings.

She was the root cause of a lot of his actions in this world, and all because he thought that people like her deserved more.

When I arrived in Tempest, the atmosphere was its usual blend of lively and as peaceful as always. There were people of all races talking and hanging out with each other, Humans included.

I could see plenty of Adventurers going around as well.

I had used Falsifier to disguise myself as my identity and looks were well known.

I sent a Thought Communication to Rimuru.

"Felix! Are you here?" Rimuru immediately answered.

"I am."

"Great. I'm in The Dungeon on the floor where you made the portals."

"I'll be there soon, then."

With that, I teleported to The Dungeon, or more specifically the hidden warehouse where the portals to the kids' worlds were.

"Felix! There you are." Rimuru said from behind me.

It was just the two of us here right now.

"I just came back from visiting their worlds." He explained.
I nodded in understanding.

"How'd that go."

Rimuru sighed. "It was troublesome, but worth it."

He went on to explain that he had to go to the parents of each kid individually and explain the situation to them, which wasn't easy.

At first all of them thought he was a crazy guy that had kidnapped their children, since at this point their kids had been gone for a long time.

So he had to show them magic, but that brought up a whole lot more issues, and it just spiraled from there.

Eventually Rimuru managed to tell them everything that they needed to know about their kids and what they had gone through. It took a few trips, but he managed. He had only just finished wrapping everything up when I called him from the Solo Leveling world.

Rimuru said that parents were extremely happy and in tears once everything was settled.

Rimuru did a bunch of wide scale magic to make sure that no questions would be asked, like where the kids had gone and whatnot. So for all intents and purposes, the kids could go back to their normal lives if they wanted to.

I was glad everything was sorted out on that end, or at least mostly sorted out.

Rimuru would still have to go back and forth for a few days to make sure that there were no odd reactions to the kids from the people around them. Rimuru sealed off their energy, but he wanted to be safe, which is why he wasn't coming back with me.

The kids were staying back in their home worlds for now, but Rimuru gave them an artifact based on the item I gave him to allow us to communicate between worlds, so the kids could contact him at any time.

All of them expressed interest in going between worlds. They did build up a life here, had friends, and whatnot. They didn't want to abandon everything.

Their parents were less certain, but he said they were just happy to have their kids back and were interested in the world that their kids had lived in. He said he'd give them time to decide since they still were in shock.

He did make them sign a contract, but he basically scammed them into doing so, not explaining anything about how the contracts were literally soul binding. Very Daemon-like.

"At least they got to go back home." Rimuru said with a sigh as he led me deeper into The Dungeon.

"Yeah, you did right by them. I'm sure Shizu would be glad."

Rimuru nodded and gave me an appreciative smile.

As we teleported to another floor I asked, "How are my not-kids doing?"

He gave me a look before responding. "The same old. They seem to just be enjoying life. No real ego has developed in any of them."

I nodded, not thinking much further on it. "What about Veldora and Ramiris? Are they going to be coming?"
Rimuru snorted. "Do you know them? Of course they are."

"Yeah, that's about what I expected."

Once we were on the deepest Floor in Rimuru's personal office area he sat down and looked at me. "Now what did you need? You said it was important?"

"It is." I held my palm out as a glowing orb appeared floating above it.

"Am I supposed to know what that is?" He drawled out.

"These are a bunch of memories."

I did get to see all of Shizu's memories thanks to recreating it. It's honestly astounding how autistic Leon can be, and I'm not even insulting him this time.

It was no wonder that Shizu wanted to see him again, for closure if nothing else.

Rimuru's eyes widened as he realized what I was hinting at. "You were able to do it!?" He asked with excitement.

I nodded. "I was, though we will need a Pseudo Soul to house all of this."

I still couldn't make a real soul, but I could make parts of it and use technology as an intermediary to make an artificial soul of sorts.

The main thing I struggled to create with souls wasn't the ego, or the core, or anything else. It was something a bit more abstract that I couldn't figure out.

If I tried to make a soul as I was now, there would no doubt be something defective about it. But the Pseudo Souls only needed a core with memories to work, which I could easily create.

Then the Pseudo Soul did the rest. This wasn't a real soul either, so the souls it resulted in were also defective, just not as defective.

Unlike what I was expecting, he seemed hesitant all of a sudden.

"Something the matter?"

He sighed. "Shizu said that she didn't want to return to a war-torn world. Isn't it a bit selfish to bring her back just because we can?"

"She also said she wanted to see the world you'd create. I think she'll be pleasantly surprised with how peaceful the Western Nations have become ignoring the most recent attack on Ruberious."
Rimuru clenched his fists. "But the Eastern Empire… I don't want to bring her back just as we're preparing to go to war. It feels… cruel."

Eventually he sighed, pushing the orb of memories away from him. "No, I don't think it's right to bring her back when we are about to go to war."

I shrugged. "It's your choice." I threw the ball of memories at him. "Keep this for now, at least."

He nodded and stored the memories in his Stomach.

I didn't have much of an opinion on Rimuru's choice. In the end, Shizu was his friend. Even if she agreed in the weird mental soul space we were inside, he knew her better than I did.

If he thought it was wrong to bring her back now, then so be it.

"That was really it then."

Rimuru nodded. "Thanks for everything, Felix. I mean it."

I waved him off. "No need for that. We're friends, right?"

He grinned. "Right. Now leave before Ramiris or Veldora get a whiff of you. They'll want to go back to the other world with you, and I don't want them there on their own without my supervision."

I rolled my eyes. "You're treating them like children."

He crossed his arms. "That's because they act like children!"

I smiled. "That's fair. I'll see you then. I'll be coming back in a few days to pick up Luminous and Hinata. Should I come for you as well?"

Rimuru looked thoughtful before shaking his head. "No, I still want some more time to make sure everything is fine with the kids."

I shrugged. "Suit yourself."

We continued to speak for a bit longer, with me telling Rimuru in a bit more detail what I was doing in the world of Solo Leveling.

He also seemed interested in the cosmology of that world, but not to a super high degree.

It had only been a few days since I left, but she was still coming to terms with the status of her mother's killer and the reasons behind the massacre of her village, among other things.

Plus I wanted to make sure she was being treated well by the people of Eurazania.

She was also very cute in this form, I could admit that much.

I nodded back. "Carrion."

"I was led to believe that you would be away for quite some time."

I shrugged. "I just came back to check on things and heard Kurumi was here, so I wanted to see how she was doing."

Carrion nodded. "I understand. Would you allow me to host you in my palace?"

"His palace is rather nice, Master. Nothing compared to yours, but the food is good!" Kurumi commented. Carrion didn't even twitch at the subtle diss either.

"That sounds great. I won't be here for long, though."

Carrion nodded before he began descending down towards his palace. I followed along.

As we touched down, a few of the Beastmen guards bowed low to us. Carrion gave them a nod, and they stepped aside wordlessly.

"I haven't been here since Milim happened, but it seems your people have recovered rather well."

Carrion winces at the memory of what Milim did here, but he nodded right after. "We are an enduring people, so long as our spirit is not broken, we will continue to work forwards." He said with pride.

"I noticed some architecture that's similar to what I've heard of in Frey's Kingdom." I commented.

Carrion nodded. "Frey has become a good friend. She sent some of her own subordinates to assist with some of the reconstruction."

I raised a brow at the feelings I could feel in him through Lover at the mention of Frey. It seems like someone was in love.

Well good for him.

"I just came to see how Kurumi was doing. I'll be leaving now." I said as I stood up. She had already given me her report via a Thought Communication while we ate.

Arcueid sent her here to make sure no rebellious elements were stirring, since Beastmen were rather unpredictable. They worshipped the strong, but I hadn't made my presence here known before. So for all intents and purposes, most only knew I was strong by hearsay and nothing more.

According to Kurumi, Carrion had a tight leash on his people, and he would make sure nothing would challenge me, both due to his respect for my power and his fear of it.

Carrion nodded. "Allow me to escort you out."

Kurumi seemed sad, but she also nodded. "I'll get stronger so I can come with you next time, Master!" Kurumi said with a firm nod.

"It's not your strength that's the reason, but your control. Relying on your tails alone is bound to cause you trouble at some point."

Kurumi pouted but nodded.

Carrion seemed clueless, but he didn't ask anything.

"Well done Raiden. You actually managed to push me there, hohoho." Middray said with a laugh.

Milim nodded. "Umu! You've become strong!"

"Master!" She said in excitement.

I smiled at her. "Raiden, I've heard you improved."
She allowed a small but proud smile to form on her face. "Of course!"

"Hohoho, indeed she has!" Middray said from the side before greeting me. "Thank you for these gauntlets, Lord Felix! They are quite wonderful!"
"Don't get too attached, I have something better in mind for you once I work out the kinks."

"Then I can only thank you." He said with a bow.

"Mou, don't ignore me!" Milim said as she stomped her foot down, shaking the entire palace.

It really was something to see her fully coming into herself, at least when compared to how she was as a Medium Dragon.

Wait… did I technically groom her?

Nah, this is different, and that's what I would wholeheartedly believe.

She continued to report her activities to me, like how Evelyn's training was going well. What training exactly Raiden was speaking of I didn't know since I'm pretty sure Evelyn's combat skills were far from lacking, but I'd leave that to Raiden. I'm sure she knew what she was doing.

"This was excellent, Raiden." Arcueid complimented as she put her fork and knife down.

We were eating a Poison Dragon steak, which of course had been purified, but it retained some of the kick a Poison Dragon was known for.

"Thank you." Raiden said with a bow.

"Mmm, she's right!" Milim said as she stuffed her face. Middray still looked heartbroken at Milim's preference for cooked meat.

"Kyuu!" Gaia said from the seat beside Milim as he stuffed his face as well.

"Thanks for the food, Raiden. It's only been a few days and I missed it already!" I said with a laugh.

Raiden seemed to be happy at my comment.

I stood up and looked at Milim. "Now I think we should be leaving. I don't want to leave Megumin and Sukuna unattended for too long." I said with a shiver.

Arcueid and Raiden nodded.

I also checked in on Ingvild who seemed to be doing just fine. She was preparing for the concert that would be hosted here in my capital city in a couple months, while Damrada was on a job from Arcueid.

"Have a good trip, my Lord." Arcueid said.

"I will make sure everything stays perfect in your absence, Master." Raiden said.

"No need to be so dramatic, Raiden. I'm not going to be gone for a super long time, and we can speak through the rings I gave you all."

Raiden nodded.

"Let me know if you need anything for Dagruel." I told Arcueid who nodded.

With that, I looked at Milim who was holding Gaia once again.

"Ready?"

She nodded, and so I teleported us back to the world of Solo Leveling.

I let out a sigh of relief at seeing the penthouse still standing. I didn't believe that Megumin and Sukuna would get that out of hand, but it was Megumin and Sukuna. Enough said.

"Hmm, this world feels different!" Milim said as she hopped towards the window. Gaia flew out of Milim's arm and began to fly around the place at supersonic speeds.

"Don't break anything!" I yelled after him.

The only response I got was, "Kyuuuuuuuuu!"

I would take that as an affirmative.

"Eh, so this is one of those modern cities you described?" Milim said as she looked out the window.

I nodded as I stood beside her. "It is." It was night time now, so all the city lights were on. The penthouse we were staying at had a good view of Seoul as well.

"It looks kinda like Tempest." Milim commented.

"I think Tempest is well on its way to this level. Also, I don't think I need to remind you, but maintain perfect control of your power. This world can't handle a fraction of what the Cardinal World can."

Milim nodded seriously.

"You're back, Milord!" I heard Megumin yell out from the other side of the penthouse, where the training dimension was situated. Megumin, Sukuna, and Lalatina quickly approached us.

"We are back." I said with a nod.

Just as Megumin was about to respond, Gaia zipped right past her causing Megumin to give him an annoyed look.

"How'd the fight go?"

Megumin smirked. "I won of course."

Sukuna nodded. "Indeed. I learned quite a bit from Lady Megumin."

"Hehe~, you guys were fighting, I want to join too!" Milim said with a grin.

"A fight with you!? Hehe sure!" Megumin said with a worry-free grin, as if she didn't just agree to fight The Destroyer.

"Do it some other time."

Milim pouted but nodded. "I'll take you around tomorrow since it's late here right now. A lot of places aren't open now."

Milim agreed easily, and so we settled in for the night, with Lalatina joining me in bed.

"Mmm, this is super good, Felix!" Milim said as she slurped on a bowl of noodles. There was a good amount of street food in this city, and Milim pretty much wanted to try everything we came across.

Right now I was just taking Milim around the city. I had told her a bit about this world like the Hunters, the Associations, the Gates, the Monarchs, and the Rulers.

She was curious about pretty much everything, so I planned to take her to the Association today which was something she wanted, even if I said that they wouldn't be able to entertain her.

She was more or less just enjoying her time in another world. This was her first time in a completely modern society, after all.

Gaia was flying along with us as well, but I had myself and Gaia under an illusion. Gaia was a bird in other people's perception, whereas I wasn't me.

My face and identity were widespread now, after all.

Lalatina, Megumin, and Sukuna had stayed behind for today, seemingly wanting to let Milim enjoy this world without interruption.

The date between Megumin and I was already mostly planned out and would occur in a couple days, just before I went to pick up Luminous and Hinata.

Milim quickly finished her bowl in record time and pointed to another stand down the street with skewers sizzling over open flames.

"Ooh! That smells even better!" She grinned, her eyes sparkling with delight.

"We just ate." I said, but I was already moving in that direction. There was no point in resisting her when she got like this. Plus, who was I to stop her from being childish? We were Demon Lords; we could do what we wanted.

As I followed behind Milim, I let a fond smile form on my face. It was moments like these that were truly the highlights, not epic world shattering fights, or enjoying myself with drop dead gorgeous women. Nah, it was the good times like these with friends.

The vendor gave us a cheerful greeting as Milim practically bounced in place. I gave him a nod, tossing a few bills onto the counter. Even if I was keeping a low profile, it didn't hurt to be polite.

Plus, I wasn't going to steal from a guy just making a living; I had standards. Gobta, on the other hand, I'd gladly mug. In fact, I already had mugged him in the past with Milim and Veldora.

As Milim munched happily on a beef skewer, I glanced up at the sky. Gaia gave a small chirp from her illusion-covered perch on a nearby lamppost.

All of a sudden Milim froze. Before I could even tell her to wait, she yelled, "I'm going on a walk, Felix!" Then she boomed off, leaving a shockwave in her wake, and cracking the cement ground.

I sighed. She had just felt the formation of a Gate. I'd felt it too, after all. The gathering of mana was pretty distinct in a world that lacked it, and it seems that it attracted her interest. I could only feel pity for the monsters inside the Gate at this point.

The vendor was staring at where Milim was in shock, Milim very carefully made sure that the shockwave she left wouldn't destroy his stand, but it seems he was still coming to terms with the fact that a girl that looked no older than 10 just caused a sonic boom.

I threw a couple more bills onto the table in front of him. "For the trouble." I said as the illusion I placed over my form dissipated. Now the vendor was looking at me in shock, but I paid him no mind.

I flew up, grabbed Gaia and then shot off after Milim.

I wasn't worried about her getting into trouble. She was probably the single most powerful person in this entire universe right now, and despite how she seemed, she wasn't going to cause wanton destruction. She was far more empathetic than she seemed.

It didn't take me long to land right in front of the Gate, where a perimeter was already being created. The Gate was glowing a soft blue color, so it hadn't mutated.

"Sir, this is a restricted a–" The man froze once he saw my face. "Uhm, I'm just going to leave." He said as he slowly stepped back. "Way above my paygrade." I heard him whisper.

Would the wonders of this world ever cease? Humans with common sense? A true miracle that was.

"Sir Felix!" I heard someone call out. I raised a brow at the presence of Jinchul.

"I'm surprised to see you here."

I'm sure I was being monitored to a certain extent, but nothing as direct as having someone following me, so him being here really was just a coincidence.

He quickly nodded. "Yes, my presence is required as this is a high ranking A Rank Gate." He said while looking at Gaia who was still in my arms, oddly.

"This is Gaia." I said introducing him.

He slowly nodded. "Greetings, Gaia."

"Kyuuu!" Gaia chirped back.
"And well, no need to worry about the Gate." I said, waving him off. "A friend of mine went into it. She'll probably handle it."

"Do you mean the pink haired child?" He asked in confusion. "Everyone has been panicking since they saw a child go through the Gate. We were unable to bring her back either."

"Yup, though don't call her a child to her face. She's over 2,000 years old. I won't be able to stop her if she gets angry."

Jinchul seemingly had no response to that.

I turned to look back at the Gate as it released an unusual pulse of mana. I could only laugh when the edges of the blue Gate begin to turn red.

"It's becoming a red Gate!" Someone shouted in panic.

Jinchul looked at me in panic, seemingly worried that if something happened to the "child" I brought with me, I'd get angry.

"As I said, no need to worry. Milim will handle it."

- Milim Nava -

She lightly whistled as she walked deeper into this new world. She had sensed the weird portal thingy being formed, and her curiosity got the best of her.

It wasn't her fault! She was just really curious about this new world. She hadn't gotten the chance to explore another world her father created before, but now she could thanks to her bestie!

Her bestie really was the best bestie to ever bestie!

She could sense that she had been transported into another dimension once she stepped through the portal, but she was still curious about where she was, so she continued going deeper.

Her breath was frosted since the temperatures in this area were very low, but she didn't really care about that. Even the blizzards and ice all around couldn't hinder her sight or her senses. It was nothing compared to Velzard's Frost.

Right now she was walking through a forest. She had seen some beasts, but all of them had the instincts to run away right away once they caught sight of her. They were small fry, so she didn't care enough about them to fight them.

This dimension had a lot more mana in it than Earth did at least. Though that didn't really matter for her anymore, not since her bestie upgraded her Magicule Breeder Reactor, making her completely self sufficient.

According to Felix, mana was an offshoot of sorts of magicules, still based on spiritrons but less pure. You would need more of it to create equal effects to what some could do in the Cardinal World.

Felix used an easy to understand example, if someone in the Cardinal World needed one unit of magicules to create a fire ball, then someone would need 5 units of mana to do the same here.

Hopefully she'd find someone strong in this dimension. Felix had said that there was no one here that would be able to give her a good fight, but she still wanted to see for herself.

Not to mention she would copy Felix and restrict her power. She'd use the gauntlets he gifted to her to restrict her power. Maybe then she'd be able to have a good fight!

As she bounded forward through the snowy clearing, she began to scan the surrounding area through the blizzard. There weren't any strong people around her, but she could sense someone around the level of a Saint further inside.

And for all Milim knew, that person could be hiding their power. She couldn't use Milim Eye over such a vast distance to see through the person right now. Still, her hopes were up!

She had only been in this new world for a few hours, but she was still having a lot of fun! Though she always had fun when she was with Felix. The same went for Rimuru, too!

They were her closest friends and she couldn't be happier that they existed!

Before long, she sensed a group of beings up ahead. With a grin on her face, she boomed forwards, landing in front of them.

She took in their appearance, their blue, snow-like skin and pointed ears. She tilted her head. "Are you guys elves?" She recognized the pointy ears, but their skin was different from what she'd normally associate with elves. But the dark elves existed, so she imagined these were another race of offshoots.

It was a group of three, with two of them holding bows, and another with a halberd.

One of them opened his mouth with a snarl on his face. She blinked as all she could understand was gibberish.

"Ah, you're speaking another language. Gimme a sec." She said, holding a hand up at them, which seemed to anger them for some reason.

Did they want to talk or not!?

She closed her eyes and quickly focused on the Information Particles around them. After a moment of understanding them, she opened her eyes again. "Can you understand me now?"
She learned the language by reading the data for it off the Information Particles. She wasn't as good at reading Infons as some people, but she was good enough to fight Guy in a Time Stop back when he fought her when she went berserk.

"We can." The Elf in the lead slowly nodded as he stepped forward, his halberd still gripped tightly.

"Eh, so what do you want?"

The Elf blinked in confusion. "You are trespassing into the territory of the Baruka Tribe, the new Kingdom of Ice Elves." The Elf gave her a once over. "You seem to be a Dragon under Lord Antares. Due to his relationship with our Lady, you may leave, but do not trespass again." The Elf stated.

"Eh? Who's this Antares guy?"

He sounded kinda familiar.

"And who's your Lady? Is she that sorta strong person I sense further down?"

"You overstep, child." The Elf with the Halberd growled out. "Leave. This is the last warning you shall receive. Our Lady has better things to do than deal with a child's tantrums."

Her lips twitched. She really didn't like being called a child by these guys.

She raised her fists, though she was still perfectly controlling her energy as Felix told her to. "Take me to your leader or I'll beat you up."

"We gave you your chance, child. It seems my Lady will have to personally deliver you to Lord Antares." The Elf with the halberd said as he got into position along with the other two archers.

She sighed. This would be a boring fight. All three of them were weak. The Elf with the halberd was around the Special-A Rank, while the others were A Rank.

"You're all weak, so I'll beat you all up quickly!" She chirped.

The gauntlets that Felix gifted her materialized on her hands. They would hold her power back dramatically, but even then she had no doubt she'd beat these guys up quickly.

She bounced once on her heels, still grinning.

"Get in formation!" The halberd wielding Elf yelled out.

At least he was taking things seriously, even if he thought she was a child.

The two archers flared with mana, drawing back frost-glimmering arrows as the leader lunged forward, sweeping his halberd in a wide arc, aiming to knock her off her feet in one clean blow.

She decided to humor them.

Milim tilted her head as the halberd whooshed past her by less than an inch. "That was a nice swing!" She said, giving him a thumbs up.

Then she moved.

A gust of wind erupted as she appeared behind the leader in a blink, tapping his back lightly with one finger. The force sent him flying forward, tumbling across the snow like a ragdoll before slamming into a tree.

The archers loosed their arrows immediately, but Milim casually slapped both projectiles out of the air, the shockwaves from her palm strikes causing the bows to snap in the archers' hands.

She pouted. "Mou, so weak." She even had the gauntlets activated! In the end, they were only Unique Grade. They couldn't truly hold her power back. She wished she could do what Felix did! Even to her Milim Eye, he seemed super weak which was super surprising. But he said it wasn't something she could replicate and he wouldn't deceive her, so that was that.

The halberd-wielding elf groaned as he got to his feet, blood trailing from the corner of his mouth. "What... what are you? A-Another Monarch?"

"Eh? Monarch? Those weak guys Felix was talking about?" She put her hands on her hips. "I'm way cooler! I'm Demon Lord Milim Nava, The Destroyer!" She said proudly.

Her title was super cool, the coolest on the Council if you asked her! Pfft, what Lord of Darkness?

They stared at her like she'd gone mad, which was weird since she was telling the truth!

Just as she was about to launch herself at them she felt a ripple in the surrounding mana. She watched as a large magic circle formed in the sky above them.

"Ooh, someone interesting!" She chirped out.

A silhouette stepped out of the magic circle as it was a teleportation circle.

The person that emerged had long silver hair tied into a braid, pale blue skin, and piercing silver eyes. She was wearing a cloak of frost which Milim thought looked cool. Maybe she'd have to try making a cloak of stardust some time!

The injured Elves immediately knelt. "Lady Sirka!"

Sirka, as she learned her name was, felt pretty strong. Stronger than most Saints, but not quite at the level of even the weakest member of the Demon Lord Council excluding Ramiris.

Still, maybe Sirka could be fun to play with. Not to mention Sirka looked like a child too! Maybe they could make a club of child-like but overpowered beings!

Sirka slowly descended as her Aura began to spread out around the area, making everything far colder, to the point that even the mana in the air was beginning to freeze. That was nothing to Milim Nava though!

"You, who are you?" Sirka asked with a childish tilt of her head.

"Neh, that doesn't matter! You're that lady they were talking about right?!" She asked with some excitement.

This was why she wanted to come to this other world! She'd get to meet new people, fight new people, make new friends, experience different things; she was excited!

Sirka blinked in confusion as she settled down onto the ground. "Leave." Sirka told the other Elves who quickly bowed and ran for their lives.

"I am the Monarch of Nightmares, Sirka, and you are trespassing."

That was a cool title, sorta like Luminous's Queen of Nightmares. Maybe they'd get along?

Milim clapped her hands. "Monarch of Nightmares, huh? That is a cool title! But I still like mine better." She puffed out her chest. "The Destroyer sounds way more awesome, right?"

Sirka didn't respond immediately. She studied Milim carefully, her silver eyes narrowing ever so slightly.

"You are not a simple Dragon." Sirka states with certainty.

"Nope! I'm a Dragonoid! And also a Demon Lord. And also kinda a god if you squint at it. But mostly just super cute and strong!" Milim declared proudly, hands on her hips and posed proudly.

"You are not one of Antares's?" Sirka asked.

"I don't even know who that guy is!"

Sirka smiled, it was small but noticeable. "Then he cannot take offense to me swatting you, Destroyer."

Milim grinned in excitement. "A fight, yay! Hopefully you'll be more fun than the last three!"

Sirka scoffed. "Even thousands of them would not survive against me." Sirka raised one hand. A moment later a pressure spread throughout the area, causing the snow around them to flatten.

The air itself shimmered as her mana condensed into a dozen spears of ice, though Milim could tell the spears, while basic, were not simple. They seemed to have some Divinity in them.

"You destroyed my scouting unit, and intruded into the territory of a Monarch. You will not survive this." Sirka stated with certainty.

Milim's grin didn't fade. Instead, her eyes lit up with excitement.

"I was really nice earlier, you know, sparing those grunts of yours, but if you're gonna go all out then I guess I can try a little bit."

Sirka got angry at her words. "Do not mock me!" Sirka didn't waste another second.

The spears launched at once, spiraling in erratic patterns. Milim's form blurred as she zipped between them with perfect ease, her feet barely touching the snow. She grabbed one out of mid-air and crushed it in her bare hand, giggling.

"Pointy! But not dangerous enough!"

Sirka appeared behind her in a flash, swinging a blade of pure nightmare. At a quick glance Milim saw that it was just a construct made from weaponized dreams and fears.

At least Sirka actually had a reason for her title as Monarch of Nightmares then. Luminous just picked it because it sounded cool. She never said as much, but Milim knew it to be true.

The weapon practically screeched as it even cut through space as it aimed for her exposed back.

But she quickly twisted, catching the blade with a palm which caused an explosion of sparks around them.

"That was pretty cool!" Milim complimented. "But you'll need more than bad dreams!"

The pressure of their clash sent shockwaves rolling across the snowfields, toppling trees and shattering nearby ice pillars. Sirka leapt back, eyes narrowing.

"You leave me no choice, child." Sirka said.

Milim's eyes narrowed. "How many times do I have to say I'm not a child!" She yelled before booming forward.

She would have to beat Sirka up to teach her some manners, of course.
