She put the gauntlets on, but with Milim Eye I could see that she didn't allow it to connect with her, which was wise.

She didn't have the same fine control over her soul that I did, so connecting herself to the gauntlets by a sliver would be harder for her.

"Ooh, these are pretty nice!" She said as she shadowboxed around. As Milim did so, Sirka arrived, took one look at what Milim was doing, then went back inside.

You know, I could respect that. I feel like Sirka and Frey will be getting along quite well.

"Yup, Middray will love this." Milim said with a nod as she took the gauntlets off and gave them back to me.

"That's good then."

I paused as I felt the ring I had given to everyone to alert me of an incoming Thought Communication.

I answered. "Felix." I heard Luminous's voice in my head come through.

"Luminous. Everything set?"

"Yes, Hinata has done enough that she can leave the rest to her subordinates."

"I'll be there soon then."

"Welp, I'm going to go pick up Hinata and Luminous." I told everyone.

Lalatina pouted as I got up, but Milim seemed excited. "Ooh, I can't wait to show Luminous my favorite ice cream store!" Milim said with a laugh.

"I'm sure she'd enjoy it too." I told Milim. "But I'll be back soon."

"Mmkay, see ya Felix!" Milim said with a wave as I teleported back to the Cardinal World.

I had pulled Saeko's coordinates directly from our soul corridor, so I could appear close to her. She was in Ruberious, so I'd like to check in on her too.

I took a deep breath as I appeared in the Cardinal World. It was always something to get used to, going from the energy poor environment of Earth to the energy rich environment of the Cardinal World. There was no comparison.

I looked around at where I had appeared. It was a kitchen of some kind, with chefs of all kinds walking around, doing their thing. They were all Vampires; decently strong ones too. They were probably Luminous's personal chefs going by our current location.

I was concealing myself so I didn't cause a panic, but it didn't take long for me to spot Saeko, so I revealed myself. Saeko immediately spotted me and grinned. "Felix-sama!" She greeted me with her arms spread as she pulled me into an affectionate hug.

I returned the hug. Saeko really was like a cuddly puppy.

"You seem to be enjoying yourself, Saeko."

She was dressed in a standard chef attire, with the sleeves rolled up, a white hat, buttoned shirt, and an apron.

"I am!" She said cheerfully, pulling back just enough to beam up at me.

"That's good then. It seems you haven't been slacking in your training either. I can hardly feel your Aura leaking anymore."

Saeko nodded proudly. "Umu! Luminous had been teaching me her tricks and helped me a lot!"

Luminous probably had to deal with the same issues Saeko was, and she seemingly had a unique knack for getting Saeko to actually learn what she was trying to teach. Saeko was a far more instinctive learner.

Saeko and I caught up for a few minutes. We didn't have a whole lot to talk about since I saw her last time I was here, which was not long ago at all when I picked up Milim. It was only a week ago.

But even then, it was nice to just sit in silence with Saeko, but I did leave her eventually. Apparently the chef overseeing her was a rather strict one, so she couldn't be gone long. Saeko respected his abilities, so she followed along with his rules.

Apparently, he was some old Vampire who had been serving Luminous for centuries. He was once a Human but Luminous had Louis himself turn the chef into a Vampire due to his cooking ability.

With all the centuries he had, and how the older the Vampire, the stronger they are, he was likely around Calamity Class, maybe Disaster Class.

Vampire hierarchy was rather interesting at first glance. I planned to ask Luminous a bit more about it at some point.

After Saeko, I ended up deciding to visit Raiden and Arcueid, even if shortly. Sure, it had only been a week since I last saw them, but what kind of lover would I be if I didn't stop by to see them when I was in the "area"?

Both were pleasantly surprised. Arcueid most of all since she said she was fine on her own, but I could tell she appreciated it nonetheless.

Though apparently Raiden and Evelyn had just finished up their "private" training session, and Evelyn was looking at me awfully weirdly. Through Lover I could read her emotions pretty well; she was aroused, embarrassed, excited, prideful, and a host of other emotions.

In the end I just decided to leave it at that. Evelyn/Elmesia had already proven to be a very emotionally complex individual. Though I still planned to continue to mess with her. Her reactions were hilarious, and since she hadn't attempted to stop me (I made it clear that she could), I could only assume that she enjoyed our little games as well.

Kurumi was also excited to see me despite seeing her only a short while ago. She showed me some of the new art work she had created, a few of them being of my own visage, which was sweet.

All of them had been making progress in their own ways, completely independent of me, which made me glad.

I had also spoken to Rimuru through a Thought Communication to see where he stood. He was still a bit busy, but he said he'd be done soon.

He already had some ideas for what he wanted to accomplish in the world of Solo Leveling aside from relaxing. He basically wanted to acquire a bunch of blueprints for random everyday things. He could make them himself or get them made, but that would require resources, so he wanted to trade basic things from the Cardinal World for them. That way both parties would benefit.

Though he also said he'd like to help them in general as well. Their Earth was massively fucked up, and had a thin veneer of not being a doomsday situation, and he was a bit of an empathetic individual.

But he understood that handing them everything would only doom them in the long run, so he planned to give ideas, and some minor resources and whatnot. But he seemed reassured when I said I'd protect them if things really went bad, though I didn't tell him that I was technically the cause of Phantoms being in that universe. He didn't even know that they were there, if he even knew what Phantoms were in the first place.

Now I was going to pick up Hinata.

In the blink of an eye I teleported close to where Hinata was.

Right now I was floating above the home she seemed to have in Lune. In the blink of an eye, I descended and knocked on the door to her home.

After a few moments the door was opened. "Ye–, Felix!?"

I had concealed my presence to surprise Hinata. "Sup." I greeted her as I walked past her and into her house.

"You didn't have this place last time I was here."

Hinata sighed from behind me before closing the door. "Indeed. Luminous gave it to me after the attack fiasco." She said as she followed behind me.

It was a pretty nice place all things considered. "Ooh, I didn't know you read manga." I said, referring to the manga shelf on the wall.

Hinata looked to the side in embarrassment. "Luminous may have mentioned that the world you originate from is one that was a manga in your first life, so she procured the manga of it for me from Tempest."

I blinked next to her and wrapped my arm around her shoulder. "Aww, you wanted to know more about little old me? I'm touched." I said as I released her, approaching the shelf again.

I looked through the shelf, there was a bunch of good stuff. One Piece, Naruto, Dragon Ball, Jujutsu Kaisen, and many others.

"I was surprised to learn how many of your, Rimuru's, and Veldora's moves were inspired by these manga." Hinata shared.

"Mhmm." I nodded. "In a world like this one, where magic is heavily based on imagination, there isn't a lot that is explicitly not possible."

"Indeed. That is something I discovered as well recently." Hinata responded.

I put the manga I was flipping through back on the shelf. "Let's go get Luminous then. She told me you all were ready."

Hinata nodded. "I believe that I completed my part a few short hours ago. I'm surprised she told you almost right away. Perhaps she is looking forward to this trip with you more than she outwardly expresses."

"Not just with me, I imagine. She cares for you dearly too." I said as I ruffled Hinata's hair.

Hinata brushed my hand away as she quickly fixed her hair, all while shooting me a look of annoyance. "I'm older than you, you know."
"Still weaker than me." I said in a sing-song tone of voice as I walked out of the house.

Hinata just sighed and followed along. "Why are we walking?"

"No reason. I just wanted to make a dramatic exit." I shrugged.

Hinata sighed once again as I transported the two of us to where Luminous was.

We appeared in Night Garden; more specifically the living room where we could see Luminous laying on her couch lazily with Gunther serving her tea.

"Hmph, picking me up last, my dear Consort?" Luminous asked with a tilt of her head.

I rolled my eyes. "Don't ask as if you didn't mind the extra time to laze around."

Luminous just smirked in response.

I gestured for her to get up. "Come on, let's go you NEET."

Hinata was just looking at us weirdly. "This looks like one of those American sitcoms waiting to happen." Hinata mused out loud, but the two of us just ignored her.

With a sigh far too dramatic for the situation, she rose from the couch, letting Gunther take her empty cup in the process. "Very well then. Lead the way."

I just shook my head and sighed at Luminous' antics. "Is there anything you want to get before we leave?"

Both shook their heads.

"Hmm, let's go then."

For dramatic effect I snapped my fingers, creating a portal in front of us. The moment I did so instead of going through the portal I could feel Luminous and Hinata attempt to analyze it, and I didn't stop them.

If they managed to actually understand how it worked, then good for them, but it required an immense mastery of Space-Time, something both currently lacked as far as I knew.

But maybe it would help them begin to understand.

After a few moments, Hinata sighed. "Even with Fortuna I cannot make heads or tails of this."

Luminous nodded. "Indeed. It is an incredibly complex manifestation of Space-Time Manipulation."

Both were looking at me with various looks of pride and appreciation.

"I can't take full credit. It would have taken me longer to really understand and begin to use it without Othinus."

At Othinus's name, Hinata pursed her lips, while Luminous just seemed moderately interested.

'What did you do to Hinata for her to react like that?'

"I merely forced her to confront her feelings."

'Ah, so you're why she's actually being proactive with me. I thank you for your assistance Mistress!'

Though it was about time that I went on the offense with her too. She's had more than enough time to consider if she really wanted something with me, and she was straightforward enough to inform me of if she had changed her mind.

Until then, I'd continue to act like we were in the courting phase to see how it goes. Perhaps I'd take her out somewhere in the world of Solo Leveling. It was an Earth, so it would probably feel closer to home for her.

"Fufufu, of course, Master. Anything for your happiness."

I just smiled at Othinus's ceaseless devotion, I knew that thanking her would only insult her so I was content to show my appreciation in other ways. She was a living being too after all. Her life shouldn't solely be about doing what I wanted; that was no way to live, and not something I'd want for her.

Going on a date with me to enjoy life was just one step in that direction, and I'd be happy if she enjoyed the date at all.

But I could think on that another time, when Luminous and Hinata weren't with me.

"Let's go then." I said, gesturing them forwards.

Both of them looked at each other before walking forward through the portal.

Chapter 154: Glassord, the True Giant

- Arcueid -

She sat pleasantly with one leg crossed across the other as she waited for the arrival of the representative of the Continent's Wrath, Dagruel.

She could already sense him in her Lord's territory, but it would be improper to teleport him here without his consent, if she even could do such a thing. And so she waited. It would give her time to think and modify her plans for Glassord's presence. She hadn't believed he would be the one to come, after all.

It was easy to learn just who it was that Dagruel sent once he arrived in her Lord's territory.

Glassord, one-third of the Mad Titan Ashura and one of Dagruel's siblings: a True Giant who was a monster in his own right. That was who Dagruel had sent.

She was surprised Dagruel would send his very own brother, but after further thought, it made sense. Who better to determine if her Lord was being genuine than one of the True Giants?

He was in the capital city now, so it would not be long. Especially since he was being escorted by Raiden's Maid Corps.

The Maid Corps had quickly grown into the elite defenders of her Lord's palace. They were acceptable enough that she would allow them to serve in her palace back in the Daemon Realm as well.

Raiden had trained them well, and seemed to be offering special lessons to Evelyn fairly often. That was an interesting maid as well, and the lessons were only getting more frequent as well.

She was easily able to notice the discrepancies with Evelyn; how her soul seemed to be less, how the vessel seemed to be less, and the connection that she could sense around Evelyn's soul. And if she could, so could her Lord, so she just ignored the oddities, content with the fact that her Lord approved of her, and so she was of no threat. He clearly had some purpose in mind for her, and he would inform her if he deemed the topic important enough.

She quickly glanced through the variety of contracts she had prepared for today. She had multiple of them outlined based on the predicted priorities of the Holy Void of Damargania.

None of them were exploitative of course. This was all to make a good impression on the Holy Void of Damargania, and by extension, Dagruel. In fact, they had little to gain. They only desired the mere ores that were naturally occurring in the Holy Void of Damargania but impossible to find elsewhere.

Normally they would be valuable, with them creating Unique Grade equipment would be child's play, and despite the armory of her Lord, Unique Grade weapons were considered genuine treasures by most inhabitants of the world. With some effort, the ore from Dagruel's territory could even craft Legendary Grade equipment, which were national treasures.

And that was from an unrefined artisan. A true master could potentially create even higher quality equipment.

Even Dwargon's own king merely had a Legend Grade weapon, and he was a descendent of the Dwarven True Ancestor.

But with her Lord's power over Creation, they were of no relevance. He could create countless Legend Grade weapons with a thought, and had in fact done so already.

But if her Lord's words about the alternate timelines he had mentioned, then she understood his reasoning for going out of the way to assist Dagruel, as the man would become a significant foe if he were to become an enemy, she knew that far better than most.

She had silently observed his fight with Guy, after all, and the man was an absolute monster in combat. Dangerous even to her for a multitude of reasons.

The fight had been incredibly close, and most of Guy's abilities were made null due to Dagruel's unique ability to negate many forms of power, a power that he and his siblings shared. And a power that his children inherited to a far lesser degree.

She was not certain what the true origin of his power was. Back then, her analytical capability was too weak to work on Dagruel, not to mention her analysis almost seemed to be negated as well. He was a true oddity.

His entire race and racial offshoots inherited his power to a certain extent as well. She did not know an incredible amount about Dagruel's people unfortunately, but Lalatina did as in the past that land used to be considered her "playground" within the Cardinal World.

The Eastern Empire was considered to be her own playground, and the land of El Dorado Megumin's.

She already had Lalatina tell her everything that she knew about the Giants, and Arcueid would not discredit Lalatina by saying she lacked information. In fact, Lalatina knew quite a lot. More than Dagruel's children, at least, as they had been kept out of most important things. Due to their immaturity, she guessed, but they would be useful pieces nonetheless.

She knew not why Dagruel entrusted his children to them, but she would be a fool to not make use of them in this negotiation.

She would have thought that perhaps Dagruel wished to be rid of them, that they had fallen out of his favor, and that he scorned them, but from their own words that did not seem to be the case. They were seemingly raised with care and love, which made Dagruel's actions all the more confusing.

And while she would not trust the children blindly, she was willing to believe them for the time being.

They already knew their orders, and their loyalty was assured, so she had no doubt that they would play their parts, making Glassord even more susceptible to her terms. The main thing she was going after with this alliance was to eventually expand to a mutual defensive pact, similar to what Azeroth and Tempest held with the Armed Nation of Dwargon.

When one kingdom was attacked, the others would come to defend. They did not officially hold such an agreement with Ruberious, but due to the close relationships developed, in practice they did.

She quickly went over the information she had gathered.

Lalatina knew quite a bit that she herself did not. From what Lalatina said, Giants were a truly intriguing race. A race created by Twilight Valentine and modeled after the True Giants, Dagruel and Glassord, with the third of the brothers having been sealed away.

The younger Giants were mostly reincarnations of the older Giants who passed away due to age as the lifespan of a Giant was a mere 500 years. Then these younger Giants essentially inherited the power and rage of their predecessors, carrying on their ancient power into the modern day.

These Giants inherit even their predecessor formidable Magic Resistance. Nothing like the nigh immunity she observed Dagruel having, but it was impressive.

She tested Dagruel's children in the past to see how much of his resistance they had inherited, but she was disappointed. While their resistance was far above the norm, it was not difficult to get around with enough raw power.

Greater Giants were even more powerful. They had surpassed their life span of 500 years through some methods, likely training and developing their life force. She had not had a chance to examine those Giants, but she believed that they must have an even greater Magic Resistance.

"He has entered the palace, my Lady." Moss said from her side.

"Hmm, thank you."

Of her Lord's subordinates, many of them were not present at the moment. Raiden and Kurumi were the only ones she could rely on, and to a certain extent Ingvild as well. Sukuna also recently arrived, giving her a far greater force than she initially believed she would have while her Lord was out, not that she believed such a force would be necessary.

Sukuna was indisposed it seemed as well. When he arrived he seemed to be deep in thought, and informed her that her Lord sent him back as there was some conflict within him.

With her power over lifeforce and the soul she was easily able to see what was occurring within him. The conflict of the two selves within him. She would have told him to eliminate the other ego entirely, but Sukuna seemed to believe that by combining, he could become the greater whole, and be of more use to her Lord.

He knew himself best, so she only gave him some advice and left him to his devices.

It didn't take long for her to hear a knock on the door. "Come in."

The door opened and the first one to enter was one of her newest subordinates: Damrada.

Damrada had not been in her Lord's territory as much as the rest of them. He had been managing the Western Nations and Free Guild in her stead, whilst at the same time providing information on all Cerberus personale and bases so they could be ransacked for her Lord's use.

Damrada gave her a nod, one she returned. He was still adjusting to being her Lord's subordinate, but she did not doubt his loyalty, her Lord assured her of it and he had explained the measures he had taken just to be certain.

Damrada was followed in by Glassord himself. At first sight of him, she could feel his barely concealed presence.

The man was incredibly powerful, and despite only radiating the power of a weak Saint, she knew there must be more hidden inside of him. A fragment of Ashura as strong as only a Saint? That was simply not possible. The more likely scenario is that his power was sealed off for whatever reason.

He seemed incredibly holy as well. As her Lord had shared, Ashura was created to be a defense mechanism of the Cardinal World itself, and so Ashura was holy by nature. He was aligned with the world and all it represented.

This holiness was spread even to the three fragments that made up Ashura as well, giving Glassord a level of holiness that none she had met could match. Dagruel was even more holy as well.

Holy was an attribute essentially all beings gained upon awakening, as taking a step further up in the hierarchy. Saints especially became incredibly holy following their evolution from an Enlightened.

Even True Demon Lords acquired a holy element, though this was not true for Daemons such as herself. Holy was simply too opposite to their nature to assimilate it into themselves to become a Chaos Spirit fully.

Upon awakening, they did acquire their own reserves of holy energy, but it was so miniscule when compared to their more demonic aligned energies that it is simply overtaken completely, being far less effective.

Instead they acquired Holy-Demonic Resistance.

Of course, despite not being holy, that didn't stop her, or any suitably strong Daemon, from still using the attribute. It just required multiple steps and a certain degree of carefulness.

She suspected that since Dagruel shared an even greater level of holiness, as one of the stronger True Giants, it was impossible for him to develop a Demon Lord Seed entirely, similar to what Ramiris' situation was.

And yet they were still so blindingly strong that they were at the same level as she was at least.

She could also sense the odd form of Magic Resistance he seemed to have, similar to Dagruel. It was likely an innate trait of the True Giants, but its exact mechanisms she could not understand, which was unfortunate.

She had hoped to understand the resistance to a greater extent for her Lord. If things did not go the way he wished despite his efforts, then information on Dagruel's abilities would become far more valuable.

"You must be the Primordial of White, Blanc." Glassord said as he laid eyes on her. His gaze was analytical, nothing more.

She stood up to greet him. "Indeed, but I prefer to go by the name my Lord bestowed upon me, Arcueid." She responded with a pleasant smile as she brushed some of her hair behind her ear.

"Very well then, it is a pleasure to meet you, Lady Arcueid." Glassord said with a humble nod.

"Ara, there is no need for such formality, you may call me Arcueid."

Glassord nodded. "Arcueid it is then. Is Lord Felix not present?" He asked.

She shook her head. "He is busy with another task at the moment, but I assure you that I am more than suitable enough to act as his representative."

Glassord nodded. "I will not doubt you then."

She gestured for him to take a seat, as she took hers. First she looked to Damrada. "You may leave." He nodded and left them alone.

"After some initial discussion, we may enjoy the feast I have prepared for you. Dagrua, Liura, and Debura will be present, I am certain they would enjoy seeing their uncle."

They were already ordered to sell an alliance with her Lord to them, mentioning their excellent treatment, and all the benefits they had been enjoying, as well as all the power Azeroth had at its disposal.

At her words, a small smile formed on Glassord's face. "I hope they have not caused you much trouble. I would have liked to give my thanks to Lord Felix in person for taking them in."

"They have been no trouble at all and have made excellent contributions in my Lord's name. They seem to have become rather taken with one of the Eight Demonic Lords as well."

The Eight Demonic Lords were far from the household name that the Demon Lords were, but it was known that they were her Lord's direct subordinates. That much information was known about all the Demon Lords, likely by Guy's own doing. Even the Beastkeeters were rather famous, despite Carrion no longer being a Demon Lord.

"They wrote of her. Saeko, is it not?" Glassord asked as some snacks were served.

She hummed in agreement. Once everything was served, she passed Glassord one of the contracts. "Let us begin our negotiation then."

Glassord gave her a firm nod before he began to read through the contract. This was where she truly began to shine.

- Felix -

The moment we appeared, Milim bounded forward and hopped around us in excitement. "Hi Luminous! Oh and you too, the Hero I beat up in the past!" Milim said with a laugh.

Hinata's lips twitched, but she didn't say anything. I didn't even know if it was Hinata that Milim beat, or Chloe.

Hinata ignored Milim and just walked to the window and looked out at the city.

"Greetings, Milim." Luminous greeted Milim as she looked around the living room with curiosity.

"This world truly feels odd." Luminous commented.

Milim nodded. "Mhmm! It took me a sec to get used to it!"
"It took you merely a moment?" Luminous said with a sigh. "This world feels far lighter, the energy in the air has far less weight to it. It will take me time to get used to this."

While Luminous and Milim were talking, I approached Hinata. Once I was beside her she spoke up. "We're in Korea right?"

"South Korea to be exact."

"It feels quite odd to be looking at this modern city when I hadn't expected to ever return to an Earth." Hinata stated.

"Hmm, have you thought about my offer to take you to your home Earth?"

Hinata nodded. "I have. It does scare me, confronting my mother, apologizing for what I did, even if it was for us. But I will never grow if I continue to run from my fears." Hinata looked to the side, at me. "You taught me that."

"Aww, you're gonna make me blush, but I'm proud of you. I won't pretend to know how you feel about everything that happened in your past, but the fact that you're confronting it rather than running away proves that you've grown, Hinata."

Hinata gave me a small smile that said so much. "Thank you, Felix. It means a lot."

"No problem. Stand proud, you are strong."

Hinata closed her eyes and sighed. "And you ruined it."

"Are you two done speaking?" Luminous called out. She was now sitting on the couch, Milim sitting across from her with Sirka who had shown up while I was speaking with Hinata.

Megumin and Lalatina were still doing their own thing, but I imagine they'd show up shortly.

I looked to Hinata, leaving her to decide. She nodded. "Hmm, we are, Luminous." Hinata said as she moved to take a seat next to Luminous. I took the single love seat.

"Milim was introducing me to her new friend." Luminous told Hinata. "Someone native to this universe, and Milim's newest subordinate as well. The next Walpurgis will be quite interesting if she comes along."

Hinata nodded along.

"Yup! Sirka is my newest minion and friend! She's strong too! She'll definitely beat up your minions! Muhahaha!" Milim laughed.

"I would not doubt that; she is incredibly powerful." Luminous nodded, all the while Sirka preened under everyone's praise.

Despite her age, Sirka was a child at heart.

"Well now that you're both here, let me tell you a bit more about everything."

Luminous and Hinata already knew the general bits of this world, but I went on to tell them the specifics as well. Where to go to see some interesting things, the interesting Humans that Luminous could look into recruiting, since I know that's something she wanted to do.

I told them about how the Gates work in detail since Luminous asked about them. The Chaos World and how it was just a massive dimension created by overlapping dimensions.

I told them more about the Monarchs and Rulers, and how Sirka was one of them, which made them look at Sirka in an even more impressive light, which of course made Sirka preen even more.

Then I told them about the new things I learned. "The Phantoms are here?" Luminous asked with some surprise.

I nodded. "They are. Have you dealt with them in the past?"

Luminous shook her head. "Not personally, but Twilight had interacted with them, and researched them as well. His notes were quite thorough."

"Eh, those corrupted Angels you mean?" Milim asked.

I nodded.

"Eh, you don't need to worry about them, they're all weak!" Milim said with a laugh.

"That may be so, but they're still worth accounting for." I told Milim.

"Phantoms. So the beings Antares is allying with originate from your world?" Sirka asked.

"Not exactly, they originate from another universe, but they were once part of our world as well, at least the first of them were." Luminous shared.

Sirka nodded, a thoughtful look on her face.

"Now I wish I still possessed his notes in that case." She sighed.

"What happened to his notes?" Hinata asked.

"Hmm, Pippin, Ashley, and Prelix took off with them once they split off from me due to our disagreements. I did not care about anything to do with Twilight, so I didn't pursue them." Luminous shared.

"They're the ones who established that Magic Tower you were telling me about, right?"

Luminous nodded. "Indeed."

"Hmm, I want to go there sometime. Maybe we can make a field trip out of it." I said with a laugh.

Luminous nodded. "It would be an excellent learning experience for the children Rimuru has taken under his care, and that you seem quite attached to. You would also enjoy it there. They have made a Kingdom based on magical advancement."

I wasn't sure that was a good place for kids, but we'd have to see.

Luminous then looked to Hinata. "Perhaps you can go with them. You have been training to create a new Art. Perhaps you will gain some inspiration there."

"Hmm, we'll have to plan it out then, but what were the disagreements you had with them really about?"

"It was their view on Humanity." Luminous began. "They believed that Humans needed to be actively dominated and oppressed, Prelix was the greatest proponent of this idea."

Prelix was another Vampire True Ancestor, though Luminous said he was more of a failure to Twilight. He was the True Ancestor of a specific branch of Vampires, the Night Stalkers.

- Felix -

She asked Felix about it and was able to learn the entire story, so she was curious why this person was so much stronger than the average Hunter. She was mostly here to satisfy her boredom.

She couldn't use her Milim Eye over such a long range, so she'd have to be in front of the moderately strong person she sensed to see what's up with him.

From the Gate, multiple kinds of monsters came out. Some she hadn't seen before, others that seemed to be variants of what could be found on the Cardinal World.

Sirka landed behind her gracefully. "Have you discovered anything interesting?" She asked as she looked around curiously. "You wished to come here due to the Gate, yes?"

She nodded. "Pretty much, but I think there might be someone fun nearby!"

"Damn it! Is that one that snuck out of the Gate!?" Some Human asked as he dodged past the strike of a large flying bird.

Sirka did look a bit out of place. She had pale blue skin, white hair, and pointy ears. Plus she was still radiating a very miniscule amount of Aura. Whereas she looked perfectly normal, if still way more awesome than everyone else.

What could she say? Her Demon Lord look was "peak" as the Humans in this world said online. That was something else she discovered too. The internet was home to some funny things, though for some reason Felix turned on something called "parental protection" before giving her her phone.

Milim nodded. "Mmm, I'm gonna go see what that guy is up to. If someone attacks, just don't kill them."

"Very well, and which guy?" Sirka asked before she paused. "I see. It seems there is a vessel present then. I could not sense him until now. Perhaps some protection the Rulers built to protect their vessels against the senses of a Monarch?" She mused. "It does not matter, I suppose."

Felix had also told her about the Ruler vessels already. "Oh, so that's why he's stronger than the rest. Let's go see him then!"

Before she could go after him, one of the winged beasts, some type of Wyvern, dove down towards her with its talons glowing with some form of energy.

Sirka appeared in front of the Wyvern's path, and casually backhanded the monster mid-dive. It exploded into a rain of gore and feathers, the shockwave blowing out nearby windows.

"Thanks!"

Sirka nodded.

That action caught the gaze of the rest of Hunters that were distracted with other monsters.

"Humans!" Milim called, waving enthusiastically. "Don't worry, I'm a Demon Lord and am here to help!" She said as she released some of her Aura, intimidating the monsters that were still around, though she made sure to avoid all the Humans with her Aura, while also keeping the monsters alive so Sirka could have fun too.

She was a generous boss!

"Is that a child?" Someone asked. "What about that monster next to her? She looks humanoid. And again, why is the child revealing so much skin?"

She wasn't a child!

She didn't get a chance to wipe out all the monsters in the area for the Humans because she sensed the Ruler vessel's aura boom towards her.

More monsters surged out of the Gate, it was practically a flood.

"Can you take care of them?" She asked Sirka as she withdrew her Aura from the surroundings.

"As you wish." Sirka said. She raised her hand towards the Gate, her eyes glowing with a pale blue sheen.

Milim thought it was funny how the people of this world had that visual effect when using their energy.

But it looked cool! Maybe she'd start making her eyes glow pink too!

She could feel the air instantly drop in temperature, with the air fogging, and the ground they were on cracking as frost raced across it. A wave of cold spread out from her palm, sweeping toward the monsters.

Eh? Was Sirka trying to show off? She could have totally killed all the monsters with a simple wave, but instead she was making a show of it.

Was this what the internet called "aura farming"? Was it super popular in this world or what? She'd heard everyone was doing that in this world, even Felix!

The flood of beasts emerging from the Gate screeched in confusion as their limbs locked mid-charge, encased in crystal-clear ice. The first row froze solid within seconds, then the second, then the third, until the entire swarm was frozen. Even the ones halfway out of the Gate were stuck just past the threshold. It actually looked pretty cool!

"What the fuck!?" Some Hunter yelled, but Milim wasn't paying attention to them anymore. Her gaze shifted down one of the streets where she could sense the vessel coming from.

His Aura actually reminded her a bit of Carrion.

After a moment she spotted the guy, who also saw her. Even his looks reminded her of Carrion.

He was a large, muscular man with long blonde hair and a toothy smile. She liked his outfit too!

His Aura roared around him as he grinned. "I thought I sensed some weird Dragon. What are you doing here, brat?" He asked with a cocky grin as he glanced at the army of frozen monsters above them. "I had to stop enjoying myself with those Mantises on the other side of the Gate because of you." He said dangerously.

Her eyes narrowed. She wasn't a kid! "Hmph! I'm 2,000 years old!"

"Heh, sure you are. What's your name?" He asked as he stepped forwards. The Hunters around them all seemed to be tense.

Sirka stepped in front of her, but Milim waved her away. Thomas only gave a passing glance at Sirka, probably because Sirka had learned to conceal most of her power.

She placed her hands on her hips. "I'm Demon Lord Milim Nava, The Destroyer and a Dragonoid! Bow down to my greatness! Introduce yourself too!"

His eyes narrowed before he clicked his tongue. "Tsk, another monster. You seem pretty strong too. And of course it's another one of your kind." He said with a sigh. "Clearly intelligent as well, are you another one of those shitstain Monarchs, or you with that Felix guy? He introduced himself as a Demon Lord too."

He shook his head. "Doesn't matter, I'll beat your ass anyway. At least I'll get to let loose a bit, those other monsters were lightwork." He grinned as he took his sunglasses off, revealing his glowing yellow eyes. "I'll take out your friend after." He looked at the still tense Hunters. "You all stay out of this, you're too weak, even for her friend. If you get in the way, I won't be saving you."

"Eh? Are we fighting!?" She asked with a laugh. She didn't take offense to his words. Why would she care for the opinion of an ant? She was above throwing tantrums for small things, though she would still beat him up to teach him a lesson. She turned to Sirka. "Stop anyone from interfering. I need to beat this guy up!"

"Hahahaha, it's been a long time since someone's treated me like a nobody! I shouldn't be too upset that I missed out on Japan then." The man said as he cracked his knuckles.

"What's your name? I can't just keep referring to you as "that guy" in my head." She asked, ignoring the bloodlust the man was releasing.

"The name's Thomas Andre." He said with a sharp toothed smile as he began to release more of his Aura. "And I'm the strongest damn Hunter on this planet." He said with a wild grin.

"Ooh, strongest Hunter eh? Hopefully you don't bore me too much then!" She said with a giggle.

She knew this was all probably a misunderstanding. He thought she was with those Monarch guys, which was a fair assumption to make since she hadn't explained anything, but so what? She was Milim Nava, and she thought this would be fun. She'd solve the misunderstanding later, so it would be fine.

Felix might scold her but that was it. Though he did say she could be with Felix, so maybe he didn't even care that she wasn't associated with those Monarch guys. He probably just wanted a fight or something, in which case she was happy to oblige.

Plus maybe she could make a new friend! If he was anything like Carrion, she knew she'd like him. She liked Carrion too, after all! He came to her territory often to "hang out" with Frey.

He always made sure to bring her sweets like a good boy to keep her happy!

"Ha! What a brat!" Thomas yelled as he coated his arms in his Aura. He raised a brow at seeing her making no preparations before shrugging.

As if she needed her Aura to deal with him.

"Oh shit, he's seriously going all out!" Some Hunter yelled from the side. "We need to get back!"

She ignored them all though as Thomas dashed forwards.

Thomas' charge split the cracked pavement like an earthquake, his Aura bursting in a violent wave of sorts that sent the Hunters that were in the process of running away flying back.

Milim only tilted her head, eyes sparkling with excitement as she planted her feet and grinned.

The air itself shattered around his strike as his fist came down at her. The shockwave shattering the already atomized glass further somehow.

Her small hand rose lazily and caught his punch, the ground beneath her exploding into a crater.

"You're decently strong!" She said with a beaming smile. "But you'll need more than that to impress me!"

Thomas' eyes widened but then his grin only widened. He twisted, bringing his other fist in a hook aimed at her jaw. She didn't see a reason to dodge this time, so she allowed his fist to connect, only for it to just flutter her hair.

She was a master in showing off!

"Eh?" One of the Hunters who had managed to stay close enough croaked.

"Not bad, not bad!" Milim said cheerfully, her eyes now glowing pink so she could look cool too. She then casually shoved him back with a single push. The force of it sent Thomas skidding across the street, his boots tearing grooves into the street before he steadied himself with a laugh.

"Now we're talking." He said, shoulders rolling as more power surged off him. With a wild look on his face he said, "Finally, someone worth throwing hands with!"

He really was quite similar to Carrion.

Milim bounced on her heels, clapping her hands together once in excitement. "Hehe, don't hold back! If you bore me after all your talk, I'll get mad!"

Thomas barked out a laugh, Aura spiraling upward as the sky above them darkened. "Good! Try not to break too easily, brat!"

She raised her fists as the Unique Grade gauntlets Felix had gifted her quite a while ago formed. The gauntlets would restrict her power in a way that she didn't feel as if she was holding back as much, making it feel more natural.

The ground between them split as they launched forward at the same time, their two shockwaves colliding mid-street.
